# Dev log

Why things changed, and what state they were left in. Newest first.
Commits carry the detail of *what*; this carries the *why*.

## 2026-11-11 (Roku: #272's review follow-ups, #237)

**Why.** Chad's merge note on #272 (tydude001) asked for four small things and one TV check.

**Changed.** `NxSrtParse`: a file with no blank line between two cues kept the next cue's counter as the last line of
the one before ("A" then "2"); an all-digit line just before a timing line is now taken as the counter and dropped,
and one before a blank line stays the cue's. `check-guards.sh` also refuses `for each box in`. The `applySubtitles`
header, the comments on `NxMbMediaInfo`, `NxMbFullSubs`, `NxMbSubtitleSidecars` and `NxPanelProgramRows`, and
`JELLYFIN-EMBY.md` no longer say Jellyfin and Emby hand the player the forced track as a sidecar; that file's
2026-10-28 measurements say they are from before #237. `NxSrtParse`'s header says the counter is dropped. The #237
entry names its author.

**Tests changed.** `SrtTests`' "no blank line between cues" checked only the second cue, so it passed with the first
reading `A` and `2`; it now compares both cues whole (tydude001's call). A new case keeps a line of digits before a
blank line.

**Seen** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4) with a test-data build of `37cc228` signed in to the lab Emby as `nxlab`, the TV's
captions set Off first by a one-off app: *Lab Forced Opus* item-linked, and Home pressed within 40 ms of a poll of
the node tree (about two a second) seeing its forced line shown, 12 s after the link, in two runs. The TV's caption
mode read Off 1, 6 and 21 s after each, and 5 and 25 s into a relaunch after the first. Set back On afterwards.
Emby only: Jellyfin wasn't run.

**Open.** The forced-sidecar branch in `applySubtitles` can't run since #237: both callers of `NxMbSubtitleSidecars`
pass `drawForced`, and Plex never sets `forcedSub`. Left in here; it comes out as its own change (Chad, #298).

## 2026-11-11 (Android: CI's release lint)

**Changed.**
- GUIDE TIMEOUT (#290) hears the remote through `Activity.onUserInteraction` now, not an override of `dispatchKeyEvent`. Calling `super.dispatchKeyEvent` reaches androidx's `ComponentActivity` override, which is `@RestrictTo`, so `:app:lintRelease` failed on CI with `RestrictedApi`. Measured on a SHIELD (Android 11): 5 D-pad presses called it 10 times, once on key down and once on key up, the same as the override did. `:engine:test :app:lintRelease :app:assembleDebug` pass locally.
- The Roku job's `trailers` check allows `Owen Voke` as well as `tydude001` (`NX_TRAILER_OK`'s default in `roku/tests/tools/scan-added.py`, and the row in `roku/tests/README.md`). It ran on #151 because the branch edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which is in the Roku path filter, and failed on the Android commits' AI co-author lines. Chad chose this over rewriting the history: #151 is squash-merged with a message he writes, so the trailers don't reach main. The allowance is keyed on the commit's author name, so the GitHub account name would not have matched. Locally the check passes: 71 commits, 70 with a trailer, all counted, none failed. The Roku suite's other checks pass, and its two warnings are read and harmless (`secrets` flags the upload key's passwords, which come from a properties file, not literals; `addresses` lists a placeholder in the server hint, test vectors and version numbers).

**Next.**
- Once CI is green, #151 comes out of draft for Chad's code owner review and squash merge.

## 2026-11-11 (Android: a file that runs past its slot no longer leaves the player behind the guide, #293)

**Measured first.** On a SHIELD (Android 11), a test copy of the app played a channel of five 2 min 50 s films from a lab Jellyfin; each gets a 2-minute slot, so each runs 50 s past it. A throwaway log line at each natural end recorded what the guide had on, and how far in, against what the player started:

| Natural end | Guide had on | Player started | Player behind the guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:53:31 | Drift One, 51 s in | Drift One at 0 s | 51 s |
| 10:56:22 | Drift Three, 102 s in | Drift Three at 0 s | 102 s |
| 10:59:13 | Drift Four, 33 s in | Drift Four at 0 s | 33 s |
| 11:02:04 | Drift Two, 84 s in | Drift Two at 0 s | 84 s |
| 11:04:55 | Drift Three, 15 s in | Drift Three at 0 s | 15 s |

The lag stays under one slot, because the player always takes the programme the guide has on now. But for most of each programme, Now Playing named one film while the guide showed the next.

**Changed.**
- At a natural end the engine's pick starts at 0 s (`advancePick(..., fromNaturalEnd = true)`), which main's Apple TV also does, because a file's real length can differ from its metadata.
- The Apple TV 1.0.32 holds a real file to the guide's clock instead (not on main yet; ported from the issue's description). `NaturalEnd.pick` does it in the app layer, so the shared schedule engine and its golden tests are unchanged:
  - when the guide has already moved on to the programme the engine picked, the player joins it where the clock says, as a tune-in would;
  - when the file ended inside its own slot, or the conflict rule picked another programme, the next one starts at 0 s as before.
- `NaturalEndTest` has the rule's cases and a model channel of 170 s files in 120 s slots over 20 natural ends: up to 50 s or more behind without the rule, never behind with it.

**Measured after,** the same channel for 13 minutes: at each of 7 natural ends the player started at the guide's own position (51 or 52 s in), with picture 0.7 to 0.9 s later, and the ends fell every 2 minutes, at :31 or :32 past. Not measured on a Google TV, or on Plex.

All 344 engine tests pass. Not pushed yet.

**Changed.**
- **#290, GUIDE TIMEOUT.** A new row under PLAYBACK & PICTURE, after GUIDE TEXT SIZE, as on the Apple TV, with its wording.
  - One press cycles OFF, 5 MIN, 15 MIN. The default is 5 MIN, and anything else saved reads as the default. It is saved as "off", "5m" or "15m" under `nostalgex_guide_timeout`, on this TV only.

## 2026-11-11 (Android: STOP WAITING ends the whole scan, and a killed first setup resumes; #285, #288)

**Changed.**
- **#285, STOP WAITING.** With more than one server on, the viewer's press now ends the whole scan, as on the Apple TV 1.0.32. No server after it is read, and what the servers before it gave is kept for the guide. Before, the press abandoned only the server being read and the next one started.
  - A server that stalls by itself (210 s with no progress, no press) is still skipped alone.
  - The loop is `ServerScan.readAll` in the engine, with 7 tests: a press on the first or second server, a press on a server that gave nothing yet, a stall with no press, and failed servers.
  - Not measured on a TV: it needs two servers, one of them slow.
- **#288, resuming a killed first setup.** Each library section is now written to its own file (`SectionStore`, `files/scan-sections`, never the library snapshot) as soon as it has been read in full, as the Apple TV 1.0.32's `LibraryScanProgressStore`.
  - The next scan uses a kept section instead of asking the server when `ScanResume.reusable` allows: under 6 hours old (the Apple TV's snapshot age), written by this `versionCode`, and on Plex with the same section change stamp (`updatedAt`, `contentChangedAt`). A Plex section with no stamp is read again.
  - A section abandoned part way is never kept. The kept sections are deleted once a whole library has been read, and on DISCONNECT.
  - Jellyfin and Emby sections are kept before the server's address and token are added to the items.
  - `ScanResumeTest`: the rule's cases, and a Jellyfin scan that dies at the third library and then reads only that one.
- **Measured** on a Google TV emulator against a lab Jellyfin 12.4 with eight video libraries, through a proxy that delayed each library's items by 4 s:
  - The first setup was killed while it read the fourth library, after keeping the first three.
  - On the next launch the app's existing guard offered TRY AGAIN (two loads in a row had been interrupted). After the press, the three kept libraries were used, the server was asked only for the five that hadn't finished, the library loaded with all 6 items, and the kept files were gone.
  - Not measured on Plex or on a TV.
- **#286 follow-up.** The saved library's `FORMAT` is 7, so a library saved before audio tracks kept their own titles is read again rather than used without them.

All 329 engine tests pass. Not pushed yet.

## 2026-11-11 (Android: no channel starts on a commentary, and the missing-channel lines held to the shared file; #286, #292)

**Changed.**
- **#292.** `ChannelRequirementsGoldenTest` replays `scripts/channel-requirements-golden.json`.
  - Android's `ChannelRequirements.plainLanguage` already gives the same lines for all 142 channels in `channels.json`, so no wording changed. No line says "package".
  - The test fails when one wording is changed ("Movies only" to "Films only" was tried and reverted).
  - The golden file is a test input in `engine/build.gradle.kts`, so a change to it reruns the test.
- **#286, the commentary rule.** A track whose title says "commentary" (any case) is never the audio a channel starts on while the file has another track. The viewer's language, the default flag and the channel count are judged over the tracks that are left. With only commentaries, the earlier rules run over all of them.
  - `AudioPick` ports `scripts/nostalgex-audio-pick.js`, and `LanguageChoice.preferredAudioIndex` uses it for the Jellyfin and Emby track it pins.
  - `AudioPickGoldenTest` replays `scripts/audio-pick-golden.json`: the commentary titles, the 15 Jellyfin and Emby cases and the 4 Plex cases all pass. Without the rule, the Jellyfin and Emby cases fail. Android's own language order (the viewer's language, then English) gives the file's answers for every case.
  - Jellyfin and Emby tracks now keep the server's own `Title` beside `DisplayTitle` (`AudioStream.rawTitle`), from the scan and from PlaybackInfo, because the display title can leave the word out.
  - **In the player** (every backend, direct play included), the language pick skips a track whose label says commentary, as the Roku's direct-play rule (#246).
  - **On a Plex server stream**, the item's own audio streams are read before the decision call (`PlexClient.audioStreams`, at most 5 s). When Plex's selected stream is a commentary and another exists, `audioStreamID` asks for that one for this stream only, as the web tuner does. The track saved on the Plex account isn't changed.
- **Measured** on a Google TV emulator against a lab Jellyfin 12.4, with a film whose first audio track is a default-flagged English "Director's Commentary" and whose second is an English "English" track.
  - **Direct play:** the player opened on the commentary, and the rule moved it to "English".
  - **Server stream:** PlaybackInfo pinned audio 2, "English".
  - Before this change both would have started on the commentary: the two tracks have the same language and channels, so the default flag or the first track won.
- **Not measured:** the Plex paths, which need a claimed Plex server and so were not run.

All 313 engine tests pass. Not pushed yet.

## 2026-11-11 (Android: the Plex code waits 15 minutes, DISCONNECT forgets playback failures, Remux or Transcode; #284, #289, #291)

**Changed.**
- **#284, the Plex sign-in code.** Android now waits as long as plex.tv keeps the code: the PIN's `expiresIn`, at most 1,800 s, and 300 s when plex.tv doesn't say (`PlexPinWait`, as the Apple TV's `plexPINLifetime` and the Roku's `NxPlexPinWaitSeconds`). It used to stop after 150 polls, which is 5 minutes.
  - It polls every 2 s by the clock, an approval on the last poll still counts, and an expired code is replaced by a new one, as before.
  - Measured against plex.tv on 2026-11-11: a new code said `expiresIn=900`, and an unentered code answered 200 at minutes 4, 6, 12 and 14, then 404 at minute 16.
  - A code approved at minute 12 on a TV was not tried.
- **#289, the last playback failure.** DISCONNECT clears the saved playback failures and the "Last playback failure" line in Settings, as the Apple TV 1.0.32 does.
  - A Plex sign-in, the server picker or a Jellyfin or Emby sign-in clears them too, unless the new servers share one with the old ones (`ServerSharing.sharesAServer`): the same machine or server id, or the same host and port. So adding or removing one of several keeps them.
  - On a Google TV emulator signed in to a lab Jellyfin, the line showed before DISCONNECT, and the saved verdicts were `[]` after.
  - The rule has 9 tests. The sign-out half has none, because the app module has no unit tests; the emulator run stands in for it.
- **#291, PLAYBACK INFORMATION.** For a Plex server stream the PLAYBACK row says Remux when Plex's decision copies the video, and Transcode when it re-encodes it. `PlexDecision` reads the video stream's `decision` from the answer the server stream already asks for (#192).
  - With no decision, and on Jellyfin and Emby, it says "Server stream" as before. Jellyfin's PlaybackInfo answer doesn't plainly say whether the video is copied, so it is left alone, as the issue allows.
  - Held to two answers for Android's real request, saved from an unclaimed lab Plex 1.43.5 that was deleted straight after: High-profile H.264 copied, and Constrained Baseline H.264 re-encoded.
  - The row itself was not seen on a screen, because a Plex server stream needs a claimed server.

All 308 engine tests pass. Not pushed yet.

## 2026-11-10 (Android: the Plex server stream keeps 5.1 and 4K, asks its decision first, and skips Dolby Vision 5; #197, #192, #193 measured)

**How it was measured.**
- **Server:** a lab Plex Media Server 1.43.5 in Docker, with 13 generated 70-second films and a second library of six Dolby Vision profile 5 films.
  - Audio: 5.1 AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS (core only; ffmpeg can't make DTS-HD MA) and TrueHD.
  - Video: AAC 5.1, 10-bit H.264, AV1, MPEG-2 and 4K HEVC Main 10, plus a control and a High-profile H.264 with DTS 5.1.
  - Dolby Vision: profiles 5 and 8.1, made with `dovi_tool` and `mkvmerge`. The profile 5 file's base layer is HDR10, not Dolby's IPT colour space, so it shows whether a decoder takes it but not what its colours look like.
- **TVs:** a SHIELD (Android 11) and a Google TV emulator (Android 16). Not measured on a real Google TV.
- **Method:** a throwaway build, not committed, that played one chosen film through the real playback path and logged the first rendered frame.
- **The two TVs:**
  - The SHIELD decodes Dolby Vision profiles 4, 5, 8 and 9 and has no AV1 decoder. It passes AC-3 and E-AC-3 through, but not DTS or TrueHD.
  - The emulator has no Dolby Vision decoder and no AC-3 or E-AC-3, outputs stereo, and decodes HEVC (not 4K 10-bit) and AV1.

**#197 (direct play decided by trying the file).** No code. On the SHIELD, tune to first frame:

| File | First attempt | Fell back | First frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| H.264 + AAC (control) | direct play | no | 0.70 s |
| AAC 5.1 | direct play | no | 1.09 s |
| AC-3 5.1 | direct play | no | 0.66 s |
| E-AC-3 5.1 | direct play | no | 0.69 s |
| DTS 5.1 | direct play | yes, no audio decoder | 1.26 s |
| TrueHD 5.1 | direct play | yes, no audio decoder | 1.69 s |
| 10-bit H.264 | direct play | yes, no video decoder | 1.12 s |
| AV1 | direct play | yes, no video decoder | 1.15 s |
| MPEG-2 | direct play | no | 1.04 s |
| 4K HEVC Main 10 | direct play | no | 2.91 s |
| Dolby Vision 8.1 | direct play | no | 2.33 s |
| Dolby Vision 5 | direct play | no | 1.96 s |

Every failed attempt fell back within the track check, about a second; none waited for the 15 s watchdog. By the issue's own test this closes with the table. A Google TV whose decoder claims a file and then shows nothing was not met here.

**#192 (Plex server stream client profile).** Measured first with today's request. Plex's decision and what reached the player both said that DTS 5.1, TrueHD 5.1 and 4K HEVC Main 10 came as 1080p 8-bit H.264 with stereo AAC. Changes:
- `PlexClientProfile.extra` builds `X-Plex-Client-Profile-Extra` in the Roku's shape (codecs added to Plex's Android profile), with the Apple TV's raised HEVC limits and E-AC-3 cap:
  - HEVC when the TV decodes it, with 3840x2160 and 10 bits when it decodes those;
  - AC-3 and E-AC-3 when the TV passes them through or decodes them;
  - no lossless target.
- The Apple TV's form, a whole `add-transcode-target`, is ignored by Plex for `X-Plex-Platform=Android`: everything still came as stereo AAC.
- The request adds `directStream=1` and `directStreamAudio=1`.
- After, on the SHIELD through the server stream:
  - DTS, TrueHD and AAC 5.1 arrive as E-AC-3 6ch, and AC-3 5.1 as AC-3 6ch.
  - High-profile H.264 is copied.
  - 4K HEVC Main 10 and Dolby Vision 8.1 are copied at 3840x2160 with E-AC-3 6ch, first frame in 2.3 s and 3.1 s.
- On the emulator (stereo, no Dolby) the profile offers neither, and 5.1 comes as stereo AAC as before.
- The STARTED log line now ends with the audio codec, channel count and video size that reached the player.
- The Jellyfin and Emby hand-built stream asks `TranscodingMaxAudioChannels=6`. Not measured against a server.
- The 8-bit H.264 test films were Constrained Baseline (ffmpeg's ultrafast). Plex re-encodes those even with the profile; High profile is copied.

**Plex's decision before each server stream (found while measuring).**
- Plex 1.43.5 refuses `start.m3u8` with HTTP 400 ("Denying access due to session lacking decision for transcode") when this client has started that film before and the session has no decision.
- The app never asked one, before this change or after, so flipping back to a channel whose film was on the server stream showed "Your server wouldn't start this one".
- Reproduced with curl and the old request: the first start 200, repeats 400 at 1 s, 60 s and 120 s, with one 200 at 30 s.
- Now `PlexClient.decision` asks `/decision` with the same query and session first, capped at 5 s, off the main thread. The same film tuned six times in a row: 6 of 6 played, decision in 26 to 72 ms.
- The Apple TV already asks it first (`PlexAPIService.decisionURL`, corrected on 2026-11-11: an earlier search for the literal path missed it). The web tuner and Roku build no decision request, read from their source; not checked whether they meet the 400.

**#193 (Dolby Vision profile 5 from Plex).**
- Plex answers 2003, "DoVi (Profile 5) color space is not supported", to a request that doesn't offer HEVC.
- With the #192 profile it copies profile 5 as HEVC instead. A TV without a Dolby Vision decoder then shows the base layer through a plain HEVC decoder, which for real profile 5 is green and purple.
- So when direct play finds no decoder for a track whose codecs say profile 5 (`dvhe.05`, `PlexClientProfile.withholdHevcFor`), the server stream offers no HEVC. Profile 8 (`dvhe.08`) is still offered HEVC: its base layer is HDR10.
- A decision that is 2003 naming DoVi (`PlexDecision.isDolbyVisionRefusal`, as the Apple TV's) skips the programme: no card, not one of the channel's five failures, the next programme straight away.
- The profile isn't read at scan: Plex's bulk listing doesn't carry `DOVIProfile`, only an item's own metadata does, and the decision answers it for nothing extra on the tune that needs it.
- A channel of nothing but such titles stops after 5 skips in a row (`PlexDecision.SKIPS_BEFORE_STOP`) with the channel-stopped card. Its diagnostics line says "5 failures", though they were skips.
- Measured on the emulator:
  - **Before**, profile 5 failed direct play and was refused, and the card said "Your server wouldn't start this one".
  - **After**: no decoder for `video/dolby-vision`, then a server stream without HEVC, then decision 2003 in 30 ms, a skip, and the next programme.
  - **A channel of six profile 5 films:** 5 skips in about 15 s, then "Nothing on this channel will play right now".
- On the SHIELD, which decodes profile 5, it direct plays as before.
- Tests: `PlexDecisionTest` from decision answers saved from the lab server (`engine/src/test/resources/plex-decision`, library ids and identifiers taken out), `PlexClientProfileTest`.

All 292 engine tests pass.

**Next.** A real Google TV for #192 and #193. Chad to decide whether the other surfaces ask Plex's decision first. The lab server is to be removed from the Plex account afterwards.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: libraries hidden on Jellyfin behind one switch, #224)

With the parameter taken out of `userViewsPath`, 3 of its 7 tests fail. All 274 engine tests pass.

On the server, the plain list leaves out the hidden library, `includeHidden=true` adds it, the library without access is in neither list, and asking that library for items directly answers HTTP 401.

Not measured on a real Google TV.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: the home-screen row of #194, held for a question)

**Half-done.** The link half of #194 is on `feature/android` (`9f5dc22d`). The "On Now" row isn't built: whether Google TV shows an app's row at all is unanswered, and Google TV is where #194 asks it to be measured.

**What the docs say.** Android TV's home-screen guide (developer.android.com, "Recommend content on the home screen") is the only one Google publishes.
- An app's first channel is its default and appears without the user approving it (`PreviewChannelHelper.publishDefaultChannel`, or `TvContractCompat.requestChannelBrowsable`).
- It needs `com.android.providers.tv.permission.WRITE_EPG_DATA` and `androidx.tvprovider`. The library also merges `READ_EPG_DATA` into the manifest.
- The home screen can be told to create the row at install with `android.media.tv.action.INITIALIZE_PROGRAMS`.
- The guide says nothing about Google TV. What reports there are say Google TV hides third-party rows or doesn't show them:
  - an open issue on Google's own `android/tv-samples` (#83) has channels created but never shown on API 30;
  - open-source TV apps' notes from this year describe the same.

**Measured.**
- A throwaway build (not committed) published a default "On Now" channel with three cards.
- On a Google TV emulator (Android 16) the channel was created (id 5), but the home screen can't be reached without signing in to a Google account, so whether it shows wasn't seen.
- On a SHIELD it was created with `browsable=false` and not shown. That SHIELD's home screen is a third-party launcher, not the stock Android TV one, so that says nothing either way.
- `PreviewChannelHelper.getAllChannels` in tvprovider 1.0.0 throws on a channel published without a description; the real channel must set one.

**Next.** Chad's answer: whether any app's row shows on his Google TV, or a probe build tried there. If it does, the row is a launcher channel as #194 describes, plus the privacy text, and posters served by the app's own content provider (a Plex poster URL carries the token).

## 2026-11-09 (Android: RESCAN LIBRARY's coverage line and last playback failure)

**Why.** The Apple TV's RESCAN LIBRARY row has four parts, so a support report can say in one screenshot what the app holds and where it went: the library summary, a coverage line, "Last updated", and the last time playback was given up on. Android's had the first and third (the cap that would have cut the rest went in `cf41c7ad`).

**Changed.**
- `LibraryDiagnostics` (new, `android/engine`) is the Apple TV's coverage and `coverageLine`: titles on a channel with every package on, titles on none (split by kind when more than one kind has some), and titles skipped for having no runtime.
- `Lineup.coverage()` filters the channels of packages that are off once, since the guide never needed them, and keeps their pools. It counts a channel with rules whose pool reaches its minItems, plus the collection and franchise channels. `AppModel.ensureLibraryCoverage` runs it in the background when SERVERS & ACCOUNTS opens and again after the lineup changes.
- Both scans count what they drop for having no runtime (`PlexLibrary.skippedNoRuntime`, `MediaBrowserLibrary.scan`'s `onSkippedNoRuntime`). The count is from the last finished scan, so it reads 0 after a launch from the saved library until the refresh behind the guide ends.
- `PlaybackDiagnostics` (new) and `PlaybackFailure.diagnosticSummary` are the Apple TV's: the last 5 verdicts, newest first, under `nostalgex_playback_verdicts_v2`, with URLs, tokens and credentials redacted. They are recorded where the Apple TV records them:
  - the watchdog's direct play to server stream, and its capped 1080p retry;
  - a stall on direct play, or on the server stream;
  - an error card, and a channel stopping.

  Each is logged as `WATCHDOG VERDICT`. A direct-play error that falls back at once isn't recorded, as on the Apple TV.
- Tests: `LibraryDiagnosticsTest` (the Apple TV's `LibraryCoverageTests` wording, case for case, and the counting) and `PlaybackDiagnosticsTest` (the line, the 5 kept, redaction including percent-encoded, the summaries). 253 engine tests, 0 failures.

**Measured on a SHIELD.** On the 11,396-item Plex library the row read "10,305 OF 11,396 ON CHANNELS · 1,091 ON NO CHANNEL (18 MOVIES, 1,073 EPISODES) · 1 SKIPPED (NO RUNTIME)". The count took 2.3 s off the main thread.

**Not checked.** The "Last playback failure" line on a TV: nothing failed after the build went on. The line's format, keeping and redaction are covered by the tests.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: collection members read four at a time, as the web tuner reads them)

**Why.** On a SHIELD, reading a Plex server's 288 collections took 81.3 to 81.6 s on every launch refresh, against 18 to 20 s for the 11,396-item library itself (noted in the entry on collection member order, below). The web tuner's `fetchPlexCollections` and `fetchBoxSetCollections` read the members of four collections at once (`mapLimit(list, 4, ...)`), but the Android port read them one at a time. Its own comment on the BoxSet read said so.

**Changed.**
- `Collections.mapLimit` is the JS's: at most `COLLECTION_READS_AT_ONCE` (4) calls at a time on a small thread pool, the results in the list's order whatever order they finish in.
- `fetchPlexCollections` and `fetchBoxSetCollections` read members through it. A collection whose read fails is still dropped, and the progress count still runs from 1 to the total.
- `CollectionsMapLimitTest` (new, 4): order kept when calls finish out of order, never more than 4 at once, an error comes through, an empty list.

**Measured on the SHIELD.** Two launches: the 288 collections read in 24.1 s and 24.3 s, against 81.3 to 81.6 s before, about 3.4 times faster. Both refreshes said "unchanged", so the parallel read gave the same collections as the one-at-a-time read had saved.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: a new member order in a Plex collection no longer rebuilds the guide)

**Why.** On a SHIELD with a 11,396-item Plex library, the launch refresh logged "collections changed, rebuilding" on runs where nothing had changed. A diagnostic build (not committed) logged the difference. All 288 collections matched by id and title, but 4 listed the same members in another order: the same set of child keys in a different sequence. They are adjacent collection ids, most likely smart collections sorted by plays or last watched, which reorder after something is watched. `refreshInBackground` compared the collections as lists, so each reorder rebuilt the whole lineup. A second launch, with no reorder, said "unchanged".

**Changed.**
- `Collections.sameMembers` (`android/engine`): the same collections, by id, title and server, with the same members in any order.
- `refreshInBackground` rebuilds only when that says no. A member order that moved is still saved, so the next build follows the server's order as the Apple TV's next load would, and the log says "unchanged (collection members in a new order, saved)".
- A pool does follow member order, and the running order follows the pool. But a packed day is stored and stays put (`DailyManifest`), so a reorder never needed a mid-day rebuild.
- `CollectionsSameMembersTest` (new, 3). It pins one limit: two lists of the same length that repeat different members compare as the same, which a server's collection, listing each member once, can't produce.

**Measured.** Three launches on the SHIELD after the change: "unchanged" each time, the refresh reading the items in 18 to 20 s. None of the three happened to reorder a collection, so the saved-reorder branch ran in the tests only.

**Noticed, not changed.** Reading the 288 collections took 81.3 to 81.6 s on every launch, one request per collection in turn, against 18 to 20 s for the library itself. The Apple TV reads Plex collections only when a collection package is on. Android reads them with every load and refresh, as the Roku does (android/README.md lists this). Reading them several at a time would cut it, and is a separate change.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: the library is read again every 6 hours, #195)

**Why.** Android read the library only at launch and on RESCAN LIBRARY, so a film added on the server while the app ran never appeared. The Apple TV (`startDailyRefresh`, `refreshLibraryIfChanged`) and the Roku (`DailyRefresh.brs`) read it again behind the guide on their own (#195).

**Changed.**
- `DailyRefresh` (new, `android/engine`):
  - the due rule: every 15 minutes, a refresh once the last load and the last check are both 6 hours old;
  - the Plex signature from each section's `updatedAt` and `contentChangedAt` (`LibraryChangeSignature`; `scannedAt` is left out because Plex's scheduled scans bump it every run);
  - the skip: unchanged signature, and a scan under 24 hours old.
  - `DailyRefreshTest` holds it to the Roku's `DailyRefreshTests.brs` cases and the Apple TV's `LibraryRefreshEfficiencyTests` signature and skip cases.
- `AppModel`:
  - The timer runs while the guide is up, never in demo mode, and never starts a refresh while a load or a refresh is running.
  - On Plex it asks each server's `/library/sections` first (`PlexLibrary.stamps`). Jellyfin and Emby have no signature and always rescan, as before.
  - A changed library is swapped in by `refreshInBackground` as before, without stopping what is playing.
  - Every full load and every refresh records the load time, the check time and the signature. An abandoned scan is backdated a day and has no signature, as on the Apple TV.
  - They live in `Prefs` rather than the saved library, so saved libraries stay valid; sign-out clears them.
- `MainActivity`: the timer stops with the activity (`onStop`) and starts again with it (`onRestart`), as tvOS suspends the Apple TV's loop. A TV left on another app doesn't rescan behind it, and the first check after coming back is 15 minutes later.

**Measured on a SHIELD (Android 11).** A temporary build with a 30 s check and a 60 s threshold, not committed:
- On the 11,396-item Plex library, the launch refresh read everything in 34.5 s, with the Java heap peaking at 114 MiB.
- The next check asked for the section stamps, found them unchanged, and skipped the rebuild in 31 ms, the heap flat at 61 MiB.
- A copy against the test Jellyfin: with the guide up, a fifth film was added on the server. The next check rescanned (no signature) and read 5 items in 448 ms. The guide gained the film as UP NEXT and two channels, with no relaunch and the programme still playing.

**Not checked.**
- A Plex library that changes, to see the signature move on a real server. The change rule is covered by the Apple TV's cases.
- The real 15-minute and 6-hour times on a TV.
- The launch refresh on this library logged "collections changed" on runs where the library hadn't changed, as in the #196 runs. That looks like the collections comparison, not this change, and is not looked into here.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: Plex titles with a Latin-1 byte, #196)

**Why.** Plex copies a file or folder name into its JSON byte for byte, so an unmatched item named in Latin-1 puts a lone 0xE9 in its title. Android read every Plex answer with OkHttp's `body.string()`, which turns such a byte into U+FFFD, so the guide would read "Caf� Society". The Apple TV, the web tuner and the Roku read the byte as Windows-1252 and show "Café Society" (#196).

**Changed.**
- `PlexUtf8Repair` (new, `android/engine`) is the Apple TV's `PlexUTF8Repair`. Every byte outside a well-formed UTF-8 sequence (Unicode table 3-7) is read as Windows-1252, and the five bytes Windows-1252 leaves undefined keep their Latin-1 code point. A valid answer is decoded as it is. One leading byte order mark is dropped, as `body.string()` did and a JSON parser expects.
- `PlexClient.getJson`, which every Plex library, section, episode, collection and plex.tv resources read goes through, reads the bytes, repairs, then parses. A repair logs the Apple TV's line, `PLEX UTF-8 <path>: repaired N byte(s) that were not UTF-8, read as Windows-1252`, with any token left out of the path.
- `Utf8RepairGoldenTest` holds it to `scripts/utf8-repair-golden.json`, the cases the Apple TV, the web tuner and the Roku already read: all 27 match. It also checks a Plex-shaped page with a lone 0xE9 in a title parses to "Café Society", with valid accents and emoji untouched. With the Windows-1252 table taken out, the curly-quote case and others fail.
- The not-ported note in `PlexLibrary.kt` and the README line that said titles weren't repaired are gone.

**Measured on a SHIELD (Android 11).** The launch refresh of a 11,396-item Plex library, two runs of each build, alternated:

| Build | Read in | Peak Java heap |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 24.3 s, 23.7 s | 143 MiB, 128 MiB |
| After | 22.2 s, 19.9 s | 120 MiB, 133 MiB |

That library is valid UTF-8 throughout (no repair line was logged), so it measures the cost of reading bytes and checking them, and that is within the run-to-run spread.

**Not checked.** A real Plex item with a Latin-1 name on a TV: the library measured has none. The repair itself is covered by the shared cases.

## 2026-11-09 (Android: a scan where every library fails is a failed load, #198)

**Why.** Chad found it reading the code (#198). When a server lists its libraries and then fails every item request, each library was skipped as one bad library, the scan came back empty, and the empty library was saved. The guide said NO CHANNELS FOUND, and so did every launch after, from the saved copy. A RESCAN LIBRARY from that screen that did find channels left the screen as it was.

**Changed.**
- `SectionTally` (new, `android/engine`): a scan counts the libraries read and keeps the first error. Both scans use it: `MediaBrowserLibrary.scan` for Jellyfin and Emby, `PlexLibrary.scan` for Plex.
  - One library that errors is still skipped while the others are read. Android keeps this, where the Apple TV fails the whole scan.
  - If every library errored and none was read, the scan throws `EveryLibraryFailed` with the first error. The load then shows CONNECTION FAILED in that error's words, and nothing is saved.
  - A library that answers with no items counts as read, so a genuinely empty library still gives NO CHANNELS FOUND.
- With several Plex servers, one whose every library failed is skipped like a stalled one. The load fails only if no server was read.
- `LibraryStore.load` ignores a saved library with no items, so a launch does a full load instead of showing NO CHANNELS FOUND again.
- `refreshInBackground`: a rescan from NO CHANNELS FOUND that builds channels closes Settings and brings the guide up, as a package switch already did.
- Tests: `EveryLibraryFailedTest` (new, 4), and `MovieSectionScanProgressTest`'s one-library failure now expects the scan to fail. Removing the check fails 2 of them. 216 engine tests, 0 failures.

**Measured on a SHIELD (Android 11).** A copy of each build under another package name, against a test Jellyfin 12.4 behind a proxy that answers 500 to every library item request:
- Before: NO CHANNELS FOUND after the load, and again on relaunch from `SAVED LIBRARY 0 items`. A RESCAN with the proxy passing everything read 4 items and built 1 channel, and the screen stayed on NO CHANNELS FOUND.
- After: CONNECTION FAILED, "Jellyfin returned HTTP 500. Check the server is running, then try again." A relaunch did a full load again rather than reading a saved copy. With every library answering empty, the load gave NO CHANNELS FOUND, and a RESCAN with the proxy passing everything brought the guide up on CH 03, playing in 0.7 s.
- A Plex sign-in on the same SHIELD still loads its 11,396-item library and plays.

**Not checked.** A Plex server that fails its item requests; the Plex path shares `SectionTally` but was run only against a healthy server.

## 2026-11-11 (Web tuner: the guide row no longer runs past its window when an airing crosses local midnight)

**Why.** The 24-hour guide window holds two days' blocks, and the next day's first airing starts at 00:00 whatever
the day's last airing is doing. When that last airing runs past midnight the two overlap, and `renderGrid` tiled blocks
end to end, so the overlap was counted twice. Found by a harness on the Roku issue #297 night (a 104 minute movie from
23:24 to 01:08, 68 minutes past midnight); the Apple TV already handles it (`ProgramRowLayout.segments` trims the
later airing), so this brings the page in line.

**Measured before, on the real engine and the page's own `renderGrid` (stub DOM).** Movie channel, that night, every
minute of the three hours before midnight: the row was wider than the 2-hour window in 90 of 180 windows, up to 156.7%
of it (the excess is clipped by the row, so what shows is an airing drawn where it does not air, 60 windows, and an
hour before midnight the row totalled 150%). Episode channel, a 36 minute episode 15 minutes past midnight: wider in
90 of 180 windows (112.5%) and the programmes after the overlap drawn up to 15 minutes late. In a real browser
(headless Chromium, clock pinned to the evenings before midnight, a Jellyfin-shaped lab server) every window checked
at phone, tablet, desktop and 960x540 had a row wider than its strip, for example 1525 px of programmes in a 1220 px
strip on desktop.

**Changed.**
- `scripts/nostalgex-program-row-layout.js` (new): the Apple TV's cursor walk. An airing that overlaps the one before it
  is trimmed at its start, one wholly inside it is not drawn, and a hole between airings is a spacer at its true
  position, so the row totals exactly the window.
- `plex-tuner.html`: `renderGrid` draws from those segments. A trimmed block is not marked live (the airing that owns
  those minutes is). Holes were also pulling every later programme left on a time-restricted channel; they hold their
  place now.
- A block under 8% of the window (about 10 minutes) drops its side padding. A browser will not draw a block narrower
  than its padding, and the real-browser run found 6 to 12 px of overflow from exactly that once overlaps were trimmed
  to a few minutes. It applies to any sliver at a window edge, not only to the midnight case.

**Tested.** `npm run test:program-row-layout` (in `npm test`): the module against the cases of `ProgramRowLayoutTests`,
the page's own `renderGrid` on the two nights above, and the hole, trim, sliver and empty-row cases. Against the old
`renderGrid` it fails 12 checks (the same runs: widest 156.7% and 112.5%, 15 minutes late); after, 0 windows wider and
0 programmes off their time. `npm run test:program-row-layout:browser` is the real-browser run (needs Playwright,
like the other `:browser` smokes): 20 checks pass after; against the old page every viewport fails with rows wider
than the window in all 12 windows.

**Not changed.** Playback and the tune: no retune happens on the web at slot end (`tickProgress` only rebuilds the
panels), so this is the guide row only. The engine and its goldens, the Apple TV and Roku are untouched. After
midnight the harness also saw the guide row name the next day's first airing at the now line while the info panel
still named the movie that is playing. That is which airing the engine calls "now" in the overlap, not how the row
is laid out; it is not touched here and its cause is not established.

**Shipped.** Pushed to main on 2026-11-11 after a review of the branch and a full `npm test` pass. The push deploys the
hosted tuner. The Docker image shares the page and picks the fix up at the next `tuner-v` tag; no tag was cut for this,
so the image on the registry does not have it yet.

## 2026-11-10 (Roku: a commentary on the player's own list is passed over on a direct play, #246)

**Why.** After #236 a Jellyfin or Emby direct play still played a commentary when the server's track list
didn't name it one: Emby 4.10.1.0 kept no title for the lab MP4's audio tracks (its `Title` is empty, where Jellyfin
12.2.0 reads the same file's), so the app's pick from that list can be a commentary. And on a Plex direct play with no film track
in AUDIO LANGUAGE the pick names no track, which left the player on the track it started with, which can be a commentary.

**Changed.** Both on the player's own list (`availableAudioTracks`, by each track's `Name`), as Chad scoped it on
#246. A Jellyfin or Emby pick the player names a commentary, beside another track, goes to the first track in the
pick's language that isn't one, else the first that isn't one (`NxAudioTrackPastCommentary`). With no pick, a player
on a commentary beside another track moves to the first that isn't one (`NxAudioTrackOffCommentary`), as #246 asks of the
Plex track: the selected one, else the first, never a commentary while another is left. The console's `audio track` line marks a commentary.

**Not changed.** Plex's server stream, which carries the track Plex chose; that half stays open on #246.

**Tested off the TV.** 15 new audio track cases; `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4), test-data builds signed in to the lab Emby as `nxlab`, item-linked. Two silent
60 s lab clips, H.264 with two AAC stereo tracks: an English "Director's Commentary" marked default, then a Portuguese
track titled "Portuguese", one as MKV and one as MP4 (the titles also as the MP4's handler names). The Roku's `Name` holds
"commentary" for the first track in both.

| | `3ea0ca9` (the no-pick rule only) | `a2972b8` (this PR's code; `111659d` is the same tree, its message reworded) |
|---|---|---|
| MKV | `audio track 3 of 2=eng (commentary) 3=por, was 2`, 1 play | the same, 4 plays of 4 |
| MP4 | `audio track 2 of 2=eng (commentary) 3=por, was `: the commentary, 1 play | `audio track 3 of 2=eng (commentary) 3=por, was `, 2 plays of 5 |

**Open.** On 3 of the 5 MP4 plays of `a2972b8` the console has no `audio track` line: `applyAudioPick` returned
before any pick, so the player kept its own track, which wasn't read. The early return is main's, ahead of this
change, and why it happens on the MP4 (3 plays of 6 over both builds) and not the MKV (none of 5) wasn't looked into. Not run on a TV: the no-pick rule
(`NxAudioTrackOffCommentary`), which a Plex direct play is the case for, a Plex file at all, and Jellyfin.

## 2026-11-10 (web tuner: parity group 5, the playback recovery ladder, #258)

**Why.** From reading the code (not measured): the web stopped a channel after 3 failures in a row where the Apple TV allows 5, never tried a 1080p
stream, and skipped a frozen stream after 8 s without asking for a smaller one.

**Changed.** `scripts/nostalgex-playback-recovery.js`, a port of `PlaybackStarvation.swift`, `ChannelFailureRun.swift` and the ladder rule in `AppState+Playback.swift`
(18 checks replaying the Apple TV's starvation tests, in `npm test`). The page now goes direct play, then the server stream (as before), then ONE retry capped at 1080p from where the
program is (Plex: `maxVideoBitrate=12000`, `videoResolution=1920x1080`, `autoAdjustQuality=0`; Jellyfin and Emby: the HIGH ceiling), then the failure card. It skips that retry
when STREAM QUALITY already caps at 1080p or lower. A stream that was playing and starves (three stalls of 3 s inside two minutes, or one freeze of 20 s) gets the same retry, then is
skipped; the old 8 s freeze also tries the retry first. Five failures in a row stop the channel (was three). `playback-recovery-browser-smoke.mjs` (13 checks, a Plex stub that fails
on demand and Playwright's clock). **Roku and Android** have their own ladders (PARITY rows 100 and 101); compare against `nostalgex-playback-recovery-smoke.mjs`.

**Not verified.** Against a real server on a stream that really starves; the 20 s and 3-stall paths are driven by a faked playhead.

that program. `plex-tracks-browser-smoke.mjs` covers the rows and the choice (17 checks).

list heading and its aria label, Settings pane lines, the hint, the keyboard help line, the seasonal offer pill). Identifiers, ids, CSS

## 2026-11-10 (web tuner: parity group 1, the audio pick, Plex tracks and the /decision check, same branch)

**Why.** Chad asked for all the web parity issues (#248 to #261) to be worked and closed before the next web and Docker release.
This is the first group: #256, #250, #249.

**#256, Plex and `/decision`.** Measured, no change needed. `scripts/plex-start-decision-probe.mjs` sends the web tuner's own
`start.m3u8` request (same query, same order) to a real Plex server for a channel change every 1.5 s and every 0.3 s, 20 changes each, with and
without the old session stopped (12 changes at 0.4 s with the stop lost), plain and with `/decision` first. Lab Plex 1.43.5 in a Linux
container, software transcode: 0 of 92 `start.m3u8` answers were not 200 in either mode, median 10 ms plain and 15 ms with the
decision call. The Apple TV saw its 400s on a Mac with a hardware encoder, so this does not prove a hardware encoder behaves the same;
the probe takes `PLEX_URL`, so it can be pointed at any server.

**#250, commentary.** New `scripts/nostalgex-audio-pick.js` (`isCommentary`, `skippingCommentary`, `preferredAudioStream`,
`plexAudioStream`), a JS port of `AudioTrackCommentary.swift` and `JellyfinPlaybackResolver.preferredAudioIndex`, with
`scripts/audio-pick-golden.json` (the Apple TV test vectors) and `nostalgex-audio-pick-smoke.mjs` (33 checks, in `npm test`). The web's
Jellyfin and Emby pick now follows the Apple TV: never a commentary while another track exists, then AUDIO LANGUAGE, then a track in the
browser's language or English with the most channels, then the file's default. Auto used to leave the server's default alone; it now
pins like the Apple TV. `jellyfin-audio-streams-browser-smoke.mjs` expects that and has a default-flagged commentary case.

**#249, Plex tracks.** At tune time a Plex program's metadata is read (2.5 s cap, cached) for its audio and subtitle streams. AUDIO
LANGUAGE, the Apple TV's pick and the commentary rule choose an audio track and the server stream is asked for it (`audioStreamID`); a
file that would play directly but needs another track goes to a server stream. Subtitles inside the file are burned into the server stream
(`subtitles=burn`, `subtitleStreamID`), a subtitle file beside the film (SRT) is fetched from `/library/streams/<id>` and drawn by the page.
Plex accepts both parameters (200 playlist on the lab server); `plex-tracks-browser-smoke.mjs` (11 checks) covers the requests
against a stub. Not verified: that the burned text shows in the picture, and an image subtitle (PGS) burn. The "Jellyfin and Emby only"
wording is gone from Settings and the keyboard list. **Roku and Android** port `audio-pick-golden.json` (#236, #245, #246 on the Roku side).

## 2026-11-10 (web tuner: CHOOSE YOUR LIBRARIES, same branch)

**Why.** Chad asked for the library pick the Apple TV has: choose which libraries become channels, so a library you do not
want is never scanned.

**Changed.** New `scripts/nostalgex-library-selection.js`: one stored set of libraries switched OFF, under
`nostalgex_deselected_library_sections` (the Apple TV's key name), entries `<serverId>::<sectionKey>`. The server id is the
Plex machineIdentifier (the name when there is none) or the Jellyfin/Emby server URL (lower case, no trailing slash); the
section key is the Plex section key or the Jellyfin/Emby view Id, so a rename or rescan never changes it. Default is none
off, so existing installs see no change. The scan loops (`scanOnePlexServerSections`, `fetchJellyfinLibraryScan`) skip OFF
libraries and nothing else. First setup shows CHOOSE YOUR LIBRARIES between the server step and the scan (Apple TV layout,
logo left, list right, CONTINUE focused, Up/Down walk, Enter/Space toggle, Esc/Left back to the server list on Plex with more
than one server); only on a visit straight from a sign-in, never on a restored saved login. Settings > SERVERS & ACCOUNTS
lists the libraries first; toggling clears the library cache and rebuilds like RESCAN LIBRARY (guide stays up), the last
library that is on cannot be turned off (as on the Apple TV), a change made during a rescan runs a second rescan after it.

**Tests.** `npm run test:library-selection` (23 checks, in `npm test`). `nostalgex-plex-paging-smoke.mjs` counts the paged
section-list calls in the page, now four. `saved-login-browser-smoke.mjs` presses CONTINUE on the first sign-in.

**Roku / Android.** No Roku or Android equivalent exists yet; the key and the id rule above are the contract to port.

## 2026-11-10 (web tuner and Docker: first visual batch, branch only)

**Why.** The Apple TV and the web tuner had drifted apart on type, contrast and states. Chad asked for the audit's first
batch, and then for the web tuner to use the Apple TV's face. Branch `web/visual-batch-1-1110`, off main at `8a06696d`,
not pushed: hosted and Docker take the same two pages, so it ships as one change when Chad says go.

**Changed.**
- **Face.** DM Mono Regular (values and text) and Medium (labels) are served by the tuner itself, `tuner/fonts/` and
  `tuner/fonts.css`, the same TTFs the tvOS app and the Roku package ship, with the OFL text beside them and in the
  Docker image's `vendor/licenses/`. Before this the CSS named DM Mono and never loaded it, so those lines drew in the
  browser's monospace. VT323 stays for channel numbers, CH tags, times, countdowns and the guide rows. Press Start 2P and
  Silkscreen are gone from the tuner pages and from the Google Fonts request and the Docker font sheet. The sign-in panel
  on `web-tuner.html` follows (it called Space Mono a stand-in for DM Mono).
- **Floors, in screen pixels.** DM Mono and anything carrying state 12px, VT323 16px (Chad's rule: 1 Apple TV pt is 0.5
  CSS px on a desktop and on a TV browser). The two TV-browser steps zoom the whole page (0.875 and 0.6667), so the audit's
  px numbers were not what the screen drew; `--nx-z`, `--nx-fs` and `--nx-fs-tag` keep the floors true to the screen at
  every step. Guide rows keep their own sizes (GUIDE TEXT SIZE owns them).
- **The rail** is a list of rows, label left and value right, so SETTINGS can no longer run into QUALITY (they shared two
  58px tiles). On a 960x540 TV browser it is two columns of 48px cells with no key hints and no APPLE TV tile.
- **Text colour.** Every white text alpha is now one of four steps (0.55, 0.7, 0.85, 1), channel colours used as text are
  mixed toward white until they reach 4.5:1, the playing cell of a selected guide row is 45% of the channel colour on the
  page background (white on it is 5.19:1 or better on all 97 colours in channels.json).
- **States.** One look for every ON/OFF button: OFF grey, ON cyan outline, focus the cyan slab. Chips: chosen is a bar under
  the chip, never a fill, so a focused chip cannot look chosen. A 3px white focus ring replaces the browser's 1px one.
- **Phone Settings tabs** share the width (they ran 9px off both edges at 390) and are 44px high.

**Half-done / not done.** Guide rows at the 960x540 step draw VT323 at 12 screen px (floor 16): the fix is a taller row and a
Large default for that class, which halves the visible rows, so it waits for Chad. A few glyphs DM Mono and VT323 lack
(arrows, star, check, cup, triangles) still come from the system font. The unused @fontsource packages for Press Start 2P
and Silkscreen are still in package.json.

**Verified.** See the audit doc, `WEB-VISUAL-AUDIT-2026-11-10.md` in the internal docs, for the before and after numbers.


## 2026-11-10 (Roku: a Jellyfin or Emby forced subtitle track is drawn by the app, #237, first half)

**Why.** Roku shows its captions only while the TV's caption mode is on, so the app switched that setting on to show
a forced track and put it back afterwards. Back restores it since #170; Home leaves it on until the next launch
(#117). Drawing the lines in the app means the setting is never touched (#117's option A). By tydude001, PR #272.

**Changed, Jellyfin and Emby.** The forced track in SUBTITLE LANGUAGE is no longer handed to the player as a
sidecar. `ForcedSubTask` fetches the server's SRT at tune, `source/subtitles/Srt.brs` reads it into cues, and
`GuideView.drawForcedSub` puts the current line in a Label under the CRT overlay, in full screen and in the guide's
preview, ten times a second. The player reports its position every half second, so the time since the last report is
added (`NxForcedSubMs`). The line gives way while the player's own subtitles show. SUBTITLES (OFF, FOREIGN AUDIO,
ALWAYS) and its full tracks are as they were, through the TV's captions.

**Not yet: Plex, and a picture track.** The Roku keeps no list of a Plex file's subtitle tracks; it would take the
per-tune request asked about on #246. A forced track that is a picture (PGS, VobSub) has no text to draw.

**A TV refused `box` as a variable name** ("Builtin function call expected", five lines of `GuideView.brs`) after the
interpreter, static analysis and the guards had passed it. Renamed, and `check-guards.sh` now refuses it as it does
`run`.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4) against the lab Jellyfin 12.2.0, test-data builds of `ad74ada` to `227f4af`
plus three scratch aids (a linked item starts 285 s in, an input that sets the TV's caption mode, a log line per drawn
change), with *American Dad!* "Pilot": an HEVC MKV whose one forced English line runs 4:57.208 to 5:02.166.
- The track came in 6 to 16 ms once the server had it (281 ms the first time) and was read in 0 to 2 ms.
- First build, the reported position alone: drawn 291 ms late, cleared 338 ms late.
- With the time since the report added (`227f4af`), by the app's own clock: direct play, drawn 30 to 96 ms after
  the line's start and cleared 1 to 76 ms after its end (six runs); server stream, 87 and 88 ms, 35 and 35 ms.
- TV captions On: On before, during and after. Set Off: Off before, during and after, and 6 s and 21 s after Home.
- Two dev screenshots show the line: at the foot of the full screen picture, and inside the guide's preview box.

**Then on the lab clip *Lab Forced Opus*** (30 MB, silent; a Portuguese AAC and an English Opus track, an English
forced track with lines at 0:10 and 0:40 and a full one at 0:20), signed in as the lab-clips user, a test-data build
of `c21c2a9` plus the scratch aids. The English Opus track is picked, so each run is a server stream.
- Jellyfin 12.2.0, TV captions On: both lines drawn 33 ms after their starts and cleared 33 ms after their ends; On
  before, 15 s in and after. Captions Off: 75 ms and 75 ms; Off throughout.
- Emby 4.10.1.0, captions Off: 33 ms and 33 ms; Off throughout. Captions On: 70 ms and 70 ms; On throughout.
- SUBTITLES on ALWAYS (Jellyfin, captions Off before): as before this change. The full track showed through the TV's
  captions, which the app switched On for it (On 15 s in) and back Off when the clip ended, and no forced line was
  drawn.
- A long track, made on the TV: 2,000 cues (186 KB) were read in 322 ms, and 100 looks near its end took 307 ms.
  So `NxSrtTextAt` now finds the last cue to have started by halving and looks at the 16 before it.
- An unchanged build of `6ebdd4a` (no scratch aids), the same clip on Emby, TV captions On: it compiled and ran; the
  node tree had the first line up with the player at 13.0 s and hidden at 16.5 s, the second up at 41.0 s and
  hidden at 48.0 s (one look every 2 to 3 s); captions On before, during and after; and a dev screenshot at 13.0 s
  shows LAB FORCED LINE ONE at the foot of the screen.

**Open.** Whether the line matches the picture and the speech was not watched or listened to (volume at zero; the
times are the player's). A stick, and a real film with a long forced track. The timings above are from the builds
with the scratch log line; the unchanged build was looked at only through the node tree and one screenshot.
## 2026-11-10 (Roku: audio tracks titled commentary are passed over, #236)

**Why.** A film with a commentary track could air with the commentary: the file marks it default, or it has more
channels than the film's own track in the same language, and the pick goes by language, channels and default (#153).

**Changed.** A track whose title holds "commentary", in any case, is dropped from the pool while the file has any
other audio track, before any language or default step, as the Apple TV's `AudioTrackCommentary.skippingCommentary`
(Chad on PR #245, stricter than the issue's wording). A file whose every track is a commentary picks among them as
before. On Jellyfin and Emby the scan marks the track from the stream's `Title` or `DisplayTitle`
(`NxMbAudioTracks`), and `NxMbChosenAudioIndex` and `NxMbPreferredAudioIndex` pick from `NxMbSkipCommentary`'s pool.
That pick is the server stream's `AudioStreamIndex` and the direct play's track. On the player's own list (a Plex
stream, a direct play that listed fewer tracks than the file has, and AUDIO LANGUAGE in the Now Playing panel)
`NxAudioTrackForLanguage` and `NxAudioTrackToSelect` go by the track's `Name` (`NxListedSkipCommentary`); with only a
commentary in the language they leave the player's own choice. The exact-language rules are as they were, and a file
with no commentary picks as before.

**Not changed.** Plex's server stream, which carries the track Plex chose. The Apple TV's cases
(`AudioTrackSelectionTests.swift`) aren't on main yet, so the Roku cases are its own.

**Tested off the TV.** 29 new audio pick cases and 5 new audio track cases; `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED.

**The first cut read "fits" by language** (`c699030`, the build the TV runs below used): a commentary alone in the
viewer's language was still picked over a film track in another. Chad's rule replaced that, and six cases written
for the first reading were turned round with it: an English commentary now loses to a Portuguese film track (three
cases), a German commentary to an English film track, and on the player's list a commentary beside another track is
never picked (two cases).

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4) against the lab Jellyfin 12.2.0, test-data builds of main `9b5292a` and of
`c699030` (the first cut, above), with The Hills Have Eyes (1977): an HEVC MKV whose default track is English mono ("Original theatrical
mono", index 2) beside three English stereo commentaries (3 to 5). Item-linked, the pick read from the console and
from Jellyfin's ffmpeg log, where the mono is stream 0:1 and the first commentary 0:2. Volume at zero: nothing was
listened to.

| | main `9b5292a` | `c699030` |
|---|---|---|
| Direct play (STREAM QUALITY Auto) | `audio track 3 of 2=eng 3=eng 4=eng 5=eng, was 2`: switched to a commentary | `audio track 2 of 2=eng 3=eng 4=eng 5=eng, was 2`: stays on the film's track |
| Server stream (STREAM QUALITY High) | ffmpeg `-map 0:0 -map 0:2`: a commentary | ffmpeg `-map 0:0 -map 0:1`: the film's track |

On `c699030` Videodrome (English mono, German stereo, two English stereo commentaries) direct-played on track 2 of
`2=eng 3=ger 4=eng 5=eng`. It was not run on main. In that library 143 films have a track titled commentary, and by
the server's track lists main's pick is a commentary on these two.

**Open.** Not run on a TV: a film whose only English track is a commentary, Emby, a Plex stream, and whether a
Roku's `availableAudioTracks` names a commentary by its title (both direct plays went by position).

## 2026-11-10 (Roku: the Plex link code is waited for as long as plex.tv keeps it, #240)

**Why.** The code on screen gave up after 150 polls, 5 minutes, while plex.tv keeps a code for 15 (`expiresIn: 900`,
measured for the Apple TV, N-007). A viewer who took longer to reach plex.tv/link entered a code the TV had already
dropped.

**Changed.** `NxPlexCreatePin` keeps the PIN's `expiresIn`, and the wait goes by the clock (`NxPlexPinWait` in
`source/mediabrowser/SignInFlow.brs`): a poll every 2 s until `expiresIn` seconds have passed, 300 when plex.tv
doesn't say and never more than 1,800, as the Apple TV. A 404 from the PIN check still ends it on that poll, and both
ends show the same "The code expired. Press CONNECT TO PLEX for a new one." A poll that couldn't reach plex.tv is not
an answer and waits on, as before. Jellyfin's Quick Connect keeps its 150 polls.

**Tested off the TV.** 17 new cases in the sign-in flow suite, the wait run against a faked plex.tv and a faked clock:
a code entered after 10 minutes signs in, one never entered expires at 900 s, a PIN dropped at 40 s stops the wait on
that poll with nothing asked after it, no `expiresIn` waits 300 s, a day-long one stops at 1,800 s, and slow polls
still end by the clock.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4), a test-data build of `dd17385`, signed out, CONNECT TO PLEX, the code left
unentered:
- The console said `waiting up to 900 s for the code (plex.tv keeps it 900 s)`.
- 6 min 4 s in, past where 150 polls gave up, the code was still on screen.
- 899 s in, plex.tv answered the PIN check 404 and the wait ended on that poll: `the code expired after 899 s
  (439 polls)`. So on a real code the 404 ended it, a second before the clock would have.
- The screen did not change then. It showed "The code expired. Press CONNECT TO PLEX for a new one." on the first
  page 4 min 29 s later, the moment a key was pressed.

**Why the screen waited for a key: the TV's screensaver, by inference.** This TV's screensaver starts 10 minutes
after the last key (measured afterwards: last key 12:22:47, Roku City up between 12:32:45 and 12:32:54), so it was
up from about 10 minutes into the wait. The sign-in task went on polling under it (439 polls in 899 s), and its
answer reached the screen only when the key woke the TV. The screensaver was not looked at during the wait itself.
So with a 15 minute wait the screensaver covers the code for its last 5 minutes on this TV, which a 5 minute wait
never reached. The loading screen holds the screensaver off (`LoadingView.xml`); the code screen does not.

**Open.** A code entered late (after 5 minutes) on a TV, a stick, and whether the code screen should hold the
screensaver off.

## 2026-11-10 (Roku: INCLUDE LIBRARIES HIDDEN ON JELLYFIN, off by default, #231)

**Why.** A Jellyfin user can hide a library from the home screen, and `/UserViews` leaves it out unless asked with
`includeHidden=true`, so the Roku scan never read it. The web tuner (1.0.15) and the Apple TV already ask.

**Changed.** `NxMbViewsPath` takes the switch and adds `&includeHidden=true` for Jellyfin only; off, the request is
byte for byte what it was, and Emby's never changes. The switch is `source/mediabrowser/HiddenLibraries.brs`, off
unless turned on, in the registry's `player` section. The row INCLUDE LIBRARIES HIDDEN ON JELLYFIN, with the web's
line, is on SERVERS & ACCOUNTS between the servers and RESCAN LIBRARY, on a Jellyfin sign-in only. A press saves the
switch and reads the library again in the background, as RESCAN LIBRARY does; while a load runs the row reads
UPDATING… and a press does nothing, so no load is ever for the other position.

**A library saved with the other position.** Read from the code, not run: if the app closes before the re-read ends,
the next launch shows the saved guide, and its background refresh scans Jellyfin again (a Jellyfin library is scanned
on every load) with the switch as it now is.

**Tested off the TV.** The golden file's nine `views` cases are read with its `sections` and `types`. A
`hidden-libraries` suite, 19 cases: the switch on a stand-in registry, and a scan against a stub that lists two hidden
libraries only with `includeHidden=true` and never lists a third. On, the hidden films and episodes are scanned; off,
none is and no hidden library is asked for items; the unlisted library is never asked. With the parameter taken out,
3 of the 19 and 3 of the golden cases fail.

**Pressed** on the 55R617 (OS 15.3.4), a test-data build of `b72d36f`, against the lab Jellyfin 12.2.0 as a user
who hides Shows (4,755 episodes) from the home screen and has no access to Lab Music Videos (4 items):
- Signed in to the lab Emby first, SERVERS & ACCOUNTS had no such row: the server, RESCAN LIBRARY, SIGN OUT OF EMBY.
- On Jellyfin the row is between the server and RESCAN LIBRARY and read OFF. The load read 834 items and built a
  guide of 11 channels (the server counts 836 in the two libraries it listed; the scan kept 834).
- OK on the row: it read UPDATING…, then ON. The re-read had 5,589 items 17.5 s after the press, 4,755 more, and
  its guide of 17 channels was handed over 28.7 s after the press with no retune of the channel playing.
- OK again: OFF, 834 items and the same pools fingerprint as before the switch.
- Nothing of Lab Music Videos was read in either position: 4,755 is Shows alone.

The row's words and states were read from the node tree (port 8080), not a screenshot.

**Open.** A stick. Not looked at: the row as drawn (no screenshot), a hidden library's title on a channel on screen
(the counts and the six more channels stand in), the request on the wire, a press while a load runs (ignored, by the
code), and the app closed before the re-read ends.

## 2026-11-09 (Roku: OPEN ON LAST CHANNEL, on by default, #230)

**Why.** The Roku opened on the first channel in the guide at every launch. The Apple TV and the web tuner open on
the channel the viewer last tuned, on by default on every platform since Chad's decision of 2026-11-09.

(on unless a stored value says otherwise) and the channel's id and name, both in the registry's `player` section.

the row after AUDIO LANGUAGE with the Apple TV's line. Sign-out clears the channel and leaves the switch.

match cases and every channel in `channels.json` finding itself, and the seed's channel. `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL
TESTS PASSED.

**Pressed** on the 55R617 (OS 15.3.4), a test-data build of `3690863` plus two scratch lines (a launch switch that
deletes the `cachefs:` files a power loss takes and keeps the registry, as #155's run had, and a timing print),
signed in to the lab Emby (5,657 items, 17 channels, CH 3 first):
- With nothing remembered the launch opened on CH 3 and saved CH 3's airings for a cold start.
- OK on CH 6 in the guide, Home, launch: it opened on CH 6, tuned 1.7 s after the app started (picture 3.2 s later).
- The seed moved to CH 6 at the next re-check, 5.7 s after that OK.
- Launched with the files wiped: CH 6 was tuned from the seed (16 airings) 1.1 s after the app started (picture
  3.6 s later), and the full guide's hand-over 27 s after the tune made no second tune.
- The row is after AUDIO LANGUAGE and read ON before anyone pressed it. Switched OFF, the seed moved back to CH 3
  10.6 s later, after Settings closed, and the next launch opened on CH 3.
- Saving the channel on a tune took 37, 41, 31 and 33 ms on the render thread (four tunes).

**Open.** The TV's power really pulled (the wipe stands in for it), a stick, a Plex library, and the 31 to 41 ms a
tune now spends on the registry write. Not pressed on a TV: Left and Right in full screen and the mini strip (only OK
in the guide was), sign-out, a deep link, and a remembered channel that is renamed or gone.
## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: GUIDE TIMEOUT sends a guide left alone to fullscreen)

**Why.** The guide holds the Apple TV awake while its preview plays (`ScreenAwakePolicy`), so tvOS's screensaver
never starts there. A guide left up for hours keeps the logo, header and grid lines still on screen, which can burn
into an OLED. Fullscreen video keeps moving.

**Changed.** New PLAYBACK & PICTURE row GUIDE TIMEOUT: OFF, 5 MIN (default) or 15 MIN, per Apple TV and never
synced. After that long with no remote press on the guide, the playing channel goes fullscreen, the same as
Play/Pause. It only runs while the guide is in front and a channel is playing; Settings, the loading screen and an
empty guide are left alone. `RemoteActivityMonitor` notes every press and touch-surface swipe with a window gesture
recognizer that never recognizes, so it never takes a press from the focus engine. `TunerView` checks every 5 seconds
and restarts the clock when the guide comes back from fullscreen or Settings.

**Tested.** `GuideTimeoutTests` (default, cycling, the timing rule) and `GuideTimeoutUITests` in demo mode with
`-uiTestGuideTimeoutSeconds 20`: a guide left alone for 30 seconds goes fullscreen, and a guide pressed every 8 seconds
for 40 seconds stays up. Both passed twice. `NostalgexTests` and the OPEN ON LAST CHANNEL UI tests pass with the new
row. Not tried on a real Apple TV.

**Not changed.** Roku and the web tuner keep the guide up indefinitely; they need the same setting for parity.

## 2026-11-10 (Docker: one lineup held by the container, I-080; branch web/docker-settings-1110)

**Built, not pushed, not run in nginx.** Chad chose option 1 for I-080 (a Docker user on a Raspberry Pi had to turn the same
packages on in every browser): one global lineup, last write wins, display preferences and the sign-in stay per browser, the
hosted site unchanged. The container now holds `nostalgex-settings.json` in a `/data` volume. nginx serves it and takes a PUT of
it with its WebDAV module, so there is no backend; `docker/40-config.sh` writes the location into `/tmp/nostalgex/settings.conf`
only when `nginx -V` lists `--with-http_dav_module` (and `NOSTALGEX_SHARED_SETTINGS` is not off), and `docker/nginx.conf`
includes that folder by glob. A missing module therefore leaves no location rather than an nginx that will not start. The page
side is `scripts/nostalgex-server-settings.js`: it runs only when the page carries the selfhost marker, reads the file once
with a synchronous request before the page's script (the page reads its packages from localStorage in its first lines), and
sends the six shared keys back after the first tap or key press of a visit and a settled 1.5 s. It never sends anything outside
those keys, drops any value that contains this browser's own token, and ignores anything outside them in what it reads. A read
that failed (500, a newer file) turns writing off for the visit, three refused writes in a row do too, and a missing file, an
image without the feature, no volume, or a read-only one all leave the page exactly as it was.

**Measured.** `npm run test:server-settings` (84 checks, including the real entrypoint script run against a stand-in `nginx -V`
with and without the module, with the feature off, and with a typo) and `npm run test:shared-lineup` (55 checks, headless, the
real `vite build --mode selfhost` output at 960x540 and on a phone, against a stand-in container: read, a change sent once with
no token, login or display preference in it, a third browser starting from it, nothing saved yet, an image without the
feature, a failed read, a newer file, a refused PUT, the hosted page never asking for the file, and the page with the module
removed as the negative control).

**Not run.** nginx and Docker. Whether `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine` has the WebDAV module is expected (nginx.org's
packages build with it) but not confirmed; the `docker-smoke` job in `ci.yml` now does the real round trip with curl (a
volume on `/data`, a PUT, the file back, still there after a restart, a DELETE refused, no volume refused, feature off) and
runs on a pull request, not on a push to main. The synchronous read is one request to the same nginx that just served the page;
it has no timeout of its own, since a synchronous request cannot be given one.

**Behaviour to know.** The first browser to make a change after the container gains the feature becomes the shared lineup,
whatever the other browsers held. Not shared, and not decided: per-user lineups.

## 2026-11-09 (Docker: settings kept on the server, I-080; looked at, not built; branch web/fixes-1109)

**Not built, on purpose.** The ask (a Docker user on a Raspberry Pi: "I keep having to go into settings and turn stuff on and
off ... I would like people to be able to log in and have it be ready") needs a decision first: what is shared between
browsers, and whether it is one lineup for the whole container or one per signed-in user. Facts gathered so the decision is
quick. The image is nginx serving static files (`docker/nginx.conf`) with a read-only root filesystem and only `/tmp` writable,
so today it can store nothing; every setting lives in the browser's localStorage. The lineup settings are small: the channel
config was 8,454 bytes on a default install, plus the enabled packages, collections and franchises. The login
(`plex90_saved_auth`) is the only credential and stays per browser either way. nginx can take a `PUT` of one small file with its
WebDAV module (`dav_methods PUT`) into a mounted volume, so no backend is needed; that is from nginx's packaging and has **not**
been run (Docker was off the table for this pass). The hosted tuner would stay per-browser, and the page already
tells the two apart (`<meta name="nostalgex-build" content="selfhost">`).

## 2026-11-09 (Web tuner and Docker: STOP WAITING during a slow library scan; branch web/fixes-1109)

**STOP WAITING (parity with Apple TV, Roku, Android).** The loading screen had START OVER and nothing else, and the scan's page
requests had no timeout: a Jellyfin or Emby `/Items` page, or a Plex section or episode page, that the server never answers
held the screen forever (only the Plex section list has the 15 s timeout). Measured first, in the browser, against a
Jellyfin-shaped server that stops answering a page: the loading screen was still up after 13 s with START OVER and the coffee
button the only things to press. Now `scripts/nostalgex-load-stall.js` watches each foreground scan the way
`LibraryLoadStallWatch.swift` does: the scan's counters (phase, section, items, the line under the headline, and a count of
server answers) are sampled every 2 s, and only silence counts, never elapsed time. After 60 s of none the loading screen says
"Still waiting on your server. Nothing has come back for a while." with a STOP WAITING button and "Keeps whatever has loaded
so far. The rest is read again next time."; after 210 s the scan is given up on its own. Either way the requests are aborted,
the whole sections already read stay (on Jellyfin and Emby also the pages already read of the one in flight, as for any page
that fails), the guide is built from them, and the library is not saved as the library and does not count as the first load
(the web's existing "lost a section" rule, which is how the saved library is marked not whole here; the Apple TV backdates a
saved one instead). Nothing read at all is the error line STOPPED WAITING BEFORE ANYTHING LOADED with RECONNECT. A Plex press
belongs to the server it was made on (Apple TV #146): every server's scan starts its own watch, and a finished watch ignores a
press. One thing taken from the Roku port, not the Apple TV: a look more than 20 s after the last one (a laptop lid, a throttled
background tab) is not counted as quiet, since the Apple TV's wall-clock comparison would have abandoned a scan that was only
asleep. Not watched: a refresh behind a cached guide (no loading screen to press anything on).

**Test.** `npm run test:load-stall` (32 checks: 60 s and 210 s, silence only, an hour of a page every 40 s is not a stall,
sleep not counted, a press belongs to its watch) and `npm run test:stop-waiting` (60 checks, headless, the real page; the
timings are shortened to 3 s and 9 s after the shipped 60 s and 210 s are checked in the file): Jellyfin stuck on the second
page of the second library, pressed and left alone, at 960x540 and on a phone (the button is on screen and on top, no keys
needed); a library that keeps answering for 12.6 s, longer than the give-up time, loads whole and never shows the block;
nothing ever read; Plex with a stuck second section; and origin/main's page as the negative control (no block, still loading).
Four older smokes that lift these functions out of the page got stubs for the new helpers.
**Not verified.** A real slow server, a TV browser, Safari. The Plex multi-server press-carry is covered by the watch's own
test, not by two fake Plex servers in a browser. Emby is the Jellyfin code path; it was run for the refused login, not for this.

## 2026-11-09 (Web tuner and Docker: saved login audit and a refused login, I-024; branch web/fixes-1109)

**Saved login (I-024).** The web tuner already keeps the viewer signed in; the card was written before anyone measured it. Measured
on the real pages, headless, against a Jellyfin-shaped server (`scripts/saved-login-browser-smoke.mjs`, `npm run test:saved-login`):
signing in writes `plex90_saved_auth` in localStorage (backend, token, server address and name, user id, plus the typed address
and user name for the next sign-in form; for Plex also the account token) and a working copy of the token in sessionStorage. No
password is stored anywhere. A browser restart (localStorage and IndexedDB kept, sessionStorage gone) forwards web-tuner.html
to the guide, signed in, no connect screen. The login stays until the viewer signs out or the server refuses it; there is no
timer. SIGN OUT leaves no copy of the token or the user id in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or cookies, and empties
the library cache. It does not clear the channel settings, the install id, or the saved day schedules (`plex90_manifest_*`,
whose keys carry the server address and whose rows carry item ids); those stay in the browser. Not measured: Safari, which
may clear script-written storage after seven days without a visit, and a TV browser that wipes site data on exit.

**Fixed: a refused login was remembered.** Measured with a server that answers 401 to everything after sign-in: the first
request, the library list, was read as a library list. Jellyfin's `{}` made an empty library (NO CHANNELS FOUND, nothing says
why), and the saved login stayed. Where the screen did say SESSION ENDED, two things made it a dead end: the RECONNECT link
was created and then removed by `resetConnectScreen()` a line later, leaving the message beside CONNECT WITH PLEX (the Plex
button, for a Jellyfin or Emby viewer); and even with the link, web-tuner.html forwards a saved login straight back to the
tuner. Now a 401 or 403 on the library list ends the scan like the item pages already did, the refused login is forgotten (the
same removal Plex already did when plex.tv refused the token, now one function), the connect screen is reset before the
RECONNECT link is made, and only the Plex button is hidden, not the container that also holds the error line and the link.
Smoke: 43 checks, Jellyfin and Emby at 960x540 and a phone, Plex through plex.tv, and a negative control with the 401 handling
taken out. Not done: a revoked login while a cached library is showing still plays the cached guide and fails at playback
with the existing "sign in again" card.

**Stripe hover.** The focused package stripe is now unmistakable: it lifts out of its slot (38 pt, over the row's left
