The static check fails if the helper stops passing it. Nothing else in the app makes sound: the channel-change static's
noise is never enabled.

`GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests`, `ChannelGuideWrapFocusTests`). Simulator only.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: CHANNEL PACKAGES scroll fixed after a run on a real Apple TV, discussion #217)

**Found on a real Apple TV.** The list above was measured on a simulator, where the focused row always came to rest at the same
height. Run on an Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, tvOS 27.2) with the real remote it did not. Going down, the focused row's centre sat
lower and lower on the screen (0.41, 0.56, 0.62, 0.70, 0.79 of the screen height); going up, every row rested with its top at one
place, so down and up disagreed; and on the jump to OVERTIME the row's top was at 197 pt, above the pinned header's lower edge at
206 pt, so its title line was hidden under the header. The walk test only compared the row against the window, so it could not see
that. What held up: every row grows and shrinks, the tallest (NOSTALGEX, 22 names) is 268 pt, and fast taps (0.23 s a press),
13-press bursts, a 20-press jitter and 2.5 and 5 second holds all ended on the right package with no row left half open.
The names of an off package read at 4.41:1 against the focused row, just under 4.5:1.

**Changed.** The Settings pane centred the focused row at the moment of the press, while the row before it was shrinking and the
new one growing. A package row (the only rows that change size) is now placed after the rows have stopped changing size: the
pane waits the row's own animation time plus a frame, centres the row once, and once more with no animation to finish a slide the
system cut short. A new press cancels the wait, so a held press scrolls once, where it stops. Every other row centres at once, as
before. The centre of the pane is one point whatever a row's height, and the tallest row is well inside it, so a package row sits
wholly below the header, in the same place going down as going up. The cause on the device was not isolated (the system's own
scroll to the focused row, or a centre worked out before the rows had finished moving); both are covered by placing the row last,
and neither is proved. The off-state names go from 45 to 47 percent white (4.66:1).

**Test.** `SettingsPackageChannelsTests` now checks the focused row's top against the pinned header's lower edge (the top of the
rows' scroll view, plus its 32 pt fade and a margin), not only against the window, and holds rows in the middle of the list to
one resting height (within 0.01 of the screen) and each row to the same height going up as going down (0.01). On the simulator
the walk reads as before: 0.58 for every middle row, and it passes with the new header check (75 s). `PackageChannelListingTests` (22) adds the 4.5:1 contrast check for every name
colour on the focused row.

**Measured.** On the tvOS simulator, one run each: `PackageChannelListingTests` 22 of 22; `SettingsPackageChannelsTests` 2 of 2
(the walk, and Select on a package; the second test was re-run alone after the test runner was killed by another run on the
same simulator).

**Not verified.** The simulator never showed the problem, so a passing simulator run does not prove this fix. It has to be run on an
Apple TV: the walk down and up, a jump to OVERTIME, fast taps and a hold.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: a focused package lists its channels on CHANNEL PACKAGES, discussion #217)

**Why.** A proposal from tydude001 on discussion #217 (Trello I-084). On CHANNEL PACKAGES a viewer cannot see what a package
adds without switching it on and waiting for the build, and the amber count on a row says how many of its channels are short
of content without saying which.

**Changed.** On CHANNEL PACKAGES (Settings, CHANNELS & BUNDLES) the focused row grows to list its channels under the
description. Names only, no channel numbers, in the package's own order (`channelIDs` in channels.json; every shipped package
lists them by ascending channel number, which is how the website's lineup sorts them, and a test pins that). They are one run
of small type, separated by commas, that wraps like any other text. A package that is off lists them dim. A package that is on
lists them brighter, with the channels short of content in amber and one line under the list, "Amber: not enough titles yet".
Only the focused row opens, so the page is no longer than before while a viewer scrolls past. Nothing new is stored: no key,
no page, and the names come from channels.json through the call the row already made (`bundleChannelAvailability`). WHY ARE
SOME CHANNELS MISSING? is unchanged and is still where the reasons are explained.

The list is a single `Text`. A custom layout that kept a separator off the end of a wrapped line was tried and dropped: a
plain `Text` wraps by itself and cannot lose a name, and a comma at the end of a line reads as ordinary typography.

VoiceOver reads the row's count as "4 channels do not have enough titles yet" ("1 channel does not have enough titles yet";
it said "need more content", and titles is the word the on-screen line and the WHY page use). It reads the names as the row's
hint, then which of them are short, because amber is colour only. The hint is applied only to a row that has names
(`accessibilityHintIfPresent`), so every other `SettingsToggleRow` comes back from it unchanged.

One rule decides which channels are amber (`PackageChannelListing`), and the row's amber count is read from the same list,
so the count names exactly what it counts. A package that is off, still building, or with nothing on air marks no channel:
the row already says so, and none of those showed a count before. (Not changed here: the total on WHY ARE SOME CHANNELS
MISSING? differs from the sum of the counts on the rows in three ways. It counts the FRANCHISES package, which has no row on
this page. It counts only channels that have rules. And it lists every channel of a package that is on with nothing on air,
where the row shows no amber. In the test library it reads 17 where the rows add up to 12.)

**Scrolling, the open risk.** The Settings pane scrolls to centre the row that took focus, in the same moment the row before
it shrinks and the new one grows. Measured on the simulator with the real focus engine, down through all 14 packages and back
up (a library of the shipped packages, some on with channels the sample library cannot fill): unfocused rows are 95 pt tall,
focused ones 129 to 268 pt (NOSTALGEX, 22 names and 4 amber, the tallest at 268; KIDZ ZONE, 15 names, off, 184; HIGH ROTATION,
last, on with 5 amber, 186). Every row in the middle of the list comes to rest at the same place on the screen whatever its own
height, 0.58 of the screen height, and the same place going up as going down. The first row and the last stop where the list
ends (0.41 and 0.70), and NOSTALGEX, second from the top and the tallest, rests at 0.56. No focused row was cut off at the top
or the bottom. Switching a package with Select keeps its list open and the row where it was, while it builds and after, and
back off. That is the simulator: how the focus engine and the scroll view behave on an Apple TV is not measured.

**Test.** `PackageChannelListingTests` (21): the names in package order, every shipped package read from channels.json with no
name dropped, every shipped package listing its channels by ascending channel number (the order the website sorts them in), a
long package, the amber set equals the channels without content and the badge counts them (exhaustive over every pattern of up
to six channels, on or off, building or not, against the rule it replaced), an empty package, a package with no missing
channels, off, building and nothing on air marking none, the drawn text (the names and nothing else, joined by commas, every
shipped package's names once and in order, a name never broken across lines, only the short ones amber, an off package dimmer),
and what VoiceOver hears (the count in titles, the names, which are short, and no hint for a package with no names).
`SettingsPackageChannelsTests` (UI, 2): the walk above, with the same row measured focused and unfocused, and the amber line
present on exactly the rows that carry the amber count; and Select on a package. Demo mode with a new test-only
`-uiTestPackageList`, which lists the shipped packages after DEMO, some on with channels short of content.

**Measured.** On this head, on the tvOS simulator (Apple TV 4K, 3rd generation): `NostalgexTests` 1,207 passed, 0 failed,
29 skipped (the live-server harnesses), `PackageChannelListingTests` among them 21 of 21. UI: `SettingsPackageChannelsTests`
2 of 2 and `SettingsChannelsDrilldownTests` 1 of 1 (it reads the row's new VoiceOver text). The screenshots show the names in
commas wrapping after a comma, with the amber ones amber.

**Half-done.** On `appletv/package-channels-preview`, off the 1.0.31 bundle branch (f2fda75d) and not merged into it, so that
build can ship without it. Not pushed, no build cut, not run on a TV. The Roku app and the web tuner are not changed. The list
text is 18 pt, a step under the row's description; whether that reads from the couch is a TV question.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: UI tests can no longer wipe a real Apple TV)

**What happened.** A UI test was run on a real Apple TV. It launched the app with `-uiTestResetCredentials` and no harness root,
so on the device the flag acted on the TV's real stores: it deleted the library snapshot, rewrote the settings and removed the
saved sign-in. The harness root was set for the test runner (`TEST_RUNNER_NOSTALGEX_HARNESS_ROOT`), but that variable only
reaches the runner, not the app a test launches. A UI test is isolated only if it sets `NOSTALGEX_HARNESS_ROOT` on the app's own
launch environment, and five test files launched with a reset and did not.

**Changed.**
- One launch helper for every UI test: `isolatedApp(arguments:)` in `NostalgexUITests/IsolatedApp.swift`. It sets
  `NOSTALGEX_HARNESS_ROOT` on the app, with a root of its own per test and run, so a new test cannot forget. Every UI test file that
  makes an app (twelve) now does it through the helper, the ones that already set a root by hand included. `realStoresApp(because:)` is for a
  test that has to see the real stores: it runs on the simulator only and skips on a device. None needs it today.
- In the app, the launch flags that delete or rewrite stored data act only while the harness root is set: `-uiTestResetCredentials`,
  `-reproAppReviewFlow` (which also overwrote the sign-in with a test token), `-uiTestInstantAuth`, `-uiTestRescanRowFixture`,
  `-uiTestLaunchMemoryInDemo`, `-uiTestForceLibrarySelection` and `-uiTestFranchiseFixture`. Any other launch ignores them, logs one
  line (`TEST FLAG: <flag> ignored ...`) and starts as a normal launch. A release build has no harness isolation, so it never
  acts on them. They are listed once, in `TestLaunchFlags`, and read through `TestLaunchFlags.isOn`.
- `scripts/ui-test-isolation-check.mjs` reads the Swift files and fails when a UI test file calls `XCUIApplication(` itself, names
  one of those flags without going through the helper, passes one to `realStoresApp`, or when the helper's copy of the flag list
  drifts from the app's. It runs in `npm test` and as its own CI job on every pull request (it needs no Mac).
- The RESCAN row test no longer launches a second "clear" app after each test: its fixture now writes into the test's own root, so
  there is nothing to clean up, and that extra launch was itself a launch on the real stores.

**Test.** `TestLaunchFlagsTests` (unit): every listed flag is ignored without isolation, acts with it, and a flag that only changes
what is drawn is never held. The static check was run against a test that calls `XCUIApplication(` directly, one that passes a
reset flag to `realStoresApp`, one with an empty reason, and a flag list that differs from the app's: each fails it.

**Measured.** On the tvOS simulator, one run each. UI: the ten classes that launch the app (`AppReviewReproHarnessTests`,
`ChannelGuideWrapFocusTests`, `FirstLaunchSmokeTests`, `FranchisesPageGateUITests`, `GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests`,
`NowPlayingPanelFocusTests`, `OpenOnLastChannelLaunchTests`, `SettingsChannelsDrilldownTests`, `SettingsOpenOnLastChannelTests`,
`SettingsRescanRowTests`): 27 tests, 26 passed, 1 skipped (the old instant-auth flow, skipped before this change), 0 failed.
Unit: `NostalgexTests` 1,236 tests, 1,207 passed, 0 failed, 29 skipped (the live-server harnesses). `LANDiscoveryUITests` and the
sign-in tour need real servers and were not run; they are converted and pass the static check.

**Not done here.** Nothing was run on an Apple TV for this change. The approach (the root set on the app, the real stores
compared before and after) was checked on a real Apple TV 4K (3rd generation) earlier the same day. A UI test added on another
branch that makes its own `XCUIApplication` will fail the check until it uses the helper. On `appletv/ui-test-safety`, off
`appletv/1.0.31-rc1` (ba30acba), not pushed, no build cut.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: package stripes in the guide, and a way to move along them)

**What.** A coloured stripe down the left edge of the guide, one per package, with the package name written up it. The
name is sticky: it sits in the part of its package that is on screen, so it stays readable while the viewer scrolls
through the package's channels. The idea is tango259's, from the contributor proposal; this is our own code.

**Where it fits.** The stripe fills the empty slot at the left of every row, so nothing moves: programs, channel names
and focus are where they were. (The slot is an accident of the layout: the header is 68 pt wider than the screen, so the
rows are centred in a frame that wide, which leaves 31.5 pt at the left of each row, 29.5 on the live and the focused row.
The stripe is 28 pt.) Each row draws its own piece of the stripe, so the colour scrolls with the rows.

**Colour.** One of ten colours that are already channel colours in the app, picked from the package name by a fixed hash,
so a name is the same colour on every launch and every Apple TV. The name is white or black, whichever reads better: at
least 4.5 to 1 on every colour. No two neighbouring shipped packages share a colour.

**Moving.** Left from the rows, with the time window at its start, focuses the stripe (a ring around the package's part of
it). Up and Down jump to the previous and next package, scrolling so its first channel is at the top (without animation
when Reduce Motion is on). Right goes back to the rows, on the first channel of the package the stripe is on, or on the
row the viewer left if the stripe has not moved. Select opens the package list (the left rail), and so does Left again.
Left on the rows used to open that list straight away; it is now two presses, the first to the stripe. The stripe is a
focus target only after that first Left, so it can never be where first focus, or the return from full screen, lands.

**Decided.** A channel in no package gets a plain grey stripe with no name, which Up and Down step over. FRANCHISES is one
package, as in the package list. A package whose channels are all filtered out has no rows and so no stripe. A one-row
package is 81 pt tall, so its name is cut to fit; below 44 pt of it on screen there is no name, only the colour. GUIDE
TEXT SIZE does not change the stripe: its name is 18 pt in both sizes, because the slot cannot grow. When tvOS brings
the first channel back into view on Right, it centres it like any focused row.

**Test.** `GuideStripesTests` (32): which package a channel is in, the runs, Up and Down past the ends and over unnamed
runs, the colour of every shipped package pinned, contrast on all ten colours, neighbours, and the label maths.
`GuideStripeFocusTests` (UI, 3, demo mode with four demo packages, own harness root): Left to the stripe, Down through
four packages and back up with each first channel at the top, no wrap at either end, Right back to the rows, Select and
Left again opening the list. The accessibility tree does not report the stripe as focused, so the test reads where focus
is from the guide's debug record. Simulator only so far; not seen on a TV.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: Retro mode loses the white tracking line)

**Why.** Feedback that the white line which ran down the screen in Retro mode is very distracting. It drew the eye away from
the picture: at each check, every 6 to 15 seconds, there was a 45 percent chance of a bright line that crossed the screen
for half a second to a second and a half.

**Removed.** The tracking line, completely: the view that drew it (`TrackingGlitchLine`), its state and timer, the
scheduling that rolled for it, and the two constants `RetroLook.glitchChance` and `RetroLook.glitchBrightness`. Retro mode's
overlay is scanlines, vignette and flicker, as before: the same constants and the same drawing code, nothing re-tuned. The
RETRO MODE row's line in PLAYBACK & PICTURE read "CRT scanlines, vignette, VHS glitch, 4:3 aspect ratio" and now reads
"CRT scanlines, vignette, flicker, 4:3 aspect ratio".

**Test.** No test pinned the constants or the line, and none here would catch the line coming back: it started hidden and
appeared 6 to 15 seconds after the overlay did, so a render of the first frame cannot show it. `CRTOverlayRenderTests` (3,
new) guards what stays. It renders the overlay over white and reads the pixels: a dark scanline every third row at about
the scanline opacity, and a vignette that darkens the corners and the edges and leaves the middle alone; and, over black, a
first frame that adds no light inside the edge. `NowPlayingPanelFocusTests` (3, the UI class that touches the RETRO MODE
rows) pass. Simulator screenshots of the guide and of full screen with Retro mode on (it is on by default), a second
apart, show the scanlines, the vignette and the edge still drawn. The whole unit suite was not run on that branch: the
change is the overlay and one line of text.

**Not changed here.** The Roku app still draws a tracking line and its Retro mode text still lists it (its Settings row and
its guide), as do two blog posts that describe Retro mode. The web tuner's removal is on its own branch, not on main. On
`appletv/retro-no-tracking-line`, off the 1.0.31 bundle branch (f2fda75d), not pushed, no build cut.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: the guide no longer shows its highlight move when it comes back from full screen, I-041)

**What the viewer saw.** Change channel in full screen, leave it, and the guide came back with the highlight on the row the
viewer had left from, then moved it to the channel that is playing. The first I-041 fix put focus on the right row, but the
move was in plain sight, and it was reported as clearly slower on an Apple TV 4K (1st generation, tvOS 26.6) than on a
simulator. The same thing happened when the guide first appeared: the first row, or the seasonal invite, was highlighted for
a moment before the playing channel.

**Why.** The highlight was drawn from the guide's focus state alone. tvOS hands focus back to the guide when the full
screen cover has finished closing, which on a simulator is about 0.55 s after the close was asked for, and it hands it to
the row it remembers, the old one. The guide moved focus to the live row a moment later (6 ms on a simulator, more on a
TV). For that moment the old row was the highlighted one. The guide itself was on screen the whole time the cover was
closing.

**Changed.**
- The guide draws the live channel's row highlighted from the first frame it is back, whatever row tvOS has focused for the
  moment (`GuideReturnFocus.highlighted`, held by `LiveHighlightHold`, from the close of full screen or the guide
  appearing). Real focus is still moved to the live row exactly as before.
- The hold lets go the moment focus is anywhere other than the handout of a wrong row: focus on the live row, or the
  viewer moving it, so a viewer's own move is never overridden. It lets go 0.3 s after a wrong row is handed out if the
  move has not landed, so the highlight cannot stay on a row that is not the focused one, and it never lasts longer than
  2 s.
- No animated scroll runs for this case any more. The guide is placed on the live row with no animation when the channel
  changes (it is covered then), when it comes back, and when it first appears. Before, the first appearance scrolled to
  the row 0.1 s later with a 0.2 s animation, and the return scrolled 0.3 s later. The viewer's own moves still scroll
  with the 0.2 s animation.
- A press on a row is ignored while the highlight is held on the live row and the row pressed is another one
  (`GuideReturnFocus.rowActs`), so a Select in the moment between tvOS handing focus to the old row and the move to the
  live row cannot tune a channel other than the one the viewer sees highlighted. Play/Pause is untouched: it full-screens
  the playing channel from any row.
- A debug-only log and probe (`GuideJumpProbe`): `[GuideJump]` lines with the time in milliseconds from the moment the
  guide came back, for the row tvOS focused, the row the guide drew highlighted and the list's scroll offset. A release
  build has an empty stand-in and logs and keeps nothing. With `-uiTestGuideJumpProbe` a UI test can read the same
  sequence.

**Measured** on the simulator (Apple TV 4K, 3rd generation), from the moment the guide came back:

| | row drawn highlighted before | row drawn highlighted now | tvOS focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| back from full screen, channel changed 4 to 6 | none, then channel 4 at 540 ms, then 6 at 553 ms | channel 6 at 2.6 ms | channel 4 at 552 ms, channel 6 at 558 ms |
| first appearance, playing channel 4 | none, then channel 1, then 4 | channel 4 at 7.6 ms | channel 1 at 59 ms, channel 4 at 90 ms |
| first appearance, invite above channel 1 | none, then the invite, then 1 | channel 1 at 7.9 ms | the invite at 79 ms, channel 1 at 106 ms |

The first frames after Menu show CH 06 highlighted and in view while the cover is still going away.

**The old row far from the live one.** tvOS scrolls a list to show the row it focuses, and the guide's own placement
does not stop that. So the far case was measured: channel 1 playing, one press down in full screen wraps to channel 20, and
the reverse, 19 rows apart. tvOS handed focus to the far row at about 552 ms and the guide moved it to the live row 6 to
11 ms later, and the list's scroll offset did not change at all after the guide came back (1158 pt before and after going
down to channel 20, 0 pt before and after going up to channel 1). The guide's placement on the live row runs in the same
pass as the handout, which probably undoes a focus scroll within the frame; the probe cannot confirm that mechanism, only
that the offset did not change. That is a simulator measurement; the offset changes on a TV are in the `[GuideJump]` lines
as `scroll offset a -> b`.

**Not measured.** The two limits (0.3 s for the move to the live row once a wrong row is handed out, 2 s overall) are
constants with a unit test that pins their values; whether they suit a TV is not measured. The build was tried on the
living room Apple TV 4K by hand and looked right; its `[GuideJump]` timings are not read here.

**Test.** `GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests` (UI, demo mode, storage isolated) now reads the probe and fails if the guide drew
any row but the live channel, in all three cases (back from full screen, the playing channel not the first, an invite above
channel 1), and has two far cases that fail if the list scrolls after the guide comes back (channel 1 to 20 and 20 to 1).
The probe exists only from this change on, so the commit before it cannot run these tests as they are; with the probe added
to the previous behaviour, the three first cases failed with "the guide drew [9004, 9006] highlighted, not only the live
channel 9006" and its two siblings, and they pass now. `GuideReturnFocusTests` gained 12 cases for the highlight rule, what
ends the hold, its generation counter, its limits and which presses act. On this head, on the simulator:
`GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests` 5 of 5, `GuideReturnFocusTests` 20 of 20, `ChannelGuideWrapFocusTests` 9 of 9 (the guide's
focus handler, which this change edits), `NowPlayingPanelFocusTests` 3 of 3, `OpenOnLastChannelLaunchTests` 2 of 2,
`SettingsOpenOnLastChannelTests` 1 of 1, and the whole of `NostalgexTests`: 1,201 passed, 0 failed, 29 skipped (the
live-server harnesses). Two of those UI classes, `ChannelGuideWrapFocusTests` and `NowPlayingPanelFocusTests`, run without a
harness root and are for the simulator only; `OpenOnLastChannelLaunchTests`, `SettingsOpenOnLastChannelTests` and
`GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests` set their own.

**Half-done.** On `appletv/guide-focus-no-jump`, off the 1.0.31 bundle branch (f2fda75d), not pushed, no build cut. Tried by
hand on the living room Apple TV 4K, where it looked right; its `[GuideJump]` timings are not read here, and the numbers above
are a simulator's. Left alone: the package panel and the rows changing behind an open guide.

## 2026-11-09 (Apple TV: OPEN ON LAST CHANNEL is on by default)

**Why.** The setting was written to be off until someone turned it on. The decision is the other way: a viewer who has not
touched it gets it, and turns it off in PLAYBACK & PICTURE if they would rather start on channel 1. It will feel different
at first for someone who updates, and that was accepted.

**Changed.** `LaunchChannelMemory.enabledByDefault` is `true`, the only line in the app that changed behaviour; the rest is
comments, tests and this log. A press on the switch is stored and always wins over the default, so a viewer who turns it
off stays off. The row's title and line ("Open on last channel", "Start on the channel you were last watching") read the
same with the setting on, so they are unchanged. Demo mode still hides the row, saves nothing and starts on its own start
channel (`DemoData.startChannel(in:)` first, then the first channel): the memory does not apply there.

**What a viewer who updates sees.** The channel is saved on every tune the viewer makes (the guide, next and previous, the
mini strip), whether the switch is on or off, and not on a tune the app makes itself. Nothing was saved by any build before
this one, so the first launch after the update opens channel 1, as it always did. From the first channel the viewer tunes,
the next launch opens that channel. A viewer who never tunes keeps opening on channel 1. A saved channel that is gone, or whose
name changed, opens channel 1.

**Test.** `LaunchChannelMemoryTests`: the default is pinned `true`; nothing saved is channel 1; a tune is what the next launch
opens, with the switch never pressed and nothing written to it; a viewer who turned it off opens channel 1; entering demo mode
with a real memory saved still starts on the demo's own first channel. `SettingsOpenOnLastChannelTests` reads the row On in
a fresh storage root, switches it off and back. `OpenOnLastChannelLaunchTests` no longer presses the switch: it reads it as
On, tunes channel 5, relaunches on 5, then turns it off and relaunches on channel 1.

**Measured.** On this head, on the tvOS simulator (Apple TV 4K, 3rd generation): `NostalgexTests` 1,186 passed, 0 failed,
29 skipped (the live-server harnesses). UI: `OpenOnLastChannelLaunchTests` 2 of 2, `GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests` 3 of 3
and `SettingsOpenOnLastChannelTests` 1 of 1.

**Half-done.** On `appletv/1.0.31-bundle`, not on main, not pushed, no build cut. Not run on a TV with the default on. With
it on, opening on a channel other than 1 is the common case, so the guide's first focus on the playing channel (the I-041
commits in this bundle) now applies to every viewer, not only to those who turned the setting on. The web tuner's switch is
still off by default in this branch (its Settings row, `docs/WEB-TUNER-FEATURES.md` and the 2026-11-08 web entry below say so),
and the Roku has no such setting. The hidden Jellyfin libraries switch is unchanged and stays off by default.

## 2026-11-09 (Roku: RETRO MODE no longer draws the tracking line)

**Why.** Chad's decision, from viewer feedback: the white tracking (drift) line that rolled through the picture in
RETRO MODE is very distracting, and it goes on every platform. Scanlines, vignette and flicker stay. The Apple TV and
the web tuner have already dropped it (parity queue item 42).

**Changed.** `GuideView.brs` loses the glitch timer, its scheduling and `m.crtHeight` (only the glitch used it);

## 2026-11-09 (web tuner and Docker 1.0.16: OPEN ON LAST CHANNEL is on by default)

**Shipped.** Web tuner and Docker 1.0.16 (`tunerVersion` 1.0.16, tag `tuner-v1.0.16`), with the Retro mode entry above. The
hosted tuner on nostalgex.app changes when main is pushed; the Docker image is built from the tag.

**Why.** The setting shipped off in 1.0.15. The product decision of 2026-11-09 is that it is on, the same on every surface
(the Apple TV's `LaunchChannelMemory.enabledByDefault` is flipped on its own branch; the Roku port is a separate item).

**Changed.** `OPEN_DEFAULT = true` in `scripts/nostalgex-last-channel.js`, and `isOn(stored)` now answers the default only when
nothing is stored; a stored value reads as before (`'1'` on, anything else off). The Settings button's static markup reads ON
(`updateOpenLastChannelControls` still sets it from storage on every load). Storage the page cannot read reads as the
default, so the button and the next start agree.

Why an existing choice survives: the button always writes `'0'` or `'1'` and never removes the key, so a browser that switched
it off on 1.0.15 holds `'0'` and stays off, one that switched it on holds `'1'` and stays on. Only a browser that never pressed
the button (no value) takes the new default. Opening on the remembered channel never writes the switch, so the default stays a
default. A viewer with nothing remembered, or a remembered channel that was renamed, renumbered or dropped, still gets the first
enabled channel. One thing to expect: 1.0.15 remembered the viewer's tunes whether the switch was on or off, so a browser that
never chose already holds a channel and its first visit after the update opens on it.

**Checked.** `npm run test:last-channel` (16 checks) and `npm run test:open-last-channel:browser` (61 checks, headless, a stub
Jellyfin): the row reads ON on a new install and a click stores `'0'`, which survives a reload; stored `'0'` with a remembered
channel opens the first channel; stored `'1'` and never-chose open the remembered one; every mismatch falls back to the first
channel; signing out clears the channel and leaves the switch as it was; the button works by mouse at 960x540 and 390x844.
Negative control: the same smoke served 1.0.15's page and engine fails 17 checks, all of them default-on checks, and none of the
stored-choice ones. `npm test` passes, and so do the include-hidden, franchise-channels, start-over and watershed browser
smokes (the ones that tune or reload).

Found on the way, fixed in its own commit: `scripts/watershed-browser-smoke.mjs` read the Apple TV's `AppState.swift` for
`UserDefaults.standard` and had been failing on main since the app moved to `AppDefaults`; it now accepts either. A test-file
change only, not part of `npm test`.

**Half-done.** Nothing on the web side. The hosted default changes for every hosted viewer who never chose, on the push; a
Docker container changes when it pulls 1.0.16. Not measured on a real TV browser.

**Next.** The Roku port defaults on too (parity item 40); the Android issue for the setting should say on by default.

## 2026-11-08 (Apple TV: Jellyfin libraries hidden from the home screen are listed, off until switched on)

**Why.** Jellyfin's `GET /UserViews` has an `includeHidden` parameter that defaults to false. With it false,
`UserViewManager.GetUserViews` drops every library in the user's `MyMediaExcludes` (the "Display on home screen" box in
Home settings), and the scan reads only the libraries the list names, so a library hidden on the server was never listed
or scanned. The web agent measured it on a lab Jellyfin 10.11.11 (a user who hides two libraries and has no access to a
third): the plain list names 3 libraries and `includeHidden=true` names 5, the third in neither; an admin gets 6 both ways;
asking the library without access directly answers 401. The same code is in 12.x by a read of the release tags. A user hides
a library on purpose (adult content, test or plugin folders), so these must not start airing on channels by surprise.

**Changed.**
- `JellyfinAPIService.loadSections` makes two requests: the plain `/UserViews?userId=` it always made, then the same with
  `includeHidden=true`. A library only in the second is hidden (`PlexSection.hidden`, `LibrarySectionRef.isHidden`). If the
  second request fails the answer is the plain list, as before.
- A hidden library is listed in the onboarding picker and in Settings under LIBRARIES, marked HIDDEN ON JELLYFIN, and OFF
  until the viewer switches it on. `LibrarySectionSelectionStore.hiddenSectionsOnByDefault` (false) is the one constant;
  true makes a hidden library follow the same opt-out as every other. The viewer's choice is its own set
  (`includedHiddenLibrarySectionKeys`), and the Jellyfin scan leaves a hidden library out unless it is in that set, so a
  library hidden after the app last listed them stays out too.
- The collection sweep leaves out the same sections the scan does (`sectionKeysLeftOutOfScan`), so it asks a hidden library
  nothing until it is switched on. The two answers are merged, so a second one that comes back smaller cannot take a library
  off the list. The picker also shows for a hidden library alone: it starts off, so without it nothing would be scanned and
  nothing would offer it. A hidden library that simply stays off is not counted as an exclusion in the picker's analytics signal.
- No forced refresh. The toggle's existing rescan fetches a library when it is switched on. A viewer with no hidden library
  sees nothing different, and one who has some sees them listed off, with the scan reading what it read before. A first
  sign-in on a server with one library on the home screen and a hidden one now shows the picker (two sections).
- Emby's list (`/Users/{id}/Views`) is unchanged.

**Test.** `JellyfinHiddenLibrariesTests` runs the real network code against a loopback server that, like Jellyfin, lists
the hidden library only when asked: it is listed and marked, not scanned by default, scanned once switched on, scanned
when the default is on (and still switchable off), unchanged when nothing is hidden, plain list when the second request
fails, the two answers merged, and Emby sends one request with no query. `HiddenLibrarySelectionTests` covers the picker's
default, the Settings toggle and its persistence, a hidden library alone getting the picker, the analytics count, the
collection sweep, that a library that is not hidden follows the old opt-out, a new sign-in starting from the defaults, and
the default-on position. Tests set the position they test; one assertion pins the shipped default. `JellyfinLibraryGoldenTests` reads `views` from the shared file when it is there (each Jellyfin case's `includeHidden`, else
read from its path) and skips until then.

**Open.** Whether the default is off is Chad's call (one constant). Held on its own branch (`appletv/jellyfin-include-hidden`).
Not run against a Jellyfin from the Apple TV side.

## 2026-11-08 (Web tuner and Docker: an opt-in switch for libraries a Jellyfin user hides; Open on last channel; 1.0.15 prepared)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `web/jellyfin-hidden-libraries` off main `b2c6f404`, `tunerVersion` 1.0.15. Not tagged, not pushed.
Since `tuner-v1.0.14` main changed nothing the tuner, the engine or the image reads (the 1.0.30 changelog entry, a QA
script, the tvOS release script, this log, Roku and Apple TV work), so 1.0.15 is 1.0.14 plus the two items below.

**Why (hidden libraries).** A report said that libraries a Jellyfin user hides from the home screen are never scanned.
`GET /UserViews` has an `includeHidden` parameter that defaults to false, and with it false `UserViewManager.GetUserViews` drops every library in
the user's `Configuration.MyMediaExcludes`, the "Display on home screen" box in Jellyfin's Home settings. The scan reads
only the libraries the list names. The same code is in 10.11.11, 12.0, 12.2 and 12.4 (read from the release tags).
**Why a switch, off by default.** Hiding a library can be on purpose (adult, kids-unsafe, test or plugin folders), and the
web tuner and Docker have no per-library picker to switch a newly visible library off, so the first version of this branch,
which always asked, was reworked: the viewer turns it on. The Apple TV has a picker and can ask without a switch.

**Changed.**
- Settings > General > Playback has "Include libraries hidden on Jellyfin", under "Open on last channel": Jellyfin only (the
  row is hidden on Plex and Emby), per browser, off unless turned on, with one line under it. Off, Jellyfin's library list
  is `/UserViews?userId=<id>`, byte for byte what it was. On, it is `/UserViews?userId=<id>&includeHidden=true`. Pressing it
  saves the choice, drops the saved library and reads the library again once, in the background: the guide stays up, the
  channel that is playing keeps playing (a foreground read ends by tuning the first channel) and Settings stays open. Pressing
  it while that read runs does nothing.
  `INCLUDE_HIDDEN_DEFAULT` in `scripts/nostalgex-jellyfin-urls.js` (point 13) is the one place the default lives; a saved
  '1' or '0' always wins over it. No scan revision is bumped: with the default off nobody needs a forced re-read.
- The shared case is a `views` list in `scripts/jellyfin-library-golden.json`: one case per position of the switch
  (backend, user id, `includeHidden`, path). Emby has no such parameter and its path is the same in both.
- The Roku port is untouched. Off, the web loader's request is what it was, so the Roku `mediabrowser.json` vectors
  generated from this branch are byte-identical to the base's. `jellyfin-library-golden.json` in the Roku vectors is a copy
  of the shared file and did change (the `_about` note and the new `views` key); the Roku reads only `sections` and `types`
  from it.
- Emby is left alone in both positions: `/Users/{id}/Views` has no such parameter in Emby's API reference, and on 4.10.1.0
  a user with libraries in MyMediaExcludes still got every library they may open.
- `.cfg-row[hidden] { display: none; }`: the new row is hidden with the attribute, and `.cfg-row { display: flex }` beat it,
  so the row would have shown on Emby and Plex. Found by the browser smoke.
- Open on last channel (Trello I-017): a switch in Settings > General > Playback, off unless turned on, with the Apple TV's
  line under it ("Start on the channel you were last watching"). The tuner always tuned the first enabled channel after a
  load. The channel is now remembered, with its id and name, whenever the viewer tunes one (a pick in the guide, channel up or
  down, a number key) on a real server, in browser storage (per browser or container client), and opened when the switch is on
  and an enabled channel has both. Tunes the page makes itself are not remembered (the first channel after a load, the
  fallback when a package is switched off), so a saved channel that is not in the lineup yet (its package off, a collection
  channel not built) is not overwritten by the first channel. The saved channel is cleared on sign-out, as the Apple TV
  clears it on disconnect. Renamed, renumbered, dropped, package off, nothing kept or a damaged value falls back to the first
  enabled channel. The choice is `scripts/nostalgex-last-channel.js`. The Apple TV builds the same setting first; the web row's title and
  line match the Apple TV's ("Open on last channel", "Start on the channel you were last watching"). Only the place differs: the
  Apple TV puts the row after AUDIO LANGUAGE, the web puts it first in Playback.
  `web-tune-ownership-smoke` lifts `switchChannel` into a sandbox and needed a stub for the new call.

libraries (Hidden Films, Hidden TV) from My Media and has no access to a third (Private Films), through the Home settings
field `MyMediaExcludes` written by API (the web client's own page was not driven). The first three bullets were measured with
the first version of the branch (it always asked) and show the two positions; the switch itself was then driven on the real page (see Tests).
- `GET /UserViews` as the tuner always sent it: 3 libraries. With `includeHidden=true`: 5. Private Films in neither. An admin:
  6 both ways. The user asking Private Films for items directly: HTTP 401. Asking Hidden Films directly: HTTP 200, 4 rows.

  episodes), 0 from Private Films. The real page, headless, signed in as that user: library 10 titles and VHS VAULT 6
  without, 17 and 10 with, no page errors.
- A playlist the user owns still stays out (6 views listed with the parameter, 17 titles).
- Emby 4.10.1.0 in a container: with `MyMediaExcludes` set through the API, `/Users/{id}/Views` listed all three libraries
  the user may open with and without `IncludeHidden=true`; the library without access was not listed.

**Review fixes (after the reviewer's pass).** No reporter's library sizes are quoted anywhere in the repo. Pressing the switch now reads in the background, so a viewer on a channel other than the first is
not retuned to channel 1 and Settings stays open (`include-hidden-browser-smoke` toggles from a non-first channel and fails

yet is not overwritten by the first channel, sign-out clears it (`open-last-channel-browser-smoke`, which fails against the
earlier page on all of these). The row says the Apple TV's one line.

- `npm test` exits 0, leak guard clean (urls smoke 96, library smoke 48, last-channel 14, tuner version 59, readme and changelog checks).
- `npm run build` and `npm run build:selfhost` pass, and so do `test:tuner-version:builds` and `test:tuner-isolation:builds`.
  `dist-selfhost` carries the new script, the row and `INCLUDE_HIDDEN_DEFAULT = false`; the image has no copy of its own.

- The switch pressed with a mouse on the real page (hosted pages and the Docker build's `dist-selfhost`, both at 960x540)

## 2026-11-08 (Apple TV: the guide follows a channel change made in full screen, I-041)

**Why.** Change channel in full screen (next channel with Right), press Menu, and the guide came back with its
selection on the row the viewer had left from while the live bolt sat on the channel now playing (Trello I-041, first
reported in June). Reproduced on main on a simulator in demo mode: focus on channel 4, Select, Select, Right, Right,
Menu. The info panel read CH 04 with channel 6 playing. The app log showed focus go from the old row to none on
entering full screen and from none back to the OLD row on leaving, with the live channel never assigned.

**Approach.**
- What is set: the focus ring goes to the live channel, as `anchorFocusToLiveChannel` already did when full screen closes.
- When: once more, the moment tvOS hands focus back to the guide, i.e. `focusedChannelID` changing from none to a row
  while the handout window is open. Closing full screen opens it; the handout, or 2 seconds, closes it. Each opening
  has its own generation number and its timer only closes the opening it belongs to, so the timer of an earlier close
  of full screen cannot shut a later window early (`GuideReturnFocus.HandoutWindow`).
- Why it survives: a request made while nothing in the guide has focus does not stick, and tvOS then restores the row it
  remembers. Acting on the handout puts our request after the engine's, not before it, and a viewer's own move is never
  "from none", so it is left alone.
- Where: `ChannelGuideView` (the window, three small hunks) and the pure rule and window in `GuideReturnFocus`.
- Second commit, same flag and rule, set when the guide first appears: with the playing channel not the first, or a
  seasonal invite above channel 1, tvOS gave first focus to the first row or the invite instead. Measured on a simulator in
  demo mode (`-uiTestStartOnChannel 4`, `-uiTestSeasonalInvite`): focus on channel 1, or on the invite, for the 5 seconds
  watched. On the basement Apple TV 4K (tvOS 27.2) both cases already land on the playing channel without this commit, so it
  protects the simulator and any tvOS that behaves that way; not measured on another tvOS version.
- The early return skips one `onFocusChanged` call, the one for the row tvOS handed focus to. Measured on a simulator with
  timestamps: the call for the live channel follows 8 ms later after full screen, and 31 to 34 ms later when the guide first
  appears, with or without the invite. The info panel goes from empty to the live channel and never shows the wrong row.
  One case it did break, found by that measurement: when the playing channel has no row in the guide (its package was
  switched off while it played), the anchor pointed at a row that is not there, the ring stayed on channel 1 and the info
  panel stayed empty. The handout is now only acted on when the playing channel has a row (`GuideReturnFocus.liveRowID`).
- Not touched: the packages panel and the rows changing behind an open guide.

**Test.** `GuideFocusAfterFullScreenTests` (UI, demo mode, storage isolated) has three cases (a channel changed in full screen then back, the playing channel not the first, a seasonal invite above channel 1); the first fails on main with "the
guide came back on CH 04, not the live channel 6", and passes with the change. `GuideReturnFocusTests` (8) covers the rule and the window, including a timer from an earlier opening firing while a later one is open.
The return-from-full-screen case fails without the first commit and passes with it on a simulator and on a real Apple TV
4K (3rd generation, tvOS 27.2). The two first-appearance cases fail without the second commit on the simulator and pass on
the TV either way. TV runs use isolated app storage, so nothing the TV holds was touched.

## 2026-11-08 (Roku: enrichment fields on a title read back from the saved library)

**Why.** On a TV `FormatJson` writes keys in lower case and `ParseJson` gives case-sensitive AAs, so a title read
back from the saved library (`source/plex/LibrarySnapshot.brs`) holds `imdbrating`, not `imdbRating`. `NxEnriched`
read by the camelCase name with a bracket, so it missed, and a `ratingMin` channel lost the OMDb fallback on a
launch from the save: #216's TV run had 132 of 142 channels' pools the same after the round trip.

**Changed.** `NxEnriched` (`source/filter/ChannelFilter.brs`) looks a camelCase key up by its lower-case spelling
too, in the record and on the item; the record still comes first. 11 cases in the new `tests/FilterCaseTests.brs`:
a hand-made lower-case copy of `MultiServerFilterTests`' fixture, which is how the TV holds it, differed in 10
channels without the fix, all `ratingMin` ones.

**Pressed** with `deploy.sh --test` on the 55R617 (OS 15.3.4), main with this, #216 and #220 merged: the suite
passed, the round trip through `FormatJson` and `ParseJson` included, and the TV printed `{"imdbrating":1}` for
`FormatJson({ imdbRating: 1 })`.

**Open.** A real library through `loadLibrary` and a relaunch from its save on a TV: our sideloads run with
enrichment off.

## 2026-11-07 (Roku: the filter's cache is dropped under both spellings, #215)

**Why.** #215: `NxFilterItem` sets its cache as `item.nxFilter`, and in an item read back with `ParseJson`, a
case-sensitive AA on a TV, that key is `nxfilter`, so `Delete("nxFilter")` left it. Three of the four deletes only
freed memory. The fourth, in `NxEnrichAttach`, is what lets a title the remote enrichment step fills in be filtered
with its record on the rebuild; when it missed, the rebuild read the view from before the record arrived.

**Changed.** `NxFilterForget` (`source/filter/ChannelFilter.brs`) deletes both spellings and `NxFilterHeld` checks
both. They replace the deletes in `NxFilterPoolsByServer`, `loadLibrary`, `rebuildForBundles`, `NxEnrichAttach` and
the coverage count, and the delete and the leak check in `MultiServerFilterTests.brs`, whose `DoesExist("nxFilter")`
would also have missed the lower-case key on a TV. New cases there: the fixture read back with `ParseJson` leaves no
cache after `NxFilterPoolsByServer`; `NxFilterForget` clears a `ParseJson` item and a literal one; and a `ParseJson`
title that SPY GAMES misses is taken by keyword once `NxEnrichAttach` gives it its record. The suite prints, as
information, whether `Delete("nxFilter")` leaves the cache on that runtime.

**Pressed** with `deploy.sh --test` on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4), build `7e86c5f`: the print read `true` on the TV
(`false` in the off-TV interpreter; the old fixture's literal items aren't case-sensitive anywhere), and every case kept
in the pull request passed there. That build had one more case, comparing the
`ParseJson` fixture's pools with the original's; it failed on the TV (132 of 142 channels the same) for a separate
reason, so the next commit takes it out: on a TV the keys `FormatJson` writes are lower case, and `NxEnriched` reads
`imdbRating` and other camelCase fields by their mixed-case name. The TV printed only the count; off the TV, lower-cased
case-sensitive copies of the fixture differ in 10 channels too, all `ratingMin`.

**Open.** The camelCase reads, as their own issue. A real title through `loadLibrary` and the remote step on a TV:
our sideloads run with enrichment off (no relay or Supabase keys).

## 2026-11-07 (Apple TV: RESCAN LIBRARY shows every line of its counts)

**Why.** A Jellyfin report of a library coming up short asked for the "X OF Y ON CHANNELS" line under RESCAN LIBRARY
in SERVERS & ACCOUNTS to be read back, and the row showed only two lines, the second ending in an ellipsis.
`SettingsToggleRow` cut every subtitle at two lines, and that row's subtitle is the library summary, the coverage
line, "Last updated ...", and the last playback failure, one per line. In the Settings pane the summary alone (98
characters for a library of 444 movies and 3,639 episodes from 55 shows) wraps onto a second line, so the coverage
line was the third and was never drawn. "Last updated" and the playback failure line were cut the same way.

**Changed.** `SettingsToggleRow` takes `subtitleLineLimit`, default 2, so every other row is as it was. RESCAN
LIBRARY passes nil and shows everything it is given. Reproduced before the fix on the tvOS simulator at 1920 x 1080
with a test library of that size: two lines ending "matched to TMDB...". After: every line shows, the row sits above
SYNC WITH MY OTHER APPLE TVS with nothing clipped, and focus and scrolling through SYNC and DISCONNECT and back land
where they did.

**Test.** `SettingsRescanRowTests` (UI target) opens the page with the real focus engine and a fixture library
(`-uiTestForceSettingsPage -uiTestRescanRowFixture plain|split`), reads the screen back with text recognition and
asserts the summary, the coverage line, "Last updated" and, in the split case, the split-by-kind, skipped and
playback failure lines are on screen. Both cases fail on the old code (the coverage line is missing) and pass on the
new. A teardown relaunches with `clear` so the fake last-load time and playback verdict do not stay in the
simulator's defaults. No unit test: this is layout, and the wording of the line is already covered in
`LibraryCoverageTests`.

**Not changed.** Other rows keep the two-line limit. Checked every Settings subtitle by length, and on screen for the
longest on PLAYBACK & PICTURE: MARK WATCHED (132 characters) fits in two full lines on a Plex server; the next longest
is 109. Nothing else is built with a line break.

looked at on an Apple TV.

**Why.** Chad's review of #211: a saved guide made with the WATERSHED switch the other way was shown at launch as it

switch in Settings reschedules the running app but leaves the file as it was.

tomorrow schedule after it) schedules with the switch off: both call `setLineup` first, which sets the switch from
the registry, so those schedules are held. The TV runs below agree.

first 22 channels of the guide over the about two hours the grid shows, matched against each server's ratings as read
on 11-05 (1 to 4 titles a read unmatched by name). A read runs about 70 s, past the full load behind the launch; on each
relaunch that load kept the launch guide's schedules.
- Lab Jellyfin, `nxtest` (5,492 titles): switch off, guide saved. Switch on, relaunch: the saved guide was skipped,
  the saved pools were scheduled and shown in 4.5 s, 0 of 79 titles on screen R, NC-17 or TV-MA, and the full load
  kept those schedules ("its schedules stand", which compares the switch). Relaunch with it on: the saved guide
  showed in 1.3 s, 0 of 79. Switch off, relaunch: pools again, and 11 of 81 held-rated titles back on screen.
- Lab Emby, `nxtest` (5,578 titles, main's `Fields` from #204): switch off, 10 of 79 held-rated titles on screen.
  Switch on, relaunch: the saved pools were shown in 3.5 s, 0 of 78.

**Open.** As before: the real 9 PM and midnight, a launch deep link onto a held channel, the golden suite through
`deploy.sh --test`, a Plex sign-in, a stick, the channels past the first 22, and the first launch after an update onto
a guide the old build saved (the cases only). The power-loss seed's key has no switch either; closing Settings
runs the re-check at once, which saves it again, so only a power loss with Settings still open would play a seed from

## 2026-11-05 (Apple TV: Jellyfin and Emby playlists, music and collections stay out of the guide, #205 #206)

**Why.** A Jellyfin Playlists view answers any items request with its playlists (`PlaylistsFolder` overwrites
`IncludeItemTypes`), and the scan treated every view that was not TV or Music Videos as a film library, so each
playlist became a film. A playlist has no year and the year rule lets that through: a 33 minute workout mix aired on
VHS VAULT, DVD SHELF and FLICKS on the web tuner. The Apple TV had the same hole (read, then reproduced on a loopback

## 2026-11-05 (Apple TV: RESCAN LIBRARY says how many titles are on a channel, on none, and skipped)

**Why.** A user's Jellyfin library showed 484 titles for a library they put at about 600, and nothing in the app said
where the rest went. Two answers were missing: how many titles the scan threw away for having no runtime, and how many
of the ones it kept never land on any channel. Chad approved both numbers, with the second defined as titles in the
pool of a channel that would show if its package were on, whether or not the package is on.

**Changed.** The line under the library summary in Settings > Servers > RESCAN LIBRARY, in the same style:
`11,633 OF 11,809 ON CHANNELS · 176 ON NO CHANNEL (4 MOVIES, 172 EPISODES) · 12 SKIPPED (NO RUNTIME)`. A part is left
out at zero, the split in brackets shows only when more than one kind has titles on no channel, and the first two wait
until counted.
- Skipped: the six runtime guards (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, movie and episode each) count what they drop through a
  `ScanSkipCounter` on the backend. A Plex section read that falls back from the bulk read to the per-show read rewinds
  the counter to where the bulk read began, so a title is counted once. The number is saved with the library snapshot
  (`skippedNoRuntime`, optional, so an older snapshot reads as none) and reset on disconnect.
- On a channel: `LibraryDiagnostics.coverage` runs every channel in channels.json through the same `filterItems` the
  guide uses, keeps those whose pool reaches `minItems`, and adds the built collection and franchise pools. It cannot be
  read off `allChannels`: the first load builds every channel, every later load (RESCAN, the six-hour refresh) builds
  the enabled packages only. So it runs on demand when Settings > Servers opens, off the main actor, once per library
  (keyed on item count, load time, enrichment count, channel set), and not at all above 30,000 titles.
- The count for the channels in the guide as it is now is kept beside it (`titlesOnChannelsCount`, debounced on
  `channels`), for the log and for contrast. It moves when a package is toggled; the all-packages number does not.
- One log line, `COVERAGE: ...`, with the counts and the first 25 titles on no channel (year, certificate, rating,
  genres, studio, runtime, TMDB or not). The titles go to the console only; the device log gets the counts.

**Checked.** Tests: a fake server per backend with zero, short and just-long-enough runtimes (movies and episodes)
proves the skipped count, once-only on the Plex fallback and across a relaunch; a lineup test proves the on-channels
number ignores a package toggle while the in-guide number follows it. The full suite: 1,118 tests, 1,091 passed, 0 failed, 27 skipped (the opt-in harnesses), 14 of them new.
`scripts/qa/library-coverage.mjs` runs the web tuner's copy of the filter over the same items and compares per kind and
per channel. On a library the size of Chad's (1,792 movies, 8,891 episodes, 1,126 music videos, synthetic, cold
enrichment) episodes and music videos agree exactly, and movies differ by 6 titles, all on the four channels with a
`productionCompanies` rule: the web filter matches the Plex studio when a title has no enrichment record, the Apple TV
needs the record (`nostalgex-channel-filter.cjs:698-709`, on purpose). The count took 16 to 19 seconds in a Debug build
on the simulator on a busy Mac. Not measured on a TV, and not on Chad's real library.

**Open.** The cost on a real Apple TV (the 4K 1st gen and the HD are the slow ones); a Release-build figure; Chad's own
numbers from his library. A list screen for the titles on no channel was not built (cost given to Chad first).
Roku and Android ports are drafted in `projects/nostalgex-internal/docs/issue-drafts/` and not filed.

**Next.** Chad's call on whether to carry per-kind figures on screen, and on the list screen.

## 2026-11-05 (Apple TV: the Emby scan asks for OfficialRating and CommunityRating, #204)

**Why.** tydude001 measured it on Emby 4.10.1.0: an Items answer carries neither `OfficialRating` nor `CommunityRating`
unless `Fields` names them (0 of 200 with the apps' list, 195 and 197 of 200 with them added). Jellyfin 12.2 sends both
either way. The scan never named them, so on Emby every title read as unrated: SAT MORNING CARTOONS (allows unrated)
aired South Park and Family Guy, VHS VAULT's 9 PM hold held nothing, WATERSHED held nothing, and the 13 `ratingMin`
channels saw no star rating. The old comment at `AppState+Channels.swift` blamed the server ("CommunityRating came back
null for 100% of a 500-title sample"); it was the request.

**Changed.**
- One list, `JellyfinAPIService.scanFields`, now ends `...,UserData,OfficialRating,CommunityRating` and both services
  use it. Every title read goes through `fetchAllItems` (sections, series, each show's episodes, collection members), so
  this is the only request that changed. Collections ask `Fields=ChildCount` for BoxSets and need nothing. Episodes take
  the show's certificate and score (`show.OfficialRating ?? ep.OfficialRating`, `show.CommunityRating`), so the series
  request is the one that matters for TV.
- Jellyfin gets the names too, one shared list. Jellyfin's `ItemFields` has no `OfficialRating` or `CommunityRating`
  value, and the scan has always sent `UserData`, which it does not have either, so unknown names are already tolerated;
  tydude's run on 12.2.0 with the field added read the same 196 of 200. Not measured on an older Jellyfin.
- A library saved before this has no ratings on any Emby title, and `shouldSkipRefresh` holds a rescan for up to 24 hours
  while the server says nothing changed. The snapshot now carries `scanFieldsVersion` (optional, so an older file reads as
  none); on Emby a restore of one older than 1 is marked stale and loses its signature, so the background refresh that
  already runs after a stale restore scans. The guide comes up from the snapshot first, as it does now. Jellyfin and Plex
  are untouched. `libraryScanFieldsVersion` tracks what is in memory, so a save before the refresh finishes does not stamp
  old items as new.
- The `ratingMin` comment now says what happened. The OMDb fallback stays: it is an alternative to the native rating
  (`nativeOk || omdbOk`), so a native rating can only add titles, and titles the server gives no score (3 of 200 on tydude's
  Emby) and Plex titles with none still need it.

**Checked.** `EmbyRatingFieldsTests` (10) runs the real Emby and Jellyfin scan against a loopback server that answers as
Emby 4.10 does (a rating is in an item only when `Fields` names it), then the app's own stock pool build. Fails on the old
request (7 of 10: TV-MA on SAT MORNING CARTOONS, R titles in VHS VAULT at 3 PM, certificates and scores unread, WATERSHED
and ratingMin channels empty), passes on the new one. Full suite: 1,113 tests, 1,087 passed, 0 failed, 26 skipped.

**Effect on what an existing Emby user sees,** measured on a synthetic library (400 films, 25 shows, certificates and
scores spread like a real one, cold enrichment) read with the fields withheld and then asked for:
- the 12 `ratingMin` channels that the test library can fill go from 0 titles (no OMDb data) to 15 to 81 each; with OMDb
  data in, the fallback was already filling some, and the result can only be larger than before;
- SAT MORNING CARTOONS, AFTER SCHOOL TV, 80S AFTER SCHOOL TV, RETRO TOONS, Y2K TOONS, FAMILY HOUR, FAMILY TV and ANIMATION
  lose their TV-14, TV-MA, R and unrated-adult titles: 42 to 0, 56 to 28, 42 to 14, 21 to 5, 14 to 0, 75 to 46, 14 to 0,
  32 to 25. A kids channel with too few real kids' shows falls under its minimum and leaves the guide (SAT MORNING CARTOONS,
  FAMILY TV, Y2K TOONS here);
- R RATED COMEDY goes from 0 to 18: its rating list has no "allow unrated", so it was empty on Emby until now.
  21 of 142 channels moved. The numbers are the shape of the change, not a prediction for a library.
Not run against a real Emby from here (the lab servers on this Mac were not up); the fake follows tydude's measurements.

**Open.** The web tuner (`plex-tuner.html:9576`), the Roku (`roku/source/mediabrowser/MediaBrowserLibrary.brs:42`) and the
Android app (`MediaBrowserLibrary.kt:200` on owen's branch) send the same list; `scripts/nostalgex-emby-dolby-vision-smoke.mjs:257`
pins it. Not changed here.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: issue #146 second round, STOP WAITING on the first-run path, and what a big first load costs in memory)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/first-load-memory` off main `5d880dd9`, for 1.0.30.

**Why.** After 1.0.29 the reporter still reaches the Apple TV home screen: Plex 1.43.5, a remote server, a 105k-movie
library that stalls, a 1k library that crashes too, stuck in onboarding. Later: every server worked when added on its
own, "adding them all sequentially, during onboarding" may hit a memory limit.

**Looked for a crash log first.** App Store Connect has none: 0 TestFlight crash submissions, no hang or launch
diagnostics for 1.0.29 (53) or 52. Production crashes are Xcode Organizer only, not in the API.

**Not reproduced (simulator).** `StopWaitingFirstRunHarnessTests` drives the first run the way the app takes it
(`confirmServerSelection`, the section list, `confirmLibrarySelection`, then the scan) with `RootView` mounted, against
a fake remote Plex whose sections never answer, stall mid-body, trickle, or drop the connection (the retry ladder runs),
with and without the slow-link page size, 1k to 105k movies, one or two servers, STOP WAITING pressed in onboarding, right
after confirming, at random moments, on a faulted section, whenever the scan sits still, repeatedly while the guide is
built, and from the real button after a minute of quiet. 96 iterations plus the four-server runs below: no crash, no
crash report. The simulator does not kill an app for memory, which is the one thing it cannot show.

**The three 105k "hangs" were a slow build, not a stuck press.** The same iteration run alone with a 25-minute limit
finished in 229 s (105,500 items, the channel build at about 0.7 channels a second). The 85 s limit was the bug.

**The eight error-screen loads in the first 40-iteration run.** Five are the designed ending: nothing had come back
before the press, so "Stopped waiting. Nothing had come back from your server". Three are different (iterations 2, 26,
27): a connection dropped mid-section (`reset`), the retry ladder ran out, and the whole server's scan was thrown away,
four finished sections included, with "Can't reach the server address saved on this device. Open Settings and reconnect
while on the same network as your server." Only a cancellation keeps partial results (PlexAPIService.swift, the catch in
`loadLibrary`); a transport error after the retries drops everything read so far, and the message tells a remote
viewer to move to their own network. Not changed here. Not the crash.

**Memory, the reporter's second message.** `testMultiServerOnboardingMemory`: four servers (105k, 50k, 10k, 10k movies)
in one onboarding, a realistic library (titles, genres and studios the channel rules match), process footprint sampled
every 0.25 s. Scanning does not accumulate: peaks 508, 535, 557, 571 MB, growing only by the items (the baseline of 296 MB
is the test's own fixture). The channel build is where it goes: peak 1,282 MB, about 986 MB above baseline, 337 s.
Inside it: the music-cache step makes a second full copy of every item (+99 MB) that the local `merged` in `loadLibrary`
then keeps alive to the end of the load; the filter cache copies every item again (+172 MB); and the pools hold whole
592-byte items by value: 91 channels, 573,333 items in 800,305 slots (451 MB allocated, 323 MB used), while the guide
shows 13 channels with 77,270 pooled items, so about 87% of the pooled items belong to channels nobody is watching.
`compactMap` grows its result in steps (1,328, 5,313, 21,254, 85,019 slots for items this size), so a pool just past a
step carries up to four times what it uses. A single 105k server on the plainer fixture peaked at 589 MB. Where the
tvOS limit sits for each model is not something the simulator or any file here tells; the TV's own
`os_proc_available_memory()` does, and the cold harness already logs it.

**Changed.**
- `loadLibrary` drops `merged` after its last use, so the pre-music-cache list is freed when `applyMusicCacheToLibrary`
  replaces it (the music-cache step: 596 MB after, 694 MB before).
- `AppState.trimmed`: `filterItems` hands back a pool with no more slots than it needs (within an eighth); one exact-fit
  copy per pool that has more.
- Same four-server run after: peak 1,164 MB (-118 MB), pools 588,320 slots / 332 MB allocated (-119 MB), load end 981 MB
  (-104 MB). What is held once the load has settled barely moves (966 MB vs 977 MB): freed pages stay in the process.
- `FirstLoadMemoryTests` (2): a 5,400-item pool had 10,627 slots on main; it fails there and passes now.
- `StopWaitingFirstRunHarnessTests` (opt-in, 2 tests): the soak and the memory run.
- NostalgexTests: 1,107 tests, 1,079 passed, 0 failed, 28 skipped (the two new opt-in tests).

**Not shown.** That memory is what takes the reporter's app down. It fits (the sum of their servers, a kill on STOP
WAITING because that is when the build starts, individual servers fine) and is not proven: no crash log, no device
run, model unknown. The cut here is about 10% of the peak; it does not change the order of magnitude. The bigger ones:
build and keep pools only for channels in enabled bundles, and pools that hold indexes instead of items. Both touch what
the schedule and the guide read, so they are a decision, not a drive-by.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: a section that fails for good no longer takes the scan with it; Jellyfin and Emby too)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/scan-keeps-sections` off main `9e2c945d`, for 1.0.30 (issue #146 follow-up, Trello N-039).

**Why.** Found while measuring #146: a fake remote Plex that dropped the connection in the fifth of five sections
threw away the whole server's scan once the retries ran out (0 items, four finished sections included), and the viewer
read "Can't reach the server address saved on this device. Open Settings and reconnect while on the same network as
your server", for a server that was not on their network. Only a cancel kept the sections already read. Jellyfin and
Emby had the identical catch, so N-039 (one erroring section fails the whole scan) is the same rule in two more files.

**Changed.**
- A section whose requests fail for good (a transport error after the retries, or an HTTP error status) is skipped; the
  scan goes on with the next section and ends by handing back what it read as a `LibraryScanInterrupted` that names
  the lost sections. One shared helper, `SectionFailures`, used by the Plex, Jellyfin and Emby loops. A cancel still
  keeps its pages; a 401/403 or an unexpected payload still ends the scan; a scan that read nothing at all is still a
  failure, with the original error.
- `loadLibrary` builds the guide from what was read, marks the library stale (a later refresh fills the section in),
  and names the lost sections in `lostSectionsLastLoad` and the install log: "server 'X' lost section(s) Documentaries,
  kept 450 items from the others". A background refresh that loses a section is still thrown away, as an abandoned one
  is. The "abandoned by the viewer" analytics flag no longer counts a lost section as the viewer's doing.
- The message follows the address: `PlexAPIService.isLikelyLocalAddress` (private ranges, `.local`, a plex.direct name
  that encodes a LAN address) keeps the "same network" advice. A remote or unknown address reads "The connection to
  your server dropped while the library was loading. Check that the server is online, then Retry." or "Can't reach
  your server from here. Check that it is online and that remote access is turned on, then Retry."
- `SectionFailureScanTests` (6): a fake server that drops one of three sections; Plex, Jellyfin and Emby each fail on
  main with the connection error and keep the other 450 movies now; every section failing is still a failure; the
  load through `AppState` builds a guide with no error and names the section; the three message cases.
- NostalgexTests: 1,109 tests, 1,083 passed, 0 failed, 26 skipped.

**Not changed.** Roku, the web tuner and Android. Roku's Plex scan already skips a failed section
(`PlexLibrary.brs`, "skipped a section that failed to load") without telling the viewer which.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: turning iCloud sync on waits for iCloud's first download before it pushes, N-036)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `appletv/n036-sync-turnon-hold` off main `9e2c945d`, for 1.0.30.

**Why.** `NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore` is a local copy that iCloud fills in the background, so on a TV that has not
finished its first download it reads empty even when the household has a lineup in iCloud. `setEnabled(true)` read that
empty copy, found no value in the cloud for any key it held a value for, and pushed them all: a new TV's first-load
defaults (the default package, Retro Mode on) became the latest write, and every other TV took them. Launch already held
its push for a brand-new TV; turn-on did not. The Settings row comment said turn-on "pushes this TV's lineup first", which
was the bug written down.

**Measured first.** `PreferenceSyncTurnOnTests` runs two TVs on a fake iCloud that behaves the way that matters: a
server, and a local copy per TV that stays empty until its first download, uploads on `synchronize()`, last write wins,
and tells the TVs that have downloaded. On main the new TV turns sync on before its download arrives and: iCloud's
`enabled_bundles` becomes `["nostalgex"]` where the household had four packages, the other TV's lineup becomes
`["nostalgex"]` and its Retro Mode flips from off to on, and the new TV never joins the household. Three of the
tests fail on main (the overwrite, the held push, turning off during the hold).

**Changed.**
- `setEnabled(true)`: when iCloud shows nothing and there is something to push, the push is held (`startHolding()`,
  the launch mechanism) for up to `holdTimeout` (30 s; injectable). The first download, or any change from another TV,
  ends the wait: what arrives is adopted (cloud wins) and only the keys iCloud still lacks are pushed. If nothing
  ever arrives, the wait ends by itself and this TV seeds iCloud. Turning sync off during the wait pushes nothing. When
  iCloud already shows values the download has arrived: nothing waits, the household wins, and only a key iCloud lacks
  goes up at once (the existing behaviour, tested).
- The Settings row comment now says that.
- Tests (5): the overwrite; the first TV seeds an empty iCloud once its download comes back empty; turning off during
  the hold; the wait ends on its own; no wait when the download is already here. NostalgexTests: 1,108 tests, 1,082
  passed, 0 failed, 26 skipped.

**Not changed.** `saveBundlePreferences` (`AppState+Channels.swift`): only a change the viewer made goes to
iCloud, so first-load auto-enable never pushes. The seeding wait is a cost for the first TV only (up to 30 s before
iCloud has its lineup). Not run on a real pair of TVs.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: Plex collection requests send a container size and read every page, N-038)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `appletv/n038-collection-container-size` off main `9e2c945d`, for 1.0.30.

**Why.** Plex logs "Missing X-Plex-Container-Size header, will fail with status 400 in the future" for the
collection requests: only the section item fetch sent a size. When Plex makes good on the warning the collection
scan would stop silently, because its callers swallow the error (`try?` on the list of collections, `continue` on a
collection's children) and an empty result reads as "this server has no collections". The per-show `allLeaves`
crawl (the fallback for a server that ignores `type=4`) had the same bare request.

**Changed.** `loadCollections`, `loadCollectionItems` and the per-show `allLeaves` read through one helper,
`fetchAllPages`, with `X-Plex-Container-Start` / `-Size` as the section fetch does (300 a page). It moves on by the
rows the server says a page holds (`size`) and stops at the server's `totalSize`, or at a short page when there is
none, so a server that sends fewer than asked, or a row that fails to decode, neither skips nor repeats rows. A
response with more rows than asked is a server that ignores paging and sent everything: it stops there. A ceiling of
5,000 pages keeps a server that never says it is done from looping us. `/library/sections` and `/identity` are
single small directory responses and are unchanged; not checked against a real server's log.

**Tests.** `PlexContainerSizeTests` (5): a fake Plex that answers 400 to a list request with no container size and
never sends more than 100 rows a response, with 318 collections (the I-068 case), a 1,250-item collection, a
250-episode show through the per-show crawl, and a legacy server that ignores paging. Four fail on main (400, or
only the first page), all pass now. NostalgexTests: 1,108 tests, 1,082 passed, 0 failed, 26 skipped.

**Not done.** The web tuner (the web agent's branch) and Roku (#189, tydude001).

## 2026-11-06 (Roku: a Jellyfin or Emby library with no videos in it is never read as films, #205)
