## 2026-11-06 (Roku: RESCAN LIBRARY says how many titles are on a channel, on none, and skipped, #207)

**Why.** #207, the Roku side of the Apple TV 1.0.30's library line and the web tuner's (2026-11-05 entry below):
a viewer who misses a title on every channel can tell "no channel takes it" from "it never loaded".

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/util/LibraryCoverage.brs` (new): the count, from the web's `scripts/nostalgex-library-coverage.js`
  and the Apple TV's definitions. The guide build filters only the switched-on packages' channels
  (`NxPoolChannelIds`), so the count reuses their filter results and runs every other `channels.json` channel
  itself, one server's titles at a time, dropping each slice's filter cache after it (I-065). It runs in steps of
  about 100 ms between the library task's messages, so a package switch or the 30 s re-check is still answered
  while it counts. A Dolby Vision profile 5 file the display can't show is on no channel, as the build has it. Over
  30,000 titles it isn't counted, as on the Apple TV. `NxCoverageReport` writes the console's `COVERAGE:` line.
- `roku/components/LibraryTask.brs`: `startCoverage` once the guide is handed over, `reportCoverage` when it is
  done and after a package switch (a franchise or collection channel moves it; a package alone doesn't). The line
  is saved in the `libraryHeld` record with the counts, for the load that made it.
- The loaders count the movies and episodes their runtime guards drop (`NxScanSkipAdd` at the four
  `durationMin <= 0` returns). The number is saved per server with the snapshot, so a Plex server read from its save
  keeps it, and in `libraryHeld`, so it survives a restart and goes with SIGN OUT.
- `roku/source/util/RescanInfo.brs`: `NxCoverageLine`, the line between the summary and "Last updated", and
  `NxSaveLibraryCoverage`. `components/SettingsView.brs`: the row shows every line it has, and grows by one only
  when the library line and a playback failure are both there.

**Tests.** `roku/tests/gen-coverage.mjs` runs the web's `compute`, `formatLine` and `orphanReport` with `itemPasses`
as `runLibraryCoverage` does, over the filter vectors' library (every second title) and every fourth real channel,
under both filter clocks, in six cases: four `minItems` settings, two of them again with built collection and
franchise pools. `roku/tests/CoverageTests.brs` (suite `coverage`, split in six off-device) checks each case's counts
per kind, the first-25 list, the line and the console line, and every third case again in many steps with ten
channels' results reused; that switching packages doesn't move the number and removing titles does; the wording; the
row's lines; the Plex and Jellyfin/Emby skipped counts from saved answers (missing, 0, 30 s, 59.999 s dropped; 60 s
kept; a music video counted with the movies); and, on a TV only, the saved record read back from the registry, a
newer load's record replacing the count, and SIGN OUT clearing it.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (Roku OS 16.0.4) against our Jellyfin 12.2.0 as a user who sees every library:
- Settings read `5,436 OF 5,492 ON CHANNELS · 56 ON NO CHANNEL (5 MOVIES, 51 EPISODES) · 2 SKIPPED (NO RUNTIME)`
  after the app was closed and opened again. The two skipped are Lab clips of 599,990,000 ticks (59.999 s); the server
  holds 5,494 movies, episodes and music videos.
- **Parity:** the 5,492 titles the TV loaded, printed from a build with a dump not in this branch and run through
  the web's `compute` with every `channels.json` channel, gave the same per kind (movies 799 of 804, episodes 4,633
  of 4,684, music videos 4 of 4) and the same first 25 titles, byte for byte.
- **Time:** 32.9 to 33.5 s over five loads, behind the guide, after the build had handed it over: 64 channels'
  results reused, 78 filtered. The longest step was 106 to 161 ms, and the final tally 197 to 213 ms. Memory 26%
  to 29% of the app's limit. The first build's longest step was 455 ms; checking the clock every 16 titles instead
  of 128 made it 366 ms, and splitting the end of the pass (marking the hits, dropping the filter cache) into steps
  of its own brought it down to the figures above.
- **The filter cache's key:** on a TV an item read back with `ParseJson` is a case-sensitive AA, and the filter's
  `item.nxFilter = ...` stores the key `nxfilter`, so `Delete("nxFilter")` leaves it (the test library's 309
  titles all kept theirs). The count deletes `nxfilter`, which clears either kind.
- **Remote:** a key reached the guide's handler 20 to 34 ms after the ECP press during the count (one at 77 ms, 12
  presses) and 17 to 21 ms after it, on the build before the cache delete's case changed (a freshly scanned
  library's items take either spelling).
- **A package switch:** KIDZ ZONE off left 5,436 on channels and moved "on the channels in the guide now" from
  4,138 to 3,882; on again, 4,138.

**Not measured.** A library of about 11,800 titles (ours is 5,492; at this rate about 70 s on this TV), a stick,
Plex on a TV (its skipped count is checked off-device only) and Emby on a TV. The Done when's
`scripts/qa/library-coverage.mjs` and `appletv/library-coverage-counts` aren't on `main`; the parity check above
used `scripts/nostalgex-library-coverage.js`, which is.

**Open.** Settings open when the count lands shows the line on its next redraw (leaving and opening it again).

## 2026-11-05 (web tuner: a library line in Settings, how many titles sit on a channel; Apple TV 1.0.30 parity)

**Why.** The Apple TV 1.0.30 says, under RESCAN LIBRARY, how many loaded titles sit on a channel, how many sit on none,
and how many the scan skipped for having no runtime (`appletv/library-coverage-counts`, `LibraryDiagnostics`). The web
had one console line (`LIBRARY: N items, M with tmdbID`) and nothing on screen, so a reader who saw a title missing
from every channel had no way to tell "no channel takes it" from "it did not load".

**Changed.**
- `scripts/nostalgex-library-coverage.js`: the count and the wording, from the Apple TV's definitions. **On a channel:**
  in the pool of at least one channels.json channel whose pool reaches its `minItems`, whether or not its package is
  on (seasonal ones count), or in a collection or franchise channel already built. **On no channel:** every other
  title, split by kind (MOVIES, EPISODES, MUSIC VIDEOS) when more than one kind has some. **Skipped:** movies and
  episodes the loaders drop on `durationMin <= 0`. Example:
  `11,633 OF 11,809 ON CHANNELS · 176 ON NO CHANNEL (4 MOVIES, 172 EPISODES) · 12 SKIPPED (NO RUNTIME)`.
  It tests each title against each channel with `itemPasses` (no pools are built), in slices of about 12 ms that give
  the page back between them, and stops at once when a newer library replaces the one it reads.
- `plex-tuner.html`: the line sits under LIBRARY in Settings, SERVER tab, in a quiet grey, and is empty until counted
  or when signed out. The four loaders count the skipped titles (once each, reset at the start of a scan) and the
  count is saved with the library cache, so the line survives a reload. The count starts 2.5 s after the pools are
  built, again after enrichment re-filters and after the collections are read, and a console `COVERAGE:` line carries
  the first 25 titles on no channel (year, certificate, rating, genres, studio, runtime, TMDB), console only.
- `scripts/nostalgex-library-coverage-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:library-coverage`, in `npm test`): 25 checks. The
  wording, the numbers against a plain loop over the real `channels.json` and filter, the slicing, the cancel, a channel
  short of its minimum, a built collection channel, package switches not moving the number.
- `scripts/library-coverage-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:library-coverage:browser`, headless): the real page against
  a stub Plex with a synthetic library. 10 checks: the line in the Apple TV's wording, the numbers against a plain loop
  over the library the page holds, the skipped count, the line after a reload, the console line, sign-out.

**Measured** in headless Chromium against a stub Plex, synthetic titles (not a real library):
- 11,800 titles: the count takes 6.7 s; the page's longest stretch busy while it ran was 25 ms (a heartbeat every
  10 ms), no task over 50 ms.
- 100,000 titles: the count takes 74 s, longest stretch busy 24 ms, no task over 50 ms, JS heap 99 MB before and after.
  The first load, including building all 142 channels and then the count, shows the line at 131 s. The JS heap peaked
  at 341 MB while loading.

**Not done.** A real Plex library was not run; the 11.8k figures are synthetic. The Apple TV needs the enrichment
record for a `productionCompanies` rule and the web matches the Plex studio without one (known, on purpose), so on a
library with no enrichment the web's on-a-channel figure is a little higher.

## 2026-11-05 (web tuner: a scan that loses part of the server keeps the rest; one that loses all of it is an error)

**Why.** Parity with the Apple TV's 1.0.30 rule (`SectionFailures`, N-039, found while measuring #146). The web already
skipped a Plex section or a Jellyfin library that threw, and went on to the next, so the "keep the rest" half was
there. Three things were not. A scan where every section failed ended in the "no content" screen, which says the
server has nothing, and saved an empty library. The Jellyfin and Emby scan read every `/Items` answer as JSON without
looking at its status, so a 401 or a 500 was an empty library and an expired sign-in never reached the "session
ended" line. And a library that lost a section was saved for 24 hours as if it were whole.

**Changed.**
- `plex-tuner.html`, Plex (`fetchPlexSectionPaged`, `scanOnePlexServer`, `fetchPlexLibraryFromServer`): a section
  page that answers 401 or 403 ends the scan with `plexStatus`, as the section list already did. Any other failed
  section is skipped and named (`lost N section(s), ...; kept M items from the others`). A server whose every section
  failed throws its last error, so the page shows its error line. A library that lost a section is not saved
  (`skipCacheSave`), so the next visit reads it whole.
- `plex-tuner.html`, Jellyfin and Emby (`fetchItems`): checks the status. 401 and 403 end the scan; another failure
  loses the library, but pages already read are kept; every library lost throws; a lost library is named and the result
  is not cached.
- `scripts/nostalgex-scan-failures-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:scan-failures`, in `npm test`): the real Jellyfin loader
  over a stub that fails on request. 18 checks; 9 fail without the change.
- `scripts/plex-section-failures-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:plex-section-failures`, headless): the real page
  against a stub Plex. 12 checks; 7 fail without the change (an all-sections failure showed the empty screen and was
  saved; a sign-in refused on a section page did the same).

**Not changed.** The page does not tell the viewer which section was lost; it names it in the console. The Apple
TV names it in its install log too, and shows nothing more.

## 2026-11-05 (Emby: the library scan asks for each title's rating and star rating)

**Why.** GitHub #204, measured by tydude001 on the Roku against an Emby 4.10.1.0 test server. Emby leaves
`OfficialRating` and `CommunityRating` out of an `/Items` answer unless `Fields` names them (0 of 200 films carried
either; 195 and 197 of 200 with them named). Jellyfin sends both either way. The web scan, like the Apple TV and the
Roku, never named them, so on Emby every title read as unrated. `SAT MORNING CARTOONS` (an allow-list of TV-Y, TV-Y7,
TV-G and G, plus unrated) took a TV-MA cartoon, because an unrated title passes it. `VHS VAULT`'s 9 PM hold on R and
NC-17, and WATERSHED, held nothing. The 13 `ratingMin` channels saw no star rating.

**Changed.**
- `plex-tuner.html` (`fetchItems` in `fetchJellyfinLibraryFromServer`, the one Items request the scan makes for films,
  shows and episodes): `Fields` now ends `...UserData,OfficialRating,CommunityRating`. The normaliser already read
  both (`contentRating` and `rating`).
- `scripts/nostalgex-emby-ratings-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:emby-ratings`, in `npm test`): the real loader as an Emby
  sign-in over a stub that withholds both fields unless `Fields` names them, then the real filter and the page's own
  `getTimeFilteredPool` at 8 PM and 9 PM. On `main` 9 of its 11 checks fail: the TV-MA cartoon is on SAT MORNING
  CARTOONS, VHS VAULT's pool keeps its R films at 8 PM, WATERSHED holds nothing, ALL TIME GREATS sees no stars. All 11 pass here.

**What changes for an Emby viewer, from the next library read** (the saved library lasts up to 24 hours): the channels
with an allow-list and no unrated pass stop being empty, kids and family channels lose their TV-MA, R and PG-13 titles
(titles with no rating still pass), VHS VAULT, WATERSHED and the 9 PM hold start holding R and TV-MA, and `ratingMin`
channels judge by Emby's own star rating instead of the OMDb fallback. Their lineups for the day move with the pools.

**Open.** The Roku's vectors (`roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` runs this loader and records its request paths) change
in 9 request lines: the Roku job goes red until `roku/source/mediabrowser/MediaBrowserLibrary.brs:42` names the same two
fields, so the two land together. The Apple TV (`EmbyAPIService.swift:218`, `JellyfinAPIService.swift:212`) and Android
(`MediaBrowserLibrary.kt:200`, PR #151) send the same list and are not changed here. Not run against a real Emby; the
Jellyfin side relies on #204's 12.2.0 measurement and on Jellyfin's Fields binder skipping a name it does not know.

## 2026-11-05 (Roku: WATERSHED, the 9 PM hold, its switch and its card, #190)

**Why.** #190: the Apple TV and the web tuner have a WATERSHED switch that holds R, NC-17 and TV-MA titles until
9 PM on every channel without its own `blockRatings`. The Roku had none, so those titles aired all day.

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/guide/Lineup.brs`: `NxTimeFilteredPool` takes the switch and applies the global pass after the
  channel's own rules, with no fallback, as `Channel.filteredPool` does. `NxIsWatershedHold` mirrors
  `isWatershedHold`. Held to `scripts/watershed-golden.json` by `roku/tests/WatershedGoldenTests.brs` (13 cases, pool
  and hold), and `run.sh` runs `nostalgex-watershed-smoke.mjs` on the file first, as for the other goldens.
- `roku/source/guide/Watershed.brs`: the switch (registry `player`, `watershed`, off by default, sent nowhere) and the
  Apple TV's words for the guide row and the card.
- `roku/source/guide/GuideSchedule.brs`, `roku/components/LibraryTask.brs`: the library task reads the switch before
  every schedule. The re-check's key and each channel's pool memo carry the gate, so the switch, 9 PM and midnight
  reschedule, and a guide built under the other setting isn't reused (`sameSchedule` compares it too). Each
  scheduled channel says whether the gate is closed on it and whether it alone emptied it. The re-check prints its
  time and memory. 13 checks on this wiring in `WatershedGoldenTests.brs`.
- `roku/components/GuideView.brs`: a held channel's row reads BROADCASTS RESUME AT 9 PM, and tuning it puts up the
  card in place of a failure, counting none. A programme playing when the gate moves is kept until it ends, through
  later refreshes too. Closing Settings asks for the re-check at once.
- `roku/components/SettingsView.brs`: WATERSHED, after MY COLLECTIONS until #188's rail moves it.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4) against the lab Jellyfin (17 channels, 18 with the collection below).
- The #190 build (`1a0af9c`): the switch rescheduled about 1.3 s after Settings closed. With a lab collection of six
  R films switched on (CH 400), WATERSHED on before 9 PM put BROADCASTS RESUME AT 9 PM in its row. A deep link to
  CH 400 put up the card, which stayed with nothing retried. Switching it off cleared the card, and CH 400 played
  (picture in 3.7 s).
- A diagnostic build (`1a0af9c` with the gate at 10 AM and pool counts printed), switched on at 9:47: R, NC-17 and
  TV-MA titles went to 0 in each of the 10 pools it printed, e.g. CH 14's from 50 to 21 and CH 13's from 20 to 5.
  VHS VAULT's pool was 25 either way. The 66 titles on screen had none of those ratings. At 10:00 the re-check put
  them back (CH 14 at 50), and 8 on screen had them. CH 3 stayed tuned through the switch and the 10:00 change, with
  no retune. Whether the kept-programme path was what held it is not known.
- The re-check of 18 channels, forced every minute in throwaway builds: main 149 to 164 ms, this branch with the
  switch off 163 to 170 ms, with it on 257 to 270 ms, and 832 ms for the one that follows switching it on (every
  day repacked). Memory 25 to 26% throughout. By the code, the ~100 ms with the switch on is each pool filtered again
  for today, tomorrow and the hold check; on a TV the re-check runs once an hour.

On Emby nothing is held: its scan never asks for `OfficialRating`, so no title is rated (#204).

**Open.** Not seen on a TV: the real 9 PM and midnight, a launch deep link onto a held channel, the golden suite
through `deploy.sh --test`, a Plex sign-in and a stick.

## 2026-11-05 (Roku: a deep link while the power-loss seed's guide is up waits for the full guide, #203)

**Why.** #203: after a power loss the app opens on the seed's one-channel guide (#182), and `MainScene.onDeepLink`

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/guide/DeepLink.brs`: `NxDeepLinkWaits`. A link waits while the seed's guide is up and can't apply

  link at all don't wait. 8 cases in `roku/tests/DeepLinkTests.brs`.

  full guide replaces the seed's.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (OS 16.0.4) against the lab Jellyfin (17 channels; the seed was CH 3), with this branch on
main `2b71559` and a scratch launch switch that deleted the `cachefs:` files and kept the registry. Times are from
the launch:
- A link for CH 14 at 2.3 s, and on a second launch at 16.0 s, waited with CH 3 still tuned. CH 14 tuned 0.5 s after the
  full guide went up, at 24.4 s and 24.7 s.
- A link for CH 7 after the guide was up tuned 0.2 s later.
- A launch link for CH 14 kept the loading screen up, with no CH 3, until CH 14 tuned at 24.3 s.
- A link for CH 3, the seed's own, went to the seed's guide at once.

**Open.** A Plex sign-in, a stick, and a link that comes in while the seed's last airing runs out (the loading screen
comes back, and the guide made then takes the link when it's created).

## 2026-11-05 (Roku: the collections lists are read in sized windows, the children 120 at a time, #189)

**Why.** A tester's Plex log from a Roku first load said "Missing X-Plex-Container-Size header" (#189). Sent from
a computer with the Roku's headers to our Plex 1.43.5, the server warns on two of the port's list requests:
`/library/sections/<key>/collections` and `/library/collections/<key>/children`. `/library/sections`,
`/library/metadata/<key>/allLeaves` and `/hubs/continueWatching/items` don't warn bare or with any size up to 20,000,
and the section item reads (`/library/sections/<key>/all`) already send one. The query-string form silences the warning, so no header is needed.
Plex also caps the window per path: `/collections` and the section item reads at 1000, `/children` at 120. Above that it
logs "X-Plex-Container-Size header exceeds limit 120. This will fail with status code 400 in the future". By that
probe the web tuner's 300 window (N-038) should draw it on every collection read; the web tuner wasn't run.

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/collections/Collections.brs`: `NxPlexPaged` and `NxPlexPagedFrom`, a port of `fetchPlexPaged`, read
  the section list, each section's collections and each collection's children in windows until `totalSize` or a
  short page. A failed window drops that list, and a server that ignores the start ends the walk. The window travels
  beside the path, so the golden vectors still record bare paths and pass unchanged. Children are read 120 at a
  time, the rest 300.
- `roku/source/plex/PlexLibrary.brs`: `NxPlexCollectionsFetcher` puts the window on the request; the children's
  first windows still go five at a time.
- `roku/tests/CollectionTests.brs`: 19 checks. 650 collections with one of 700 children give the same result as
  whole answers, no request goes without a size, and the collections go 300 and the children 120 at a time. Also a server
  that caps the window, one with no `totalSize`, one that ignores the start, and a failed window. 14 fail on main.

**Pressed** on our 55R617 (Roku OS 15.3.4) against our Plex 1.43.5: 5,501 titles and 69 collections. RESCAN
LIBRARY three times on each build. Main (`2fb4625`): the collections step took 2.2, 2.2 and 2.4 s, and Plex logged
74 warnings each time, 5 on `/collections` and 69 on `/children`. This branch (`91dc0df`): 4.2, 4.2 and 4.0 s, no
warning, and the same 22 channels and pools fingerprint. DISCOVERING COLLECTIONS finished every time on both. The
step is slower because Plex answers a sized `/children` request more slowly: a median of 258 ms against 128 ms in
Plex's log for the TV's requests, and 104 against 57 ms from a computer, the same there at 120 or 300. The TV ran
`91dc0df`; the next commit changes only tests and docs. A first load after a fresh sign-in: main
18.6 s for the step and 74 warnings, this branch (build `6868848acfb3`, what the head stages) 22.6 s and none; the guide came up
38.5 and 42.5 s after sign-in.

**Open.** A library of a few hundred collections, as the tester's 318: by our server's
per-request cost, an estimate, the step would take about 9 s longer than now. Whether the tester's hang was this is unknown. The web tuner's `/children` window is 300.

## 2026-11-05 (privacy: the Roku app saves its first channel's next few hours)

**Shipped.** Today, 2026-11-05, on Chad's go under his standing rule that privacy text ships once reviewed: the Roku
section of the privacy policy now covers the power-loss start in Roku 1.0.12, with the effective date November 5,
2026. No tuner file changed and there is no `tuner-v` tag, so the Docker image is untouched.

**Why.** @tydude001's #182 saves the first channel's airings to the Roku registry so the app can play something
right after a power loss, while the library loads again. The saved library and guide sit in the Roku's cache, which a
power loss or the Roku's own clean-up takes. The seed is in the registry, so it survives both. The Roku section's "On
the TV it keeps" paragraph has to say so.

**Changed.** One sentence group in "The Roku app" section, in `privacy.html` and `Nostalgex/PRIVACY_POLICY.md`, the
same words in both:
- the list of what the app keeps adds "the titles, times and file details of your first channel for the next few
  hours, so it can start playing right away after the TV loses power";
- sign-out now lists "those saved hours" among what it removes (it clears the seed with the other caches);
- removing the app removes "your sign-in, settings and those saved hours", and the cache sentence now says "the saved
  library and guide sit in the Roku's own cache", because the seed does not;
- the Effective date moves from November 3 to November 5, 2026, the day it went live.

**Checked.** Against the 1.0.12 source on main (`2b71559f`), not just the PR. `source/guide/ColdBootSeed.brs` holds the
first channel's id, number, name and colour and its airings from the one on now, each with its times, title, episode,
year, rating, part key, container, codecs, audio and subtitle tracks, duration, size and server index, and no summary,
inside a 10 KB budget. `LibraryTask.saveSeed` writes it to the registry and nothing in the seed code makes a request,
so nothing new is sent. `NxClearAccountCaches` deletes it on sign-out, and on a fresh sign-in over caches another
account left. It holds no token and no server address. The first draft said "titles and times"; it now says "file
details" too, because the part key and the codecs are in it.

**Open.** Nothing.

## 2026-11-05 (Jellyfin and Emby: a playlist is no longer scanned as a film)

**Why.** A report from a Docker web tuner on Jellyfin: a workout playlist of eight songs aired on CH 7 VHS VAULT
as a 33 minute programme, and tuning it answered "Jellyfin answered HTTP 500 before it started sending video".
Not seen on a real server here; this is rebuilt on a stub and the cause is read from Jellyfin's source.

**The path.** `fetchJellyfinLibraryFromServer` read `/UserViews`, called every view that was not TV or Music
Videos a movie library, and asked it for `IncludeItemTypes=Movie`. The Playlists view (CollectionType `playlists`)
is one of those. Jellyfin's `PlaylistsFolder.GetItemsInternal` (Emby.Server.Implementations/Playlists/PlaylistsFolder.cs)
sets `query.Recursive = true; query.IncludeItemTypes = [Playlist]` over whatever the client sent, so the answer to
"Movie" under that view is its playlists. The loader mapped any row to `type: 'movie'`. The playlist came out as
`type movie, duration 33, year '', genres [], contentRating '', partKey null` (it has no media source). The year
rule lets an item with no year through (`passesYearRange`), so by the real filter it entered CH 7 VHS VAULT (type
movie, 1980 to 1999), CH 16 DVD SHELF (2000 to 2009) and CH 51 FLICKS (type movie, genre excludes only).

**The 500.** Measured in the real page with the real hls.js against a stub: tuning the playlist sends
`POST /Items/{id}/PlaybackInfo`, then `GET /Videos/{id}/master.m3u8`, and with HTTP 500 on both the page shows
the card word for word. That the real server answers 500 for a playlist id is not measured. A raw
`GET /Items/{id}` and the status of those two requests from the reporter's server would settle it.

**Changed.**
- `scripts/nostalgex-jellyfin-urls.js` (point 12): `sectionType(collectionType)` returns `'other'` for Music,
  Playlists, Collections, Books, Photos, Home Videos, Live TV, Trailers, Folders and Channels, and the scan never asks
  those for items. `itemTypes` and `hasAskedType` give what a section is asked for and drop any row whose `Type`
  was not asked for (a row with no `Type` is kept), for a server that answers with more than it was asked.
  `scripts/jellyfin-library-golden.json` pins both, for the other apps to port; the urls smoke reads it.
- `plex-tuner.html`: the scan calls them. Movies is still asked for `Movie`, Music Videos for `Movie,MusicVideo`
  (I-067), TV for `Series` then `Episode`. The Roku vectors (`roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` runs this loader over
  a fixture) are unchanged.
- `scripts/nostalgex-jellyfin-library-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:jellyfin-library`, in `npm test`): the real loader and
  the real filter over a stub library with a playlist, songs, an album, an artist and a collection, answered as
  Jellyfin does and by a server that ignores `IncludeItemTypes`. On `main` 16 of its 28 checks fail; the playlist is
  in the library and in three channels' pools. Here all 28 pass.
- `scripts/jellyfin-non-video-items-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:jellyfin-non-video:browser`, headless): the real
  page on Jellyfin and Emby. On `main` 14 of 22 checks fail and it prints what playing the playlist showed.

**Open.** A library cached before this change keeps the playlist until the 24 hour cache is refreshed. Not checked on a
real Jellyfin or Emby; whether Emby's Playlists view answers like Jellyfin's is not known. Apple TV
(`JellyfinAPIService.sectionType`, `EmbyAPIService`), Roku (`NxMbItemTypesFor`) and Android (`MediaBrowserLibrary.kt`)
read the same views the same way and have no `Type` check; none is changed here.

## 2026-11-04 (Roku: a "finished" while the server is asked after an error hands over nothing, #184's Plex way)

**Why.** #184: on the Roku, a stream the server answers for but the player can't play never reached the
playback card or the five-in-a-row stop. On Plex the server stream errors, its retry errors too,
`failAttempt` asks the server with the attempt still running, and Roku's player then says `finished`.
`NxFinishedAction` took that as the file's end and handed over to the next airing, a fresh start with its
own retry, so the server's answer was dropped.

**Changed.** `roku/source/guide/Fallback.brs`: a probe started by an error (`probeFor.finished` not true)
passes `probingAfterError`, and a `finished` then is ignored, as one after the card or while a retry waits
already is (`components/GuideView.brs` passes it). The existing case for a probe started by an end is
unchanged. Three cases in `roku/tests/FallbackTests.brs`.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (Roku OS 16.0.4) against Plex (5,470 items), with a scratch launch switch that
broke the player's copy of channel 2's server stream and left the probe's. Main at `5971d06`, 40 s: 21
tunes, 10 hand-overs, no card. This branch, 40 s: 9 tunes and four cards, "1 in a row" up to 4; run for
70 s, the fifth card at 42 s stopped the channel, and nothing was tried in the next 29 s.

**Open.** Jellyfin and Emby go another way (the stream ends unplayed, then the server's 200 is read as a
short file's end), a second PR per Chad on #184, with the same 40 s check on a TV.

## 2026-11-04 (Roku: an end the server answers for, after the start failed while it was asked, isn't a short file's end, #184's Jellyfin and Emby way)

**Why.** #184: on Jellyfin and Emby the server stream ended unplayed, so the server was asked. The player ended
again (an error), which `failAttempt` dropped with the probe under way, and the server's 200 was read as a join
past the end of a file shorter than its slot, so the next airing started fresh, and the card never came.

**Changed.** `roku/components/GuideView.brs`: `failAttempt` marks a probe it can't act on
(`probeFor.failedWhileAsking`). `roku/source/guide/Fallback.brs`: new `NxProbeAnswerAction` decides what an answer
leads to; an end, an answer and that failure is a failed start (the next rung, or the card). An end and an answer
with no failure still hands over. 9 cases in `roku/tests/FallbackTests.brs`.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 (Roku OS 16.0.4) against the lab Emby as `nxlab`, with a scratch launch switch that broke
the player's copy of every stream of channel 7. Main at `456a511`, 40 s: 106 tunes, 53 hand-overs, no card (26 this
way, 27 the Plex way). This change alone: the ends the server answered went down the ladder, and the hand-overs
that were left came the Plex way (41). With #199 too: 12 tunes, five cards, the fifth at 31 s, then nothing tuned.
On the lab Jellyfin with both: five cards in 41 s.

## 2026-11-04 (Web tuner: every Plex list request sends X-Plex-Container-Size, and long lists are read whole)

**Why.** A Plex server log from a Roku first load said "Missing X-Plex-Container-Size header, will fail with
status 400 in the future" (Trello N-038, Roku issue #189). The web tuner sent no size on four Plex list reads:
`/library/sections`, `/library/sections/{key}/collections`, `/library/collections/{id}/children` and
`/library/metadata/{id}/allLeaves` (every show's episodes). Only the paged section fetch did. Measured with a fake
Plex that answers 400 to a list request with no size: `main` loads nothing at all from it, the first request
(`/library/sections`) is refused and the library never loads. So the day Plex starts refusing, the web tuner and
the Docker image stop at the first request. A size alone is not the fix: Plex answers it with the first window
only, and a collection of 650 films would come back as 300.

**Changed.**
- `scripts/nostalgex-collections.js`: `fetchPlexPaged` reads a Plex list in windows of 300 until `totalSize`, or
  until the first short page when the server sends no total. The next window starts where the last one ended, so a
  server that caps the window below 300 loses nothing. A server that ignores the window ends the walk instead of
  looping. A failed window throws, so a caller never keeps half a list: a half-read collection is dropped, as a
  failed one already was. The window travels as the second argument of the caller's getter
  (`getJSON(path, { start, size })`, turned into the request by `plexWindowPath`), so the path the engine asks for
  is still the bare endpoint. The Roku golden vectors (`roku/tests/gen-collections.mjs`) record those paths and are
  unchanged.
- `plex-tuner.html`: the section list, each show's episode list and the collection scan page through it. The
  episode list now checks the HTTP status before it parses, as the other reads do.
- `scripts/nostalgex-plex-paging-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:plex-paging`, in `npm test`): the fetchers against a fake
  Plex that refuses a list with no size and returns only the window asked for, in four server shapes (totalSize
  sent, left out, window capped at 100, window ignored), plus a failed second window and a 750-episode show, and a
  read of `plex-tuner.html` that every getter sends the window. 33 checks pass here; run against `main`'s code 24
  fail (and 5 pass). A version that sends the size and never pages fails 12.
- `scripts/plex-container-size-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:plex-container-size`, headless, not in `npm test`
  like the other browser smokes): the real page against the same kind of server. 7 of 8 checks fail on `main`, all
  8 pass here: 13 list requests, none without a size, the 750-episode show in three windows, the 650-film
  collection whole.

**Open.** Not run against a real Plex server: the window parameters are the ones the section fetch has always
sent, but no real server has been asked for `/library/sections` or `allLeaves` with them from this change. Which of
the four endpoints Plex warns about is also unknown; all four now send a size. Roku (#189) and the Apple TV
(`PlexAPIService.loadCollections`, `loadCollectionItems`) still send none. The engine change is the web side only.

## 2026-11-04 (Web tuner: the Deezer genre lookup was blocked by the site CSP; one-source fix)

**Why.** Found by reading the code on 2026-10-26 (Trello N-012), confirmed today. `scripts/nostalgex-music-brainz.js`
asks Deezer for music video genres by JSONP, because api.deezer.com sends no CORS headers: it adds a
`<script src="https://api.deezer.com/...?callback=...">`. That load is governed by `script-src`, and `vercel.json`
allowed only `'self'`, `'unsafe-inline'`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and `statsngraphs.lol`.

**Measured** with headless Chromium, calling `NostalgexMusicBrainz.deezerResolve("Smells Like Teen Spirit",
"Nirvana")` on the live `https://nostalgex.app/plex-tuner`: the browser refuses the script (a `script-src-elem`
violation on `https://api.deezer.com/search`), and the call rejects with "Deezer script error" after 4 ms. The same
page with the CSP header removed in flight resolves in 822 ms with the album genre (Rock) and year. A local copy
served with `vercel.json`'s header behaves like the live page; with `https://api.deezer.com` added to `script-src`
it resolves. The live header and `vercel.json` match.

**Changed.**
- `vercel.json`: `https://api.deezer.com` added to `script-src`. It is the site-wide header (`/(.*)`), so it also
  applies to the marketing pages.
- `scripts/tuner-isolation-check.mjs`: the CSP check now lists `https://api.deezer.com` among what the tuner needs,
  so a later edit cannot drop it unnoticed.
- `scripts/deezer-csp-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:deezer-csp`, headless): the real page with the CSP read
  from `vercel.json`, Deezer answered by a stub, so no network. 3 of its 6 checks fail on `main`'s header, all 6
  pass with the change; a header without the host is refused, which is the negative control.

**Docker is not affected.** The image sets `<meta name="nostalgex-build" content="selfhost">`, so `lookupsEnabled()` is
false and `deezerJSONP` rejects before it makes a script. Its nginx CSP never listed Deezer and does not need to.

**Open.** A failed lookup is cached as checked: `withDeezerGenres` stamps `deezerCheckedAt` even when Deezer threw,
and `isSettled` counts that as done until the entry is 90 days old. After the header changes, music videos a browser
already tried will not ask Deezer again on their own. That needs its own change (stamp only on an answer).

## 2026-11-04 (Roku: the loading screen holds the screensaver off; a paused app isn't a stalled server)

**Why.** The 2026-11-04 entry on the Apple TV staying awake owed "one stick check of a long load under" the
Roku screensaver. Measured on our 43S45 (Roku OS 16.0.4, screensaver wait 10 min) with main at `29203c9`: the
screensaver came on over the loading screen, and the Roku paused the whole app under it. For 39 min no request
went out, nothing printed and the loading dots stopped. The first stall look after a button woke the TV read
that as 210 s with no progress: "abandoning this scan" with 4 items read, and the guide came up NO CHANNELS
FOUND and was saved.

**Changed.**
- `roku/components/LoadingView.xml`: a hidden `Video` node with `disableScreenSaver`, Roku's switch for
  this, for as long as the loading screen is up. It never gets content. The Apple TV's counterpart is
  `isIdleTimerDisabled` while loading (`ScreenAwakePolicy.swift`).
- `roku/source/util/LoadStall.brs`: `NxStallSkipPause`, which `MainScene`'s watch calls before every verdict.
  A look 20 s or more after the last one (they are 2 s apart) means the app was paused, and that gap doesn't
  count as quiet. It covers a pause the hold doesn't prevent. 12 new checks in `roku/tests/StallTests.brs`.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 with the lab Jellyfin behind a proxy that made the load slow but never stalled: one
item per page with the real total, each answer held 28 s, and two 500s before each, so 84 s per page. Main:
the screensaver at 10 min, then the stop and NO CHANNELS FOUND above. This branch: no screensaver in 25.5 min
without a key, and the load finished after 23.8 min with all 13 items, the same 36 channels and pools
fingerprint as an unslowed load.

**Open.** Not seen on a TV: `NxStallSkipPause` itself, since with the hold no pause happened. A Plex load, a
stick, and a long load behind #182's seed channel.

## 2026-11-04 (channels.json v50: no channel is built from fewer than three titles)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `rules/min-items-floor` off main `29203c9f`, not pushed.

**Why.** Chad's rule: "the minItems should never be 1." A channel's `minItems` is the smallest pool it is built
from. At 1, a pool of one title fills the whole day with that title back to back: on the Android build, TRUE CRIME
aired the same documentary six times in a row. The Android app was right to do it, because it reads the same
`channels.json` and the file said 1. TRUE CRIME (id 40, CH 121) and PREMIERES (id 403, CH 64) had been at 1 since
1.0.21. Every other channel was already at 3 or more (85 at 3, 45 at 5, 8 at 10, one at 15, one at 50).

**Changed.**
- `channels.json` v49 to v50: TRUE CRIME and PREMIERES `minItems` 1 to 3. Nothing else in the file moved.
  `CHANNELS.md`, `public/sitemap.xml` and `scripts/bundle-lastmod.json` regenerated (only the essentials and
  truecrime bundles re-stamp, because they hold the two channels).
- A guard so it stays that way. `scripts/nostalgex-filter-smoke.mjs` (part of `npm test`, and of CI's channel-engine
  job whenever `channels.json` changes) reads the shipped file and fails on any channel whose `minItems` is below 3,
  naming it: "TRUE CRIME (id 40, CH 121) has minItems 1; the floor is 3". It was run against v49 first and failed on
  exactly those two. It also catches 0, which the Apple TV reads as 0 while the web tuner, Roku and the Android app
  read it as 50. A channel with no `minItems` is fine: every engine defaults it to 50.
- No golden file, fixture or vector pinned either value or the version, so none changed. The filter, schedule,
  franchise, rating, season and DST goldens and the Roku vectors are as they were. The Swift tests that build
  channels by hand with `minItems: 1` or 0 are exercising scheduling on small pools and never read `channels.json`,
  so they stay.

**Checked, one suite at a time.** `npm test` green (the filter smoke is 212 checks, 143 of them the new guard).
`npm run build` and `npm run build:selfhost` green, and both outputs carry v50. Roku off-device suite (`roku/tests/run.sh`,
capped at 2 interpreters): 54 of 54 parts passed, `ALL TESTS PASSED`. tvOS `NostalgexTests`: 1,103 tests, 1,077 passed, 26 skipped
(the opt-in harnesses), 0 failures, run against an app bundle that held v50. Not run: the Android engine tests (no
Gradle here) and anything on a device.

**What PREMIERES sees.** PREMIERES is every title added to the server in the last 14 days (`addedWithinDays` 14,
movies and episodes, 29 genres). On a server nobody adds to, its pool is 0 and it is off at 1 or at 3. The change
only bites when 1 or 2 titles arrived in the fortnight: PREMIERES used to air that one title (or two) all day, and
is now off the guide until a third arrives. The Apple TV's "why is this channel off the air" line is built from
`minItems`, so it will read "Needs 3 matching titles. You have 2." (from the string in `SettingsSharedComponents`,
not seen on a TV). Plex normally stamps `addedAt` at scan time, so a freshly scanned library counts everything as
new and PREMIERES is on either way for the first 14 days, then follows the trickle; that is from the rule, not
measured, and how Jellyfin and Emby fill `addedAt` was not checked.

Measured by replaying PREMIERES' real rule through the shared JS filter over a sliding 14-day window of one large
library's add dates, for the 269 days after its bulk import aged out, then thinning the same history to every 10th,
50th and 200th title to stand in for libraries that grow that much slower (days on the guide at `minItems` 1, at 3;
share of days the pool sat at 1 or 2):
- the full library: 100% and 100%; the pool never fell under 10, so nothing changes;
- every 10th title: 100% and 75%; 25% of days at 1 or 2;
- every 50th title: 77% and 30%; 47% of days at 1 or 2;
- every 200th title: 43% and 3%; 41% of days at 1 or 2.
So on a small or slow library PREMIERES is now mostly off, and the days it used to show were mostly one title on
loop. A library that adds a few titles a fortnight, or a server fed in bursts, keeps it. This is one library's
history thinned, not a survey; the thinning keeps the burst shape.

**Which surface gets it, and when.**
- Web tuner: `plex-tuner.html` fetches `channels.json` from its own origin, so the hosted tuner has it on the push
  that carries this, and Docker on the next `tuner-v*` tag (the file is in the image).
- Apple TV: a build step copies the repo's `channels.json` into the app, so the next build. The app tries
  `<server>/channels.json` first and falls back to the bundled copy, but a Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server does not
  serve one, so in practice the bundled file is what runs.
- Roku: `roku/data/channels.json` is a link to the repo file, so the next package.
- Android (PR #151): `android/app/src/main/assets/channels.json` is a link to the repo file too, so the next build
  from a tree that has this commit. The PR's tests do not pin either value, and its demo channels use ids outside the
  file. The PR branch and this one share the same merge base on main and does not touch `channels.json`; a trial
  merge of the two conflicts only in this file, where both prepend an entry (keep both).

**Not changed.** The floor is checked in JS only. The Swift and Roku suites read the same file but do not assert
it; one check on the file is enough, and a second copy of the number in Swift would be one more thing to drift.

**Seen, not touched.** `ci.yml`'s `tvos` filter does not list `channels.json` or `channels-memberships.json`, so a
push that changes only those skips the tvOS unit tests until the nightly run, though several Swift tests read them
(`BundleBuildTests`, `FilterGoldenTests`, `ChannelNumberingTests`). The `roku`, `android` and channel-engine

## 2026-11-04 (tests: the Plex discovery harness measures the grace window, not the runner)

**Shipped.** Nothing; test code only. Branch `test/discovery-harness-ci` off main `29203c9f`.

**Why.** `PlexDiscoveryDeadLocalHarnessTests.testARemoteThatAlreadyFailedDoesNotStretchTheGrace` failed twice on
GitHub's macOS runners (runs 41850712310 and 41874032385; 12.9 s for two discoveries that take about 3.3 s each
here) and passed locally every time. The log carried no timeline, so which candidate held the wait is unknown.
Measured here: a port opened and closed just before the run refused in 30 ms or less in 30 of 30 tries, ports are
handed out in sequence (198 of 199 steps were +1, so a freed port is not reused soon), and 192.0.2.1 black-holes
for the full 12 s local timeout. Two things in the tests depended on the machine: the dead candidates (a closed
port relies on the OS refusing at once; RFC 5737 addresses can black-hole, refuse or route depending on the
network) and the bound (total time under 5 s includes how fast the stand-in server answers on a loaded runner,
which leaves 2 s of headroom over the 3 s grace).

**Changed.**
- Both tests assert the grace as served: from the first hit to the answer, under 5 s (the failure modes are 12 s
  and 15 s) and over 2.5 s (the locals still get their 3 s). The failing-remote test also checks its precondition:
  that remote reported a failure before the grace ran out.
- Dead candidates that behave the same on any machine: seven locals are stand-ins that take the app's 12 s timeout
  and honour cancellation; the eighth is a real loopback server that accepts and never answers, so a real
  URLSession request still has to be cancelled when the grace ends. The failed remote is a loopback server that
  accepts and closes (`LoopbackSilentServer`), held open for the whole test.
- Every run's timeline is attached to the result and quoted in every failure message.

**Measured (simulator).** The class 20 times under `-parallel-testing-enabled YES -test-iterations 20`: 80 test runs,
0 failed; 120 discoveries, grace served 3.00 to 3.10 s every time, first hit at 0.35 s or sooner. With the old bug put
back (a remote that had already failed still counted as a pending patient candidate) the failing-remote test fails
both runs with the grace at 11.7 s, and its message carries the timeline. NostalgexTests 1,103 tests, 0 failed.

**Not found.** The cause on GitHub. The new timelines will name the candidate that held the wait if it happens again.

## 2026-11-04 (Android: the 1.0.30 fixes from main, ported)

**Why.** Four of the Apple TV, web and Roku fixes that landed on main on 2026-11-04 apply to Android. `feature/android` is rebased onto `29203c9`.

**Changed.**
- **Music Videos libraries on Jellyfin and Emby (I-067, #172).** A library typed `musicvideos` is asked for `Movie,MusicVideo`; every other library still asks for `Movie`. `MediaBrowserScanTest` reads the web tuner's vectors, which now hold four clips, and its fake server reads `IncludeItemTypes` as a comma list. Putting `Movie` back makes it fail. Against the test Jellyfin 12.4.0, CH 500 HIGH ROTATION and CH 501 POP filled from its Music Videos library.
- **Big Jellyfin and Emby movie libraries (N-033).** A movie library reports progress after every 200-item page, as Plex does, so the stall watch sees it arriving. A scan stopped mid-library keeps the pages already read. A library that fails with an error, rather than being stopped, still leaves none of its items, as the web tuner's per-view catch. `MovieSectionScanProgressTest` (new, 3 tests, both backends, 1,000 films): the old scan reported once and kept nothing from a stop at the fourth page; now it reports 0, 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000, and keeps 600.
- **A burned-in forced subtitle the server can't produce (q106).** `PlaybackInfoHandshake.negotiate` fetches the burned stream's master playlist, its first variant and the first segment before choosing it, as `JellyfinPlaybackResolver.negotiate` does. An HTTP error on any of them means the plain answer is used and the refused session is stopped. A timeout, a dropped connection or a playlist it can't read keep the burned stream.
  - 6 new cases in `PlaybackInfoHandshakeTest`; 4 fail with the check turned off.
  - Measured on an Android 16 Google TV emulator against the test Jellyfin behind `scripts/lab-forced-subtitle/logproxy.py` in `segments` mode, which answers 500 to the burned stream's segments as Chad's Emby 4.10.1 does:
    - With the check: the first segment refused, the session stopped 0.13 s later, and the film playing without its forced lines 1.0 s after the handshake.
    - Without it, Android was worse off than the Apple TV's 20 s wait. ExoPlayer fails on the first HTTP 500, so the programme counted as one that wouldn't start, and the film never played.
    - With the route healthy, the burned stream is still chosen; the check waited 552 ms for the first segment.
- **The TV stays awake on the loading screen (N-033, `ScreenAwakePolicy`).** `FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON` is held on the window while the screen is a load (`Loading` or `LibraryLoad`) and released anywhere else. Playback keeps its own hold through the player's view, so neither releases the other. A refresh behind the guide never shows these screens. Checked on the emulator with the server paused mid-load: the flag was on throughout the load and off on the library choice before it.
- `engine/build.gradle.kts`: the generated vectors are inputs to the test task, not only dependencies. Before, a change to `plex-tuner.html` or a Roku fixture left the test task up to date, and it reported the last result. That is how the music video change first looked like it passed after the rebase.

**Not needed.**
- **Plex discovery's grace window.** Android's `ServerResolve` is the web tuner's module, which works the outcome out again on every report.
- **AUDIO LANGUAGE on transcodes (#177).** Android already does this.
- **Saving the enrichment cache across launches (I-073).** Android keeps its cache in a file with the web's 7-day TTL, and builds the lineup from the saved library on every launch, so there is no saved lineup to lose a channel from.

**Not checked.** A real Emby with the burn-in fault. A movie library big enough to be slow on a real server. Most of the test Jellyfin's films are gone from disk, so only the films still there were played.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: the enrichment cache survives a relaunch; a rebuild that can't see it keeps the lineup)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `appletv/i073-enrichment-cache` off main `7bc68850`, for 1.0.30 (I-073, GitHub #185:
CARTOON NETWORK gone after 1.0.29).

**Why.** The networks rule never changed. The TMDB/OMDb enrichment cache was memory only, filled inside
`enrichItems`. After a snapshot restore it was empty; the 6h refresh skips an unchanged library under 24h, so it
stayed empty for the session. The first package rebuild after that (a switch in Settings, a lineup from iCloud)
read `networks` off the empty cache, CH 215 came back with 0 of its 5, `mergeBuiltPackageChannels` dropped it and
saved the dropped lineup as the snapshot, so it stayed gone across relaunches. 50 of 142 channels carry a rule that
reads enrichment (networks, keywords, production companies, OMDb scores), so it was a class; 1.0.29's Settings
explainer made it visible. The web tuner and Roku already persist their caches with a 7-day TTL.

**Changed.**
- `EnrichmentCacheStore`: one JSON file, `enrichment_cache_v1.json`, under `LocalStore` (Caches; under the harness
  root when isolation is on), rows keyed by TMDB id, 7-day TTL on `fetched_at` like the web and Roku. Saved in
  the background when a pass ends; loaded in `applyLibrarySnapshot` before any pool can be rebuilt. Server
  independent, so a sign-out keeps it.
- `mergeBuiltPackageChannels`: while `enrichmentPending` (no row in memory for a library with TMDB ids), a channel
  whose rule `dependsOnEnrichment` and comes back under `minItems` keeps the last build's copy instead of being
  dropped. The rule is narrower than "never drop below minItems while pending": a plain genre or title channel
  that emptied still goes, because its pool is evidence; an enrichment channel's small pool from a build that
  could not see the rows is not.
- `refillEnrichmentAfterRestoreIfNeeded`: when the disk cache was missing or past its TTL on a restore, a
  background pass refills it (the shared Supabase cache answers nearly all of it), then
  `refilterChannelsWithEnrichment` (never called before), the found-franchise rebuild and a snapshot save, the
  way the web tuner's `onCacheReady` does. Cancelled by a sign-out.
- Tests: `EnrichmentCacheStoreTests` (5: harness root, TTL, broken file, merge under memory, the 12,000-row
  cost); `BundleBuildTests` gains the report's case (restored lineup, empty cache, package rebuild keeps CH 215
  with its 52 episodes; fails on main) and its counterpart (a genre channel that emptied still drops).

**Measured (simulator, `EnrichmentCacheStoreTests.testTwelveThousandRowsCost`).** 12,000 rows shaped like the
shared table (6 to 15 keywords, companies, genres, half with OMDb scores): 5.4 MB on disk, 90 ms to encode and
write, 112 ms to read and decode on a restore, 18 MB of footprint for the test's two copies (about 9 MB for the
cache alone). The library snapshot's own size and load time are unchanged; the cache is a separate file.

**Not changed.** No studio fallback on the networks rule (it would undo f134d3df). The library snapshot format is
unchanged; the cache is its own file, read by nothing else.

**From the review.** `dependsOnEnrichment` also counts `ratingMin` (it falls back to the IMDb rating, and on Emby
the native rating can be null for a whole library, so the 13 ratingMin channels are enrichment-dependent there).
`loadLibrary` cancels a refill still in flight, and a cancelled pass stops after the Supabase step rather than
falling through to TMDB for every id; chosen over "skip the refill when the restore is stale" because a stale
restore's `refreshLibraryIfChanged` may decide not to reload (unchanged, under 24h), which would leave the cache
empty for the session, the very hole this closes, and because RESCAN and the daily check are loads too.

**Not yet checked.** Persistence of `enrichment_cache_v1.json` on a real Apple TV. The simulator once showed the
snapshot and the old enrichment cache persisting when the device did not (`LocalStore.swift`); this file goes
through the same `LocalStore` root, but only a device run proves it.

**Next.** On a TV: restore, delete the file, relaunch, confirm "no cached rows after restore, refilling" and that
CH 215 stays through the refilter; and a RESCAN while a refill is running, to see the cancel line.

## 2026-11-04 (Apple TV: the TV stays awake on the loading screen; what Plex changes at 15,000 movies, measured)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `appletv/n033-load-awake` off main `66fd72c9`, for the next Apple TV build (N-033).

**Changed.** `ScreenAwakePolicy` is the one answer RootView writes to tvOS's idle timer: playback, or a foreground
load (first load, RESCAN) with a sign-in. A background refresh never holds it. Released on the guide, the error
screen and sign-out. 10 tests. Before, only playback held the timer, so a first load longer than the TV's Sleep
After setting could end in a sleeping TV: the basement TV is set to 15 minutes and last night's 11-minute cold
load only just beat it.

**Measured.** The cold Plex harness grew nine Plex-shape knobs and a two-section server, each run alone at
15,000 movies with the enrichment cache warm, so the pool build is the stage under test: 37 s baseline, 41 s with
non-ASCII titles, 54 s with 1,500 to 3,000 character summaries (the two Christmas channels read every one), 73 s
with the library in two sections (30,000 items, since the dedupe only drops a same-server same-ratingKey copy).
Nothing superlinear, every tick taken by the main actor at once, peak 250 to 383 MB. The build order is
channels.json order, so "Channel 60 of 142" means CERTIFIED GOLD done and OSCAR WINNERS in flight, about 0.5 s
here (its 100-entry title list against 15,000 titles). The Plex collections scan does not run for a new user,
because no collection package is on; franchise discovery does, but after the pool build.

**Not reproduced.** The stall at 60 of 142. After parsing, nothing Plex-shaped makes the pool build stall. If it
is real on the reporter's Apple TV 4K (2021, A12), it is in something only that device shows: the main actor not
taking a tick, memory, or thermal. An A12 turns a 37 s build into minutes, not an hour.

**Next.** The reporter's answers (does the counter move, how many sections). The harness through the UI on a real
Apple TV with the `longSummaries,twoSections` shape, reading tick hops and main-thread blocks. Roku never holds off the
screensaver during a load; one stick check of a long load under it is owed.

## 2026-11-03 (Roku: after a power loss, the first channel plays while the library loads, #155)

**Why.** The saved guide, pools and library live in `cachefs:`, which is RAM. A TV that loses power
comes back to a full scan behind the loading screen, which is what #155's reports describe. Agreed on
#155: a playable seed, one channel for as many hours as fit in 10 KB, a hand-over to
the full guide that doesn't restart what's playing, and the loading screen again if it runs out.

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/guide/ColdBootSeed.brs`: the seed. Each build and each new hour write the first
  channel's airings from the one on now, as many whole ones as fit in 10,240 bytes, each the guide
  block less its summary, to registry section `seed`, keyed to the build, only when it changed.
- `LibraryTask`: a launch with no saved guide and no saved pools plays the seed's channel and loads
  as a first load (not `shown`), so a failure or a stop is a first load's and its guide is always
  handed over.
- `GuideView`: on the seed's guide, SETTINGS and the sidebar say STILL LOADING YOUR LIBRARY, and the
  seed's last airing ending sets `seedEnded`. `MainScene` then puts the loading screen back; a load
  error takes the seed's guide down to show it; a launch deep link waits for the full guide; the
  LaunchGuard marker stays for the seed's load.
- Sign-out clears the seed with the other caches (`NxClearSeed`). 31 cases in
  `roku/tests/ColdBootSeedTests.brs`.

**Pressed** on the 43S45 with the lab Emby (5,509 items) and a scratch switch that deleted the
`cachefs:` files at launch: the seed's channel tuned 1.0 s after the launch, and the full guide went up
about 25 s later with the same film still playing. The run-out, the load error and the SETTINGS note
behaved as above. Details in `roku/docs/PORTING.md` § After a power loss.

**Registry room** (asked on #182). A throwaway build on the 43S45 filled its own registry sections
with a heavy setup: 5 Plex servers and the picker's copy, 40 bundles, 100 franchises on and 100 off, and
300 collections on (15,001 bytes of ids). Space is charged at far less than a value's length (those ids
took 1,656), so values look stored compressed. From 32,273 bytes free, the setup took 3,593 and a
10,211-byte seed of random hex text 2,864, leaving 25,816. With the seed in
place, 3,000 collections (about 150 KB of ids) still wrote, with 12,026 free. A real seed wasn't on hand
to measure, but even stored uncompressed it would leave about 18 KB here, so the seed has no reserve check.

**Open.** The seed holds the first channel, where every launch opens (Chad on #182: opening on the last
channel watched is a separate decision). Not tried: a real power cut, a Plex sign-in, the hourly
re-save, the sidebar and a deep link on the seed's guide.

## 2026-11-03 (Roku: a Music Videos library on Jellyfin or Emby loads its MusicVideo items)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. On main since 2026-11-04, pushed together with the web tuner's copy of this fix
(`web/1030-fixes`) so the `roku` job never went red. Tested off-device and on a Roku stick. Reaches users in the
next Roku build.

**Why.** Jellyfin and Emby file the videos in a Music Videos library as `MusicVideo`. The Roku scan, like the web
tuner's and the Apple TV's, asked every library that is not TV for `IncludeItemTypes=Movie`, so such a library
came back empty and HIGH ROTATION never filled. A contributor measured it on Jellyfin 12.4.0 (PR #151): `Movie`
returns 0 items, `MusicVideo` returns 4.

**Changed.**
- `roku/source/mediabrowser/MediaBrowserLibrary.brs`: new `NxMbItemTypesFor`. A library whose type is
  `musicvideos` is asked for `Movie,MusicVideo` (a clip someone filed as a film still loads). Movies, mixed
  (no type), home videos and every other type are asked for `Movie`, as before. TV is unchanged (`Series`, then
  `Episode`). The second page of a library asks for the same types as the first. The library's type still stamps
  its items `librarySource: "musicVideo"`, which is what HIGH ROTATION's channel rule reads.
- `roku/tests/fixtures/mediabrowser-server.json`: four MusicVideo clips in the Music Videos library (one with no
  genres, one with a year and a play count, one with two genres), and one MusicVideo filed in the Movies library,
  which must stay off the film channels.
- `roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` and the test's fixture server read `IncludeItemTypes` as a comma list, as
  the servers do. Before, a request for `Movie,MusicVideo` matched nothing.
- `roku/tests/MediaBrowserTests.brs`: new `NxRunMusicVideoTypeTests`, 110 cases, run for both Jellyfin and
  Emby. It checks what each library is asked for, that every clip loads stamped as a music video and passes
  HIGH ROTATION through the real filter, that a MusicVideo in a Movies library stays out, the bug as reported
  (a library of MusicVideo items only fills HIGH ROTATION), and 201 clips across two pages.

**The vector comparison.** The web tuner's scan makes the vectors the Roku suite is held to. While this branch
waited for the web fix, the suite read the port's `Movie,MusicVideo` request as `Movie` and left the four clips
out of the item-by-item comparison. With both fixes on main the vectors hold the clips, so that allowance came out
in the same push: the loop holds the port to the web's items for them field by field, and the check "vectors hold
the MusicVideo clips" fails if a later web change stops asking for them.

**Not changed, on purpose.**
- HIGH ROTATION's genre channels (#105) stay parked. Only the item type changed.
- The title cleanup. `parseTitle` in `scripts/nostalgex-music-brainz.js` leaves `Song ( Music )` for
  `Song (Official Music Video)` and `Song ( )` for `Song (Official Video)`, and the port matches it. It needs an
  engine change (JS, Swift and the port together), so it is not folded in here. The new clips avoid the suffix so
  the tests don't pin it.
- Plex. The bug is the Jellyfin and Emby item type, which the Plex scan does not use.

**Verified.**
- `bash roku/tests/run.sh`: ALL TESTS PASSED, 54 parts. mediabrowser 5,883 passed, music video item type 110
  passed, stall 22 passed.
- The same suite on the stick (`scripts/deploy.sh --test`): ALL TESTS PASSED, the same three counts.
- The bug put back (the scan asking `Movie` again, everything else kept): 24 cases fail and 48 pass (the checks
  that need a loaded clip do not run), among them "a library of MusicVideo items only loads all of them" (0 of 4)
  and "HIGH ROTATION fills from it" (0 of 4). The 5,883 vector comparisons still pass.
- Main plus the web tuner's fix plus this change, in a scratch copy: mediabrowser 5,987 passed, 0 failed, music
  video 110. The four clips match the web scan's field by field.
- Main plus the web tuner's fix without this change: 616 mediabrowser cases fail. That is the `roku` job going
  red if the web fix merges alone.
- The pushed main (web fix, this change, the allowance removed): mediabrowser 5,988 passed, 0 failed, music video
  item type 110 passed.

**Not verified.** Against a live Jellyfin or Emby server: the tests run saved answers, and the 0 and 4 above are
the contributor's. Android's scan test (PR #151) reads the same vectors, which now hold the four clips, so its scan
has to ask a music video library for `MusicVideo` too or it goes red on rebase. Not checked against its code.

**Next.** Ship it in the next Roku build. Check a real Jellyfin or Emby Music Videos library.

  intermittent and the unfixed build was not rerun on the TV, so this shows the fix under the failing
  condition rather than proving it.

LANGUAGE and Music Videos are not checked against a real Jellyfin or Emby server (the lab servers were down).

## 2026-11-03 (Apple TV: harness isolation, and a cold first load of a 15,000-movie Plex library)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. On main since 2026-11-04 for the next Apple TV build: `915d20a` (isolation),
`5b2a0ae` (cold Plex harness).

**Why.** A 1.0.29 report: a Plex library of about 15,000 movies stops at "Channel 60 of 142" on the loading
screen and the app closes about an hour later (N-033). The earlier scale harness handed the app a ready library
and a filled enrichment cache, which skips most of what a new user's first load does on the network, and the
next measurement has to run on a real Apple TV. The harnesses could not run there: they cleared the app's real
library snapshot, schedules and settings.

**Changed.**
- `HarnessIsolation` (DEBUG only): while active, the app's files, settings (every `UserDefaults.standard` now
  goes through `AppDefaults.standard`, plain `.standard` in a release build), credentials (in memory, never the
  Keychain), iCloud sync (an in-memory store, and a harness's AppState never takes over the shared one) and HTTP
  cache stay under `Library/Caches/NostalgexHarness/<name>`. `TEST_RUNNER_NOSTALGEX_HARNESS_ROOT` turns it on
  first thing at launch, so on a device the test host's own launch stays off the real stores too. A Release
  build carries none of it (checked with `nm` and `strings`).
- `RealStoreFingerprint` hashes the real stores from their real paths; a harness run compares before and after.
- `ColdPlexScaleHarness`: the real first load against a fake Plex, a fake Supabase cache, a fake TMDB proxy that
  rate-limits, and OMDb, with times per stage and per channel, the main actor's delay on each "Channel N of M"
  tick (a new probe mark, only when a harness listens), memory, threads and requests per endpoint, then an
  optional soak with the guide up. A 300-movie version runs in the normal suite as the isolation proof.

**Measured (simulator).** 15,000 movies, nothing cached: first load 664.5 s. Plex 42.4 s for 30 pages;
enrichment 586.1 s (15,000 TMDB requests at about 27 a second, then 75 upserts taking about 28 s); pool build
34.9 s for 142 channels, slowest 1.8 s, pools 59 to 61 at 158, 158 and 439 ms; the main actor took every tick
at once; peak 248 MB, 17 threads. Through the UI with a 2-minute soak (2,000 movies): memory flat at 83 MB,
12 threads, no requests after the first 30 s. Real stores: no difference in any app-owned store in either run.
Outside them, CFNetwork's `Library/HTTPStorages` database (its rows unchanged) and AVFoundation's
`tmp/MediaCache` index changed; neither holds the app's data.

**Not reproduced.** The stall at "Channel 60 of 142" and the close after an hour did not happen in the
simulator, cold or warm. While a cold load enriches, the screen says "Fetching metadata", not "Channel N";
the channel count only shows during the pool build, which took 35 s here.

**Fixed before the push (2026-11-04, from the review).**
- `HarnessIsolationTests` skips when isolation is already on and only turns off what it turned on. Before, a
  whole-target run on a TV under `TEST_RUNNER_NOSTALGEX_HARNESS_ROOT` switched isolation off in this class, and
  the classes after it alphabetically cleared the TV's real library snapshot and manifests.
  `HarnessIsolationPreexistingTests` proves an active isolation survives it (all 7 checks fail on the old guard).
- AUDIO LANGUAGE is read through `AppDefaults.standard`, where Settings writes it, and `JellyfinAudioLanguageTests`
  uses it too, so a harness run on a TV never touches the real setting. A Release build is unchanged.
- The unused `serverName` parameter of `PlexAPIService.bestReachableURI` is gone.
- NostalgexTests: 1,086 tests, 1,060 passed, 0 failed, 26 skipped.

**Next.** The same run on the basement Apple TV 4K (3rd generation), through the UI with a 60-minute soak
(tester). Not covered: Plex collections (no collection package is on in a new lineup, so the scan never ran),
a real Plex server's own speed, and artwork, which a load never fetches.

## 2026-11-03 (Apple TV: a 15,000-movie Emby library no longer reads as a dead server)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. On main since 2026-11-04 for the next Apple TV build.

**Why.** A #support report on 1.0.29: an Emby library of about 15,000 movies, every one with genres and a TMDB match, never finished loading, and the same library on Plex stopped at "Channel 60 of 142" with the app closing about an hour in.

**Measured.**
- The channel engine is not slow at this size. `MovieLibraryScaleHarness` (new) drives the real `loadLibrary` with a synthetic movie-only library shaped like the report: every title with a TMDB id and a cached enrichment row, a third of the ids taken from the membership manifest, 15% in a TMDB collection. M4 Pro simulator, Debug build, all 142 channel pools: 2k movies 4.8 s, 5k 12.3 s, 10k 24.2 s, 15k 36.5 s. Linear, about 2.4 ms per movie for the whole lineup. Slowest channels at 15k: CHRISTMAS SPECIALS and KIDS CHRISTMAS TV (1.9 s each, their episode rules read every movie's summary), APPLE TV+ 0.8 s. Peak memory 178 MB (204 MB with every package on). The guide's schedules for 95 channels: 60 ms. Through the real `RootView` (loading screen and guide on screen): first load 39.8 s, guide then sat for 10 minutes at a flat 186 to 191 MB, RESCAN 38.2 s. Nothing near an hour, no growth.
- The Emby scan was the failure. Against a fake Emby (15,000 movies, 200 a page, 3 s a page) through the real `EmbyAPIService` and the stall watch: the scan's item count stayed at 0 for the whole section, because Emby and Jellyfin only reported progress when a section started (Plex reports every page). STOP WAITING appeared at 65 s and the watch abandoned the scan at 210 s with the server still answering (71 of 75 pages served). The request it cancelled then threw away the 14,200 movies already read, so the load ended on "Your server stopped sending data" with 0 items. Any single Emby or Jellyfin movie library that takes longer than 210 s to page through hits this, however healthy the server is.
- After the fix, same fake server: 15,000 items in 265.7 s, the count moving every 2 s, no STOP WAITING, guide built.

**Changed.**
- `EmbyAPIService`, `JellyfinAPIService`: a movie section reports progress after every page, as Plex does, so the stall watch sees a big library arriving. A cancel that lands while a page request is in flight keeps the pages already read (Plex already did), so a stopped scan still builds a guide from them.
- `MovieSectionScanProgressTests` (new, 2 tests): both backends, 1,000 movies over a local server. Fails on main (one progress event, and a cancel mid-page returns nothing), passes now.
- `MovieLibraryScaleHarness` (new, off by default): the measurements above. `rebuildStaticChannelPools` marks each channel through `LibraryLoadProbe` when a harness listens (no cost otherwise).
- NostalgexTests: 1,037 passed, 0 failed.

**Not explained.** The Plex half of the report. The Plex scan already reports every page, and the engine builds 142 channels from 15,000 movies in under a minute on the simulator, so "Channel 60 of 142" for an hour is not reproduced. Not measured: the same harness on a real Apple TV 4K (A12) and the enrichment phase on a first load (enrichment is off in these runs; the site's TMDB proxy answered 27 requests a second from a Mac, so 15,000 titles missing from the shared cache would be about 9 minutes). The hour matches the Apple TV's default one-hour sleep, which ends a long load; unverified.

**Next.** Run `MovieLibraryScaleHarness` on the living room Apple TV 4K (needs Chad's OK). Ask the reporter for a photo of the stuck Plex screen and his Apple TV's Sleep After setting. Web tuner and Docker: n/a, no scan watchdog there. Roku: n/a, its stall watch counts every 2xx answer as progress.

## 2026-11-03 (N-013: forced subtitles when the server cannot burn them in)

**Changed.** Test code only, on main since 2026-11-04 (from `test/n013-emby-forced-sub-burnin`). `ForcedSubtitleBurnHarness.swift`
drives `AppState.loadCurrentItem` and `selectChannel` against a lab Emby or Jellyfin. `scripts/lab-forced-subtitle/`
holds what it needs: ffmpeg-made films with a forced English track, a script that starts the lab server in colima, a
logging proxy that can answer HTTP 500 on the burn-in stream only, and an HTTP probe. No product code changed.

**Why.** The app asks the server to burn a forced track into the picture (a second PlaybackInfo with
`SubtitleStreamIndex` and Encode subtitle profiles). A unit test cannot show whether the app copes when the server
cannot.

**Measured.** Lab Emby 4.10.1.0 in a Linux container, lab Jellyfin 12.2.0, tvOS 26.1 simulator, main at 6a2d6df7.
- A healthy server burns the track and the film plays in 0.3 to 0.9 s (a 4K film 1.6 s). The `Key: threads` failure
  seen on a macOS Emby 4.10.1.0 did not reproduce in the container: 10-bit, HDR10 and burn-in all transcode there.
- With HTTP 500 injected on the burn stream's segments (master and variant answer 200, as the failing server did),
  AVPlayer retries the first segment six times in 16 s and never fails the item. At 20.4 s the watchdog asks for a
  stream with no burn and the film plays at 20.7 to 21.3 s, without its forced lines. Same on Jellyfin's fMP4 with the
  init segment refused. A channel of such films sat in loading for 20.8 s per programme; the failure count stayed 0.
- 500 on the burn PlaybackInfo request: the app uses the unburned answer and plays at 0.9 s. 500 on the variant
  playlist: the error card at 0.9 s.
- The 4 s fail-fast check never fires in the simulator: the player's error log holds `-16847 HTTP 500` events and no `uri`.
- On Emby and Jellyfin the watchdog is always 20 s, never the 40 s a UHD source gets, because only the Plex loader sets
  `videoWidth` and `videoHeight`.

**Half-done.** Not run on a device, so AVPlayer's give-up time (31.5 s in the simulator) and error code on a real Apple
TV are unknown. Not run against the macOS Emby the bug was seen on; `server-login.py` then `probe-burn.py` is the
check. Image subtitles (PGS, VobSub) were not tested.

**Fix check.** `fix/forced-burn-probe` (a27928c4, probes the burn stream's first segment before choosing it) was
cherry-picked onto this main in a throwaway worktree and run through the same harness, nothing committed from it.
- 500 on the burn segments: the six burn films play in 0.4 to 1.0 s on the plain stream (20.7 to 21.3 s before). The
  refused session is stopped at +0.16 s. A channel of forced films starts each programme in 0.3 to 1.0 s (20.8 s before).
- 500 on the variant playlist: plays in 1.0 s (the error card before). On Jellyfin with the init segment refused:
  0.6 to 1.0 s (20.8 s before).
- Healthy servers: films with no burn are unchanged (0.3 s). Burn films start about 0.1 to 0.4 s later. A 4K burn on
  Jellyfin in a 2-CPU VM starts in 3.5 s against 1.4 s, because the probe waits for the first burned segment.

**Done 2026-11-04.** `fix/forced-burn-probe` is on main for the next Apple TV build, applied on top of AUDIO LANGUAGE
(I-070), which changed the same function: the burned stream keeps the chosen audio language too.

## 2026-11-04 (Android: the 4K out-of-memory crash, and the Plex server picker)

**Why.** Chad tested release 3 on a Google TV (PR #151). Two of his findings are fixed here.
- A 4K HDR film played for about 15 seconds, then the app ran out of memory. The TV caps an app's Java heap at 192 MB.
- After Plex sign-in, the app never asked which server to use. The Apple TV asks when the account reaches more than one.

**Changed.**
- **The player's buffer is capped at a quarter of the heap the app may use** (`Playback.bufferBytes`), and the manifest asks for `largeHeap`.
  - Media3's default for a network video is 2,000 x 64 KB, about 128 MB, held as Java byte arrays in the same heap as the library.
  - A quarter is 48 MB at 192 MB, 96 MB at 384 MB and 128 MB at 512 MB.
  - Measured on an Android 16 Google TV emulator (192 MB heap, 384 MB with `largeHeap`) with an 80 Mbps test file in demo mode, the library a few demo items:

    | Build | Peak Java heap |
    |---|---|
    | Default buffer | 169 MB of 192 |
    | Cap alone | 72 MB of 192 |
    | Cap with `largeHeap` | 124 MB of 384 |

  - On a SHIELD with a library of about 11,400 titles, the Java heap is 45 MB with nothing playing and about 70 MB while a 1080p film plays in the guide.
- **Stalls, measured.** With 300 Mbps and an 8-second dropout every 30 seconds, on the same file:

  | Build | Stalls |
  |---|---|
  | Default buffer | none |
  | Cap with `largeHeap` (96 MB) | none |
  | Cap alone (48 MB) | one per dropout |

  So the small buffer only applies on a TV that refuses `largeHeap`, where the choice is a stall on a long Wi-Fi dropout or running out of memory.
- **Plex sign-in finds every reachable server, owned and shared, as the Apple TV does.** Before, it looked only for owned servers (the Roku port's rule) and used all of them without asking. With more than one, it shows the Apple TV's `ServerPickerView`:
  - the same heading, words and rows ("Your server" or "Shared with you", INCLUDED or OFF);
  - owned servers ticked, or all of them if none is owned;
  - focus on CONTINUE.

  The plex.tv token is saved only with the chosen servers, as on the Apple TV. Checked on the emulator with an account that reaches two servers: both ticked, and turning one off gave a library choice from the other alone.

**Not checked.** The fix has not been run against Chad's film or on his TV, and the crash itself was not reproduced, only the memory it ran out of. The library's own memory still grows with its size; trimming what is kept per title needs a heap dump from a debug build first.

**Next.** TRUE CRIME playing one title over and over, Chad's third finding, is not a threshold difference. Its `minItems` has been 1 since 1.0.21, all three apps check `itemPool.count >= minItems`, and Android passes all 148 `filter-golden.json` cases, 36 of them with keywords. So the Android build found a match that the Apple TV didn't for the same library. That needs the title's genres and keywords from Chad, and whether his Android build has enrichment on.
