## 2026-11-03 (Roku: the Jellyfin and Emby scan test follows the web's audioStreams)

**Shipped.** On main as `692492a`, 2026-11-03. Test code only.

**Why.** Web tuner 1.0.13 (`4602216`, #176) put `audioStreams` on every Jellyfin and Emby movie and episode.
`roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` writes the web scan's items into the vectors the Roku suite is held to, and
`MediaBrowserTests.brs` compared every key of a web item with the Roku item's key of the same name. The port has
no `audioStreams`: it keeps the same tracks as `audioTracks` (index, language, channels, codec), and only for a
file with two or more. So 222 of the suite's 5,882 mediabrowser cases failed, one per scanned item, all on that
field. The `roku` job on main failed on `4602216` (it passed on `f083748` before it). The runs after it look
green because the job was skipped on them: `be6254a` and `72f958e` touch only docs, the relay and a smoke
script, none of which that job watches. The next push that touches `roku/` or the engine would have shown red.

**Changed.** `roku/tests/MediaBrowserTests.brs`. The web's `audioStreams` is now compared with the port's
`audioTracks`: the same index, language, channels and codec in the same order for a file with two or more
tracks, and no `audioTracks` for a file with fewer. The web's `title` and the port's `isDefault` have no
counterpart and are not read. One more check fails if the vectors hold no item with two or more `audioStreams`,
so a generator that drops the field cannot turn the comparison into a pass on nothing. The suite reads
5,883 passed, 0 failed (222 field checks replaced by 222 track checks, plus that one).

**Not changed, on purpose.**
- `roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` still emits `audioStreams`. Android's `MediaBrowserScanTest` (PR #151)
  reads it from that output and compares it with the Kotlin scan's tracks, and the generator is in that PR's
  CI filter. Removing the field there would leave that test comparing an empty list with real tracks.
- The port takes no second copy of the track list. The web measured +26% on the saved library for it (+4.9 MB
  at 20,000 films), and nothing on Roku would read it. The Roku never had the #176 bug: its AUDIO LANGUAGE pick
  comes from `audioTracks` (it sends the server stream's `AudioStreamIndex`, or on a direct play names the
  track to select in the player's list), and FOREIGN AUDIO subtitles read the player's `availableAudioTracks`
  (`GuideView.brs`). Read from the code, not re-checked on the stick.

**Verified.** Reproduced on `be6254a` first: `mediabrowser cases: 5660 passed, 222 failed`, every failure on
`audioStreams`. Three deliberate breaks, each restored: a port that reports the wrong channel count, a port that
keeps single-track files, and vectors with `audioStreams` removed. Each fails the suite. The vectors from
`gen-vectors.mjs` are byte-identical before and after this change, since the generator, `plex-tuner.html` and
the fixture are untouched.

**Not verified.** Android's Gradle tests were not run; PR #151 has merge conflicts with main, and its inputs
(the generator, the fixture, `plex-tuner.html`) are unchanged by this branch.

**Next.** Merge this to turn the `roku` job green on main, then rebase #180 and #181 on it.

## 2026-11-03 (Android: Back on Android 16 stays in the app, and versionCode 3)

**Why.** Reported by Chad on his Google TV: Back from full screen, or from a Settings page, closed the app instead of going to the guide (as on the Roku) or up a level in Settings. The app targets API 36, and on Android 16 that turns on predictive back. The remote's Back is then never sent to the app as `KEYCODE_BACK`, which every screen's Back handling listened for. It goes to the `OnBackPressedDispatcher`, and with nothing registered there the activity finishes. To confirm the cause, the same build with `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false"` in the manifest went from full screen to the guide on the Android 16 emulator. That opt-out was only a test and was not kept, because a later Android drops it.

**Changed.**
- `ui/Back.kt` adds `Modifier.onBack(enabled, action)`. It registers a `BackHandler` for Android 16 and keeps the key check for older versions. A key the check consumes never reaches the dispatcher, so only one of the two runs.
- The guide (full screen, its strip and panel, Settings, the package sidebar, the invite's question, STILL WATCHING?), Settings over a status screen, the connect screens, and START OVER's question all use it. Before, each of these left the app on Android 16.
- `versionCode` is 3.

Measured in demo mode on Google TV emulators running Android 16 and Android 14, and on a SHIELD running Android 11. The SHIELD used a real library, and on it only the full-screen and Settings steps were checked:
- Full screen goes to the guide.
- The STREAM QUALITY picker goes to PLAYBACK & PICTURE, then the Settings menu, then the guide on the live row.
- Back on the live row leaves the app, as before.
- On Android 16, CONNECT TO JELLYFIN goes back to the server choice, and Back on the server choice leaves the app.

**Not checked.** Chad has not tried the fix on his Google TV yet. Back from START OVER's question was not pressed on any device.

items of 5,404) and exited 0. Plex's log shows the cause: the first page of Movies took Plex

and Plex logged the request as "Completed after connection close". The loader catches each
section's and each show's error, warns and goes on without it, and
`roku/tests/live/plex-loader.mjs` silenced those warnings. It refused only an empty library, so a
library without Movies passed. `compare.mjs` and `collections.mjs` load through the same
`loadLibrary`.

**Changed.** `loadLibrary` keeps the loader's warnings and stops when there are any, listing each
one with the fetch error's code. The loader itself is unchanged.

**Measured.** Against a real Plex library: a clean load keeps 5,404 items, and
`dump-library.mjs` writes them. With the Movies page fetch failing as a timeout does, it stops
with `Failed to fetch section Movies: fetch failed (UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT)` after 4,635 items,
the short library's count; one show's episodes failing stops it at 5,400; a missing loader
global stops it at 0. `collections.mjs` still matches upstream. The slow page didn't happen
again in 15 loads.

## 2026-11-02 (Roku: a background refresh that builds no channels keeps the guide on screen)

**Why.** Left open by #96: a refresh that comes back with no channels while a guide with channels
is on screen. `GuideView` put up NO CHANNELS FOUND but kept the tuned channel, the airing and the
clock, so the airing's end crashed the app in `NxAdvancePick` (`Advance.brs` 169, `channels`
empty). Left/Right in full screen takes a `mod` by the channel count, which is 0 then: a crash
too, by reading the code.

**Changed.** `LibraryTask` drops that refresh the way it already drops one that reaches no server
or can't read the library: the guide on screen stays (`keepSavedGuide`), and the saved library,
guide and pools aren't replaced, so the next launch shows that guide too. Only the background
refresh's builds do this (the launch refresh, the 15-minute check, RESCAN LIBRARY); a package
switch is unchanged. The Apple TV differs: an empty channel list replaces its tuner with NO
CHANNELS FOUND (`Plex90App.swift`). The cost: a dropped refresh is silent, and RESCAN LIBRARY's
row keeps its old "Last updated" time. Still open, by reading the code: a package switch built in
place that leaves no channels (the last package on fills nothing) hands `GuideView` an empty list
the same way.

**Measured.** On our 43" TCL (43S45, Roku OS 16.0.4), test-data builds signed in to the lab Emby
as a user whose library made one channel (CH 7 VHS VAULT, five 1990 clips), RESCAN LIBRARY after
the library stopped filling it:
- Main (`0a810fb`), the five clips taken off the server: the guide said NO CHANNELS FOUND while
  CH 7 kept playing, and the airing's end crashed the app as above.
- This branch (`9e85fb3`), the five clips moved to 2026 in Emby (same files and ids): six items
  read, no channels, `background refresh built no channels; the guide on screen stays`, and no
  save. CH 7 played on, the airing's end moved to the next clip (picture in 1.0 s), and a
  relaunch opened on the saved guide's CH 7.

`tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED; no off-device test runs `LibraryTask`, so the TV runs
are the check.

Before, the web's items had none, so the field was skipped. All 222 items in the shared fixture match, two of them with several tracks. ## 2026-11-02 (Web tuner and Docker 1.0.13: Jellyfin and Emby items keep their audio tracks, #176)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `web/tuner-1.0.13`, cut from `origin/main` at `f083748`, not pushed. It
carries the fix for #176 and the `tunerVersion` bump to 1.0.13 that the Docker release needs. The parity
bundle (WATERSHED, GUIDE TEXT SIZE, the faster Plex connect, the failure card) is already on main.

**Why.** @owenvoke found it while porting the Jellyfin and Emby audio track choice to Android (PR #151).
The scan's `mediaInfo` read every audio stream of a file into `audioStreams`, but the movie and the
episode items it built took only `subtitles`, so on the web tuner and in Docker
`pickAudioStream(item.audioStreams || [])` always saw an empty list. AUDIO LANGUAGE was ignored on Jellyfin
and Emby, and the foreign-audio subtitle fallback (`shouldAutoEnableSubs`) never switched on there.

**Changed.**
- Both item types, movie and episode, now carry `audioStreams: mi.audioStreams`. Nothing else reads
  `audioStreams`: `pickAudioStream` (the `AudioStreamIndex` in the PlaybackInfo body and on a direct
  stream's URL), `shouldAutoEnableSubs`, and `loadSubtitleForCurrentItem`. All three already expected the
  field. The shape is `mediaInfo`'s, unchanged: `index`, `lang`, `codec`, `channels`, `title`.
- No change to the library cache version. A library saved before this fix has no audio tracks until its
  24 hour refresh, or until a sign-out and back in; a version bump would make every user (Plex too)
  rescan on first load. AUDIO LANGUAGE therefore starts working within a day of the update.
- Not changed: an MP4 that direct plays and has several audio tracks. A direct stream is the file as it
  is, and a browser cannot switch its tracks, so its default track plays. A file the server has to
  transcode (an MKV, which is most multi-language files) plays the track that was asked for. Not
  measured against a real server.

**Verified.** New `scripts/jellyfin-audio-streams-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:jellyfin-audio:browser`,
24 checks, headless Chromium, a Jellyfin-shaped and an Emby-shaped server that record every request): a
scanned movie and a scanned episode carry their tracks; AUDIO LANGUAGE Auto asks for no track; English,
picked in Settings by click, asks for the English track (index 2, the file's default is French), then German
(3), then French on an episode (1); a film with audio only in French and German asks for its English
subtitles by itself, a film with an English track does not. origin/main's page fails 14 of the 24.
Library cache growth, measured with `CACHE_MEASURE=20000` on the same smoke (20,000 films, three audio and
two subtitle tracks each, a 350 character summary): the saved library goes from 18.7 MB to 23.6 MB of JSON
(934 to 1,179 bytes an item, +26%, +4.9 MB), and the load takes the same time (14.6 s both). A film with
one audio track adds about a third of that. IndexedDB has no 5 MB ceiling (#152), so this stays inside it.

**Not verified.** A real Jellyfin or Emby server with a multi-language file; Safari's own track switching.

**Next.** `roku/tests/gen-mediabrowser.mjs` vectors and Android's scan comparison can include `audioStreams`
again, as the issue says.

and the web tuner has had START OVER since 2026-10-23 ("Roku has no START OVER on its loading screen yet;
that's a port"). On the Roku, * already signed out during a load, but its hint sat under the
loading screen, so nobody could see it, and it didn't ask first.

**Changed.** Branch `roku-start-over` (tydude001), off main at `03c7ae9` (1.0.10).
- `source/util/LaunchGuard.brs` (new): upstream's unfinished-load half of `LaunchGuard.swift`, over
  a `launch` registry section. A marker for a load the viewer waits on (no guide on screen),
  cleared on any end the app sees; a saved guide shown first, or a load the app stops (a rejected
  Plex sign-in drops it), clears it without resetting the count.

  FINISH (OK tries again, * starts over) instead of a third load. On the loading screen the first *
  arms START OVER, a second signs out, OK or Back disarms. A sign-out clears the marker and count.
- `LoadingView`: `* START OVER` near the bottom for the whole load, and upstream's confirm text
  once armed (`startOverArmed`, `serverName`), in its own group so the stack isn't rebuilt.
- `tests/LaunchGuardTests.brs`: 17 cases, transcribed from `LaunchGuardTests.swift`, plus the
  registry side of `StartOverTests`.

**Measured.** `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED (launch guard 17 passed). Pressed on our 43"
TCL (43S45, OS 16.0.4) with a scratch build of this branch on its first base, `54cb410` (a 40 s hold in the library step,
saved guides off; the rebase onto `03c7ae9` brought only the EMAIL keyboard fix and the version), signed in to the lab Emby: the confirm, OK and Back keeping the load; Home mid-load
twice read 1 then 2 in a row and the third launch asked without loading; a load that finished
just before Home counted nothing; OK loaded, ** signed out to CONNECT YOUR SERVER, and the next launch read 0.
That run came before one review change (a load the app stops clears the marker too), which none
of its steps reach except START OVER, whose sign-out clears it anyway. Details in
`roku/docs/PORTING.md` (A way out of a load).

wasn't tried). Not run on a Streaming Stick.

## 2026-11-02 (Roku: kbps rounding floors only a Double or a Float, #160 follow-up)

**Why.** Chad's merge note on #160: `NxMbBitrateKbps` skipped `Int()` only for a list of
whole-number types, so a Double still went through it and a boxed `roInt` wasn't in the list.
On a TV `Int()` goes through a Float (`Int(19269499)` is 19269500), so anything left on that path
can round a bitrate wrong.

**Changed.** The check is flipped: a Double is floored by `NxFloorDouble`, which never calls
`Int()` on the whole value, a Float still goes through `Int()` (it can't hold 19269499 anyway),
and every other number is taken as it is. Five cases in `tests/MediaBrowserTests.brs`: a Double
with a fraction, a whole Double, an `roInt`, and 20000499 and 20000500 bps, which round to 20000
and 20001, either side of `NxMbVideoQuery`'s line: over 20,000 kbps it sends
`AllowVideoStreamCopy=false`.

**Measured.** `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED, mediabrowser 5660 (5655 before), but the
interpreter's `Int()` is exact, so these cases pass there either way. On our 55" TCL (55R617, Roku
OS 15.3.4), `scripts/deploy.sh --test` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED, mediabrowser 5660 passed, 0 failed.

## 2026-11-02 (Roku 1.0.11: Roku's email screen is asked for on a button, not as the sign-in screen opens)

**Shipped.** Goes out in Roku 1.0.11, to the beta and the public app, with tydude001's #173, #174 and #175 (their own entries are below).

**Why.** Roku's automated behavior analysis ran on the public app (1.0.10). Sign In and Sign Out passed; launch
performance, deep linking and content play errored, each with the connect screen as the active element, and the
launch beacon absent. The sign-in script never got the TV signed in. 1.0.9 and 1.0.10 asked Roku for the account
email (`getUserData`, certification RP 2.1 and RP 4.1) the moment USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD opened, and Roku's own
Sign in screen is not on our clock. Timed on one Streaming Stick Plus, same build: under a second, then 25.5 to
25.8 s in seven tries over five minutes, then 0.7 s. A recorded script presses OK on a timer, so it needs the
screen to be where it expects it: with the screen simulated 5 s late the script ended on the connect screen, never
reaching plex.tv; 15 s late it works only if the script waits longer than that; 25 s late it ended inside Roku's
Privacy policy dialog. A person typing a password would get the same screen dropped over the keyboard.

**Changed.** The ask moved from opening the screen to a button, USE MY ROKU EMAIL, under SIGN IN. It says
WAITING FOR ROKU... until Roku answers. Sharing still fills the EMAIL field only, and nothing else about the
sign-in changed. `getUserData` is still called from `ConnectView.brs`, so static analysis still sees it.

**Not verified.** That this was the cause of the result on Roku's lab device: no log from it exists. The result is
consistent with it (no sign-in reached plex.tv), and the mechanism reproduces on the stick.

**Next.** Package, upload to the public app, re-run Roku's behavior analysis. The privacy page line about the Roku
email names USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD and needs the new button's name.

## 2026-11-02 (Web tuner and Docker: the playback failure card shows in the split view)

**Shipped.** To the hosted tuner on nostalgex.app 2026-11-02, from `web/parity-bundle`. Docker gets it in the next
`tuner-v` tag (`tunerVersion` stays 1.0.12 until then). Branch `web/failure-card-split-view`, cut from `origin/main` at `03c7ae9`.

**Why.** Found while building the WATERSHED card (branch `web/watershed-switch`). The failure card
("This one wouldn't play", amber when the server is at fault, red when the browser is) and the
connection errors ("NOT CONNECTED. RECONNECT YOUR SERVER") are drawn inside `.channel-display`. The
split view, the default at every size, hides that block with
`.player-screen.layout-side .channel-display { display: none !important; }`. Measured at desktop
and phone sizes: the card has a 0 by 0 box. A programme the server would not stream was a black
picture with no reason, in the layout everyone uses, so the card, which was shipped for parity with
the Apple TV and Roku, never showed.

**Changed.** A failure or a connection error puts a `has-failure` class on `.channel-display`,
which shows the block again in the split view and hides the text display's title lines behind it.
`clearVideoError` takes the class off, so the split view is as it was, and `signOut` calls it, so a card from
one session is not on screen over the next sign-in. The full view is unchanged.

**Verified.** New `scripts/failure-card-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:failure-card:browser`,
headless Chromium, a Jellyfin-shaped server that refuses every video request so the page's own
recovery runs to the card) at phone, tablet, desktop and 960x540: the card is on screen inside the
picture with its headline and detail, a connection error shows the same way, clearing hides the
block again in the split view, signing out takes the card down, the full view still shows it, no page
errors: 48 checks (40 on the branch's own head `d6aa6cc`, the 8 sign-out checks added in the bundle), the same
40 on the hosted build (`dist`) and the Docker build (`dist-selfhost`) at `d6aa6cc`. Negative controls:
origin/main's page fails 16 of the 40, with the card at 0 by 0 at all four sizes; without the `signOut` line
the 4 sign-out checks fail, the card staying up over the connect screen.

**Not verified.** A real server refusing a real stream; a real TV browser; Safari. The playback
recovery ladder behind the card is unchanged and is a separate, larger gap (no 1080p step, stops
after 3 failures where the Apple TV stops after 5).

**Next.** Nothing for this change.

**Why.** Measured on a Streaming Stick Plus on 1.0.9: after Continue on Roku's own Sign in
screen, EMAIL holds the Roku account email, and opening the keyboard from EMAIL showed that
text with the cursor at the end. A sign-in script recorded in the Roku Remote Tool types its

failed, and a person who wants a different address had to delete the shared one first. Back on

(`NxRfiKeyboardStart`), and closing it with nothing typed leaves that address in place
(`NxRfiKeyboardKeep`). An address the viewer has edited opens with its text as before. Both are in
`SignInFlow.brs` with 11 cases in `SignInFlowTests.brs`; `ConnectView` calls them from
`openKeyboard` and `keyboardDone`. Nothing is sent, saved or printed that wasn't before. The
build is 1.0.10 (`build_version=10`), its own commit.

**Checked.** Off the TV: the sign-in suite (142 cases), and two deliberate breakages of the helpers each
fail the new cases. The full suite and the stick check on the 1.0.10 build are recorded in

## 2026-11-02 (Web tuner and Docker: Plex sign-in stops waiting once the answer cannot change)

**Shipped.** To the hosted tuner on nostalgex.app 2026-11-02, from `web/parity-bundle`. Docker gets it in the next
`tuner-v` tag (`tunerVersion` stays 1.0.12 until then). Branch `web/plex-lan-early-exit`, cut from `origin/main` at `54cb410`.

**Why.** `findWorkingConnection` tested every address plex.tv lists with `Promise.all` and then
took the best that answered, so a sign-in waited for the slowest address even when the home
network's answered in 30 ms, and a dead remote address cost its whole 5 s timeout every time.
`confirmMultiServerSelection` asked the servers one after another, so each server that was off
added its own wait. The Apple TV (`PlexAPIService.bestReachableURI`) and Roku
(`ServerResolve.brs:NxResolveOutcome`) stop as soon as the answer cannot change and ask every server
at once.

**Changed.**
- New `scripts/nostalgex-server-resolve.js`, the rules of the Apple TV and Roku in one pure file:
  home network first, then remote HTTPS, remote plain, relay (HTTPS first within a kind); the best
  kind that has answered wins as soon as nothing better is still waiting, so a home answer settles at
  once; a home address silent for 3 s counts as failed, but only once another address has answered;
  every probe is told to stop when the choice is made; everything still waiting at 10 s counts as
  failed. `findWorkingConnection` is that, with the same 5 s probe.
- A lone slow home address is still waited for. A seeded property check over random servers found
  my first version returning no address for a server whose only answering address replied at 3.2 s,
  which the old code connected to. The grace applies only when something else has answered. (Roku's
  `NxResolveStatus` counts a silent home address failed after its grace whether or not anything else
  has answered; not run on a stick, so unverified there.)
- An address that answers as a different Plex server is turned down, as on Roku: `/identity` must
  name the `machineIdentifier` plex.tv gave. An answer that cannot be read, or a missing identifier,
  is accepted as before. Before, the page connected to the other server's library.
- Servers are resolved together, not one after another; the list keeps the order they were picked in,
  so the first stays the primary.
- The old wait-for-everything path stays as `findWorkingConnectionWaitingForAll`, used only if the new
  script did not load.
- One difference from before that is deliberate: the home network now ranks above remote HTTPS. On
  nostalgex.app, which is https, only HTTPS addresses answer anyway; in Docker a home http address now
  wins over a remote HTTPS one, as on the Apple TV.

**Verified.** Headless Chromium, real sockets: the page signs in the way a second visit does (a
plex.tv token, plex.tv's server list served by the harness, a Plex server per address that answers,
hangs like a dead address does, or is refused). The connect phase is plex.tv's list arriving to the
first library request, median of 3 runs, and includes about 0.7 s of page work that is the same in
both:

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| home 30 ms, remote and relay dead | 5671 ms | 699 ms |
| home 30 ms, remote 300 ms, relay 1800 ms | 2474 ms | 699 ms |
| home refused, remote 150 ms, relay dead | 5668 ms | 821 ms |
| shared server, remote 150 ms, relay dead | 5673 ms | 819 ms |
| home dead, remote 150 ms, relay dead | 5668 ms | 3678 ms (the home address gets its 3 s) |
| only the relay answers (200 ms) | 871 ms | 872 ms |
| home is another Plex server, remote 150 ms | 820 ms, wrong server | 820 ms, right server |
| nothing answers | same error | same error, same time |
| three servers, each: home 30 ms, remote and relay dead | 15672 ms | 686 ms |
| two servers: first answers in 900 ms, second in 30 ms | 1606 ms | 1572 ms, the first stays the primary |
| three servers, two of them off (every address dead), one answering | 10701 ms | 5665 ms (one wait for the dead ones, not one each) |

`scripts/nostalgex-server-resolve-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:plex-resolve`, in `npm test`) runs the
engine on a virtual clock: the cases of the Apple TV's `ConnectionDiscoveryEarlyExitTests.swift`
and Roku's `ServerResolveTests.brs`, then 400 random servers, 1,988 checks. `npm test` green.
`scripts/plex-resolve-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:plex-resolve:browser`) holds the table to
bounds (46 checks), on source, the hosted build and the Docker build; origin/main's page fails 8 of them.

**Not verified.** A real Plex server and plex.tv: the addresses here are loopback sockets. Chrome's
local network access prompt, and a real `*.plex.direct` home address, were not exercised. Probes are
still `/identity` only, 5 s, no retry (the apps use `/identity` and `/library/sections`, 12 to 25 s and a
retry); the timeouts are unchanged on purpose.

**Next.** Roku: check the lone slow home address case on a stick.

## 2026-11-02 (Roku: ask for the Roku account email at sign-in, getUserData / RFI)

**Why.** Roku's static analysis gives an authenticated app an error: "All authenticated
channels must use the Request for Information (getUserData) API call to obtain a user's email
address" (RP 2.1 and RP 4.1), and an error blocks scheduling a public app. The dashboard showed
it on the 1.0.5 beta, because the listing says customers sign in; it names no exemption for a
free app. Roku's ChannelStore page says the call works for free apps and that a viewer who
declines leaves `userData` invalid. Nostalgex has no Roku Pay and no ads, and reads nothing
from the viewer's Roku account today.

**Changed.** `ConnectView` asks once per view, when the viewer opens USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD: a
ChannelStore node with `requestedUserData` "email", `requestedUserDataInfo.context` "signin" and
`command` "getUserData", which brings up Roku's own "Sign in" screen. It is asked there, on the
viewer's own press, because that is where an email is typed (Roku asks for the minimum) and
because a recorded sign-in script then meets Roku's screen at the same step every time. A viewer
on the plex.tv/link code or a Jellyfin or Emby server isn't asked. It is skipped in the sign-in
tour (`dryRun`, `discoveryFixture`). Nothing waits for the answer, so sharing or cancelling
leaves the flow as it was. A shared address only starts the EMAIL field when that field is empty.
It is kept in the view, never saved and never printed; it goes to plex.tv only if the viewer
presses SIGN IN, as anything typed there does. `NxRfiEmail` (what a `userData` holds) and
`NxRfiPrefill` are in `SignInFlow.brs`, with 20 cases in `SignInFlowTests.brs`.

**Not run.** Nothing here has been on a TV: the ChannelStore node and Roku's screen can't run off
the TV. Open: whether a sideloaded build shows the screen, whether the observer fires when the
viewer cancels (nothing depends on it), whether Roku's reviewers, who may sign in with the link
code and never open USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD, accept that, and, only in the dashboard, whether the
analysis stops flagging the error. A recorded sign-in script needs one more step: Roku's screen,
between USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD and the EMAIL field. The Roku section of the privacy page needs a line saying the app may ask
Roku for the account email and only fills a field with it (`privacy.html` and
`Nostalgex/PRIVACY_POLICY.md` together).

## 2026-11-02 (Android TV: rebased onto main; Plex addresses chosen as the Apple TV and Roku do)

**Changed.** On `feature/android`, rebased onto `main` at `e0c41cc`; the 17 commits since `e6cc985` touched no Android file and none of the files its tests read.

- `main` brought the web tuner the Apple TV's and Roku's way of choosing a Plex address (`scripts/nostalgex-server-resolve.js`). Android had the web's old way. It waited for every address before choosing, and preferred remote HTTPS over the home network. It also took any address that answered, even as a different Plex server. Now ported:
  - `ServerResolve.kt` holds the rules as a state machine with no clock: home network, remote HTTPS, remote plain, relay; settled once nothing better can answer; a silent home address is given up after 3 s once something else has answered; everything ends at 10 s.
  - `PlexClient.findWorkingConnection` asks every address at once (`/identity`, 5 s), cancels the rest when it settles, and turns down a different `machineIdentifier`. Each server's choice is logged as `SERVER ADDRESS`.
- `gen-resolve-vectors.mjs` runs the web module on the smoke's virtual clock: its 16 named cases (the Apple TV's `ConnectionDiscoveryEarlyExitTests`, Roku's `ServerResolveTests`) and its 400 seeded random servers. `ServerResolveTest` replays every run, and all 416 choose the same address at the same millisecond. Removing the "once something else has answered" condition made it fail. The CI path filter now includes the module.
- The other changes on `main` (GUIDE TEXT SIZE, the WATERSHED switch, the failure card in the split view, and the site) were the web catching up with the Apple TV. Android already had all of them.

**Measured** on the SHIELD, on Settings' server list for a real account, twice:
- An owned server with four addresses settled on its home HTTPS address in 22 to 26 ms, without waiting for the other three.
- A shared server with three addresses settled on remote HTTPS at 3,008 to 3,015 ms: the 3 s grace, because its home-network address (on its owner's network) never answered. The old code waited out that address's 5 s timeout.
- A shared server whose only address is plain HTTP failed in 27 to 41 ms with `ConnectException` (refused), as it would have before.
The `SERVER ADDRESS` log line now says why each address failed: the exception, the HTTP status, or "another server". The different-server check has not been seen to turn anything down on a real network.

## 2026-11-02 (Android TV: the PlaybackInfo handshake on Jellyfin and Emby)

**Changed.** On `feature/android`. Android asked Jellyfin and Emby for the stored file, then a hand-built HLS stream, which is only the Apple TV's fallback. It now asks the server first, as the Apple TV does.

- `PlaybackInfoHandshake.kt` ports `JellyfinPlaybackResolver`: the body (`SubtitleStreamIndex` -1 with every subtitle format External; `EnableDirectPlay` and `EnableDirectStream` false on the retry after a failed direct play, because Emby still offers the file with only the first), `resolve` (the server's TranscodingUrl as built, `api_key` added once, the audio track pinned), `forcedSubtitleToBurn` and `negotiate` (a second request burns a forced track in the viewer's SUBTITLE LANGUAGE; if it fails, the first answer plays). 24 tests, the Apple TV's `JellyfinPlaybackInfoTests` cases that apply to this player.
- Asked where the Apple TV asks: when the app skips direct play (a container Media3 has no extractor for, or a file over the remote ceiling), and on the retry after a direct play failed. The capped 1080p retry stays hand-built, as on the Apple TV. A failed answer, an empty one, or none within 12 s plays the hand-built stream. An answer for a tune already replaced is dropped and its session stopped.
- The device profile differs from the Apple TV's on purpose: H.264 and AAC in MPEG-TS, the stream the hand-built request already plays, where the Apple TV asks for fMP4 with HEVC for AVPlayer; and no DirectPlayProfiles, because this app decides direct play by trying the file and asks the server only after deciding not to. The 10-bit H.264 cap is kept. The audio track is pinned by the Roku's rule, as the hand-built stream already was.
- The startup watchdog's fallback now starts from the planned offset, as the Apple TV's (`beginServerFallback(position: seekOffset)`), not from the playhead. Found in this test: an MKV whose video Media3 could not read went ready without its seek, played sound from 0 s, and the server stream then started at 14 s on a programme 137 s in. The starvation fallback still resumes from the playhead, as on the Apple TV.

**Measured** on the Android TV emulator against Jellyfin 12.4 and Emby 4.10.2 in Docker, with two generated files: an MKV in MS-MPEG4 (no decoder on the emulator) with a French default track, an English 5.1 track, a default English subtitle and a forced English one; and a WMV.
- The MKV: the watchdog moved it off direct play at 15 s; PlaybackInfo with direct play off answered in 58 to 100 ms on both servers, asked a second time for subtitle 4, and played in 1.2 to 1.3 s. Both servers' ffmpeg burned stream 4 (`subtitles=`) and mapped the English 5.1 track (`-map 0:2`, AAC 6 channels) into MPEG-TS with libx264. The forced line shows in the guide preview.
- The WMV: one request, no forced track, answered in 56 to 77 ms, played in 0.6 to 0.7 s, no subtitle filter.
- An AVI whose direct play failed for lack of a decoder: answered in 163 ms, played in 1.5 s at the right offset.
- The next programme stopped the last one's encode by the server's session id: Jellyfin deleted its stream files 13 ms before the next PlaybackInfo; Emby answered the `DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings` 204.
- Through a proxy holding PlaybackInfo: held 8 s with Home pressed at 3 s, the answer was dropped at 8.1 s and its session stopped; held 15 s, the request gave up at 12.1 s and the hand-built stream played in 1.3 s.

**Not checked:** the SHIELD, a real library, an HEVC or Dolby Vision file through the handshake (the profile offers H.264 only, so those are re-encoded, as by the hand-built request), and a file over the remote bitrate ceiling.

## 2026-11-02 (Android TV: STOP WAITING, SHOW NOW PLAYING and MARK WATCHED)

**Changed.** On `feature/android`. Two Apple TV features Android lacked.

- STOP WAITING (`LibraryLoadStallWatch.swift`). `LibraryLoadStallDetector` is ported to the engine with the 12 cases of its Swift tests: a scan is judged by whether its counters (section, items, shows done, server) still move, never by how long it has run; quiet for 60 s is slow, 210 s stalled. Each server's scan runs under the watch, sampled every 2 s. Slow, the loading screen says "Still waiting on your server" and offers STOP WAITING (focused as it appears; a stray press only keeps what has loaded); pressed, or at 210 s, the scan is abandoned. Both scans now hand over each library once it is read whole, so an abandoned scan builds the guide from those; with none the load fails in the Apple TV's words. The Jellyfin and Emby scan blocks on its requests, so it checks a stop flag before each one, and its per-show and per-library catches pass the stop through, so a half-read library is never counted whole. A background refresh is watched silently and, abandoned, keeps the guide on screen.
- Measured on the emulator through a proxy that answers two listings and then holds the third open, sending a byte every 20 s (a connection that neither fails nor finishes): the block appeared at about 60 s; STOP WAITING at 68 s kept the 19 items of the two libraries read and the guide came up; with the server quiet from the first listing and no press, the watchdog acted at 210 s and the load ended on "Your server stopped sending data partway through the scan and never resumed"; a background refresh against the same server gave up at 210 s and the saved guide stayed. Found and fixed while measuring: after an abandoned scan the collections read asked the same quiet server and hung on DISCOVERING COLLECTIONS; it is now skipped for that load. A first attempt with a proxy that went silent never reached 60 s: the client's 60 s read timeout fails each request, the scan moves on to the next library, and progress keeps moving, which is the design (a request that times out ends in a real error).
- SHOW NOW PLAYING and MARK WATCHED (`PlaybackTracker.swift`, plex-tuner.html `makePlaybackTracker`), under WATCH HISTORY in PLAYBACK & PICTURE, both off by default, under the Apple TV's keys. The pure half of `scripts/nostalgex-watch-state.js` is in the engine (`WatchState.kt`: the cleanup plans, the pulse backoff, the reporting scope's epochs, the 15% and 75% gates, the 89% stop), held to `scripts/watch-cleanup-golden.json` (the Apple TV's WatchStateGuardTests read it too) and to the web tuner's answers over the Roku's scripts (`genWatchVectors`). The app's `WatchReporter` sends Plex a position-free `/:/timeline` (PUT, as the Apple TV) every 10 s and `/:/scrobble`, and Jellyfin and Emby `/Sessions/Playing`, `Progress` and `Stopped` and `PlayedItems`, all through one queue so a restore lands after the last report.
- Measured on the emulator against Jellyfin 12.4: Jellyfin listed the programme as now playing from client "Nostalgex"; a film tuned in at 17% (past the entry gate) was stopped and its state put back (unplayed, play count 0, no resume point); a film watched from its start was marked watched at 140 s of 180 s and left played, play count 1, no resume point. Not checked: Plex (no Plex server in the harness), Emby, and turning a switch off mid-programme.

## 2026-11-02 (Android TV: the transcode's audio track, and the 4K deadline)

**Changed.** On `feature/android`. Two small gaps from the earlier entries.

- A Jellyfin or Emby transcode now asks for its audio track. The scan keeps each source's audio tracks (`MediaItem.audioStreams`: index, language, codec, channels, title, and IsDefault) and `LanguageChoice.preferredAudioIndex` picks one (JellyfinPlaybackResolver.preferredAudioIndex), which goes on the HLS request as `AudioStreamIndex`, only when there is more than one track. `AudioTrackSelectionTest` carries the cases of `AudioTrackSelectionTests.swift` and the language cases of `LanguageCodeMatchingTests.swift` (Estonian is not Spanish, `cze` and `ces` are Czech, and so on).
- The rule is the Roku's (`NxMbChosenAudioIndex`, issue #62), which the owner chose over the Apple TV's: the viewer's AUDIO LANGUAGE ranks first and English only after it. The Apple TV adds English to the wanted languages and takes the most channels, first on a tie, so a German viewer gets an English 5.1 mix over German stereo. Measured on the emulator with AUDIO LANGUAGE Norwegian: Kon-Tiki (English default first, Norwegian second, both mono) was asked for in English, where Android's direct play picks the Norwegian; after the change it asks for track 2 (Norwegian), and The 39 Steps (French default, English) still gets English. Probed against Jellyfin 12.4: the same transcode request decodes to different audio with `AudioStreamIndex=2` than without it.
- The startup watchdog's deadline reads the frame size, so a 4K transcode gets the Apple TV's 40 s: `videoWidth` and `videoHeight` from Plex's Media and Jellyfin's or Emby's video stream (Kon-Tiki saved as 1280 x 720). `LibraryStore` format 6.

**Found, in the web tuner.** Its Jellyfin and Emby scan builds `audioStreams` in `mediaInfo` (plex-tuner.html around line 9313) but the item only takes `subtitles: mi.subtitles` (lines 9400 and 9460), never `audioStreams`. So `pickAudioStream(item.audioStreams || [])` always gets an empty list: the web tuner never asks for the viewer's audio language on Jellyfin or Emby, and its foreign-audio subtitle fallback never switches on there. Not changed here: it is the web tuner's to fix, in its own pull request. `MediaBrowserScanTest` leaves the field out of its comparison and says why.

**Not checked:** an actual 4K file (the deadline function is tested, the frame size reaches the item; no 4K file in the test library), Emby, and the SHIELD.

## 2026-11-02 (Android TV: the playback recovery ladder)

**Changed.** On `feature/android`. Android had the direct-play-to-transcode fallback, the failure card and the five-in-a-row stop, but nothing watched a stream that never showed a picture or one its source couldn't keep up with. It now has the Apple TV's ladder (`AppState+Playback.swift`): `PlaybackWatchdog` and `PlaybackStarvation` ported to `engine/PlaybackRecovery.kt` with the Apple TV's tests transcribed (`PlaybackRecoveryTest`), and `Playback.kt` running them per attempt, numbered so a late callback from an earlier attempt does nothing.

- Startup watchdog: no picture (ready, playhead moved 0.25 s across 2 s, a decoded frame) by 15 s moves a direct play to the server stream; by 20 s moves a transcode to one retry capped at 1080p (Plex: the HIGH preset, 1920x1080 at 12 Mbps; Jellyfin and Emby: `MaxWidth=1920`, 8 Mbps, a new `PlaySessionId`); then the card.
- Starvation monitor, once a second after picture: three stalls in 2 minutes, or one of 20 s, moves a direct play to the server stream and a transcode to the capped retry, from where the viewer is; a capped stream that starves too ends in "Your server couldn't keep up".
- The five-in-a-row count now resets on a confirmed picture, not on reaching ready, as on the Apple TV.
- PLAYBACK INFORMATION gains the two reasons ("No picture reached the startup deadline", "Playback stopped making progress") and the RECOVERY REQUEST row. Its BACKEND row said "Plex" on every server; it now names the server.
- A log line for every rebuffer and every counted stall, so a stall can be counted from `adb logcat -s Nostalgex`.

**Measured** on the emulator against Jellyfin 12.4, through a proxy that throttles or cuts media delivery. Before: direct play at 0.67x real time froze for 2.6 to 2.9 s every 8 to 9 s, 16 times in 150 s, and never stepped down; a direct play that never sent a byte was black for 36 s before the transcode; with segments cut too, 72 s of black per programme and a card saying "Can't reach your server". After: the starving direct play moved to the server stream after 3 stalls (27 to 38 s after picture) at the same point in the film, and that stream started in 0.9 to 1.1 s and played clean; a hung direct play moved at 15 s; a transcode that never pictured reached the capped retry at 20 s and the card ("couldn't keep up") at 55 s; a capped stream that starved ended on that card after 3 stalls of 9 to 10 s. Healthy direct play and healthy transcoding, 3 minutes each: no stall counted.

**One number differs from the Apple TV, on measurement.** A stall counts from 2 s, not 3. AVPlayer froze for good on a starving source; ExoPlayer stops and carries on, and at 3 s the monitor counted none of 20 freezes in 120 s. Healthy rebuffers on the emulator peaked at 511 ms (31 in 200 s, median 61 ms). `PlaybackRecoveryTest` samples both shapes at ten phases of the once-a-second clock. A 4K transcode also gets 20 s, not 40, because `MediaItem` carries no frame size yet (since fixed, in the entry on the transcode's audio track).

**Seen, and left as the Apple TV does it.** A transcode already on screen but mid-stall at its 20 s deadline (moved 0.1 s across the window) counts as no picture, gets the capped retry, and if that is mid-stall too ends on "This one wouldn't play" rather than "couldn't keep up". It is the Apple TV's rule as written; changing it belongs in both apps.

**Not checked.** Plex (the capped request and the HLS clock rule, `hlsBaseOffset`, are unmeasured there; no Plex server in the harness), Emby, and a real SHIELD.

**Next.** Check on the SHIELD against Plex, ideally with a file the server transcodes slower than real time.

## 2026-11-01 (Roku: one title on one channel at a time, the lineup's days packed together)

**Why.** The Apple TV and web engines pack each day for the whole lineup now (`89a2f5c`, review
fixes `faede9b`, below): on a pulled Apple TV guide, doubled minutes went from 94.2% to 0.2%. The
Roku engine is held to the same golden file, which it failed 123 of 366 on until this port.
Trello z4K7aJG6.

**Changed.** On `roku/cross-channel-dedupe`, off `faede9b` so it merges with it as one, not
pushed. A line-for-line port of `scripts/nostalgex-daily-manifest.js`:
- `DailyManifest.brs`: the occupancy, the multi-part guard, `NxPickCandidate` (the next 8 are
  looked at); `NxPackDay` takes the occupancy and a `gated` flag. The filler is the rotating
  queue; the main pass hands over to it when nothing waiting fits.
- `Lineup.brs`: on a cache miss `NxManifestBlocks` packs the registered lineup's day
  (`NxPackLineupDay`): time-gated channels last then by id, yesterday's overruns and the days
  already stored fixed, a gated channel giving way to the rest but not to another gated one, a
  channel off the lineup packing after it and adding nothing. The lineup's pools are read at the
  hour the guide's own are. A channel the lineup names twice counts once, at its first place, as
  on the web and the Apple TV.
- `GuideSchedule.brs`, `LibraryTask.brs`: `NxSetLineup(ordered)` before every `NxScheduleGuide`;
  a library load clears it.
- `ScheduleParityGoldenTests.brs`: gated rows get `timeRestrictions`, every row but `offGuide` is
  registered, and `offGuide` rows are still dumped. `CrossChannelTests.brs` (48 cases) for the
  pieces; `tests/bench/BenchLineup.brs` for the time.

**A bug the bench found.** `NxManifestBlocks` first walked the lineup with `for each`, and
`NxScheduleGuide`'s own `for each` is over that same array. A nested `for each` over one array
shares its place on a TV, so the guide stopped after its first channel (1 of 142 on the stick).
The interpreter doesn't do it and every golden case walks by index, so only the bench saw it. The
lineup is walked by index now, and `CrossChannelTests` schedules the very array it registers.

**Measured.**
- Parity golden: 363 passed, 0 failed off-device (it was 243 passed, 123 failed with the new golden
  and the old engine); the whole suite runs on the Streaming Stick Plus (OS 15.3.4) and ends in
  ALL TESTS PASSED, the golden in 5.9 s there.
- `BenchLineup`, a made-up 142-channel lineup on the stick, before then after: wide (12,000 items,
  pools of 80 to 3,000) cold 39.3 s then 40.6 s, warm 0.62 s then 0.61 s, package switch 6.5 s
  then 6.4 s, doubled minutes 1.0% then 0%. Crowded (600 items, pools of 40 to 200, every title on
  dozens of channels) cold 4.8 s then 6.1 s (+27%), warm 0.60 s then 0.65 s, switch 1.16 s then
  1.18 s, doubled minutes 17.6% then 0.15%.
- A test library of about 12,000 items on the stick: cold schedule of both days 2.62 s and
  2.91 s before, 2.73 s and 2.82 s after, two launches each. A launch shows the saved guide (1.1 s
  to AppLaunchComplete both ways); the schedule runs behind it, so launch time doesn't move. The
  first launch with no saved guide, and the first guide after an update's rebuild, are where the
  cold cost shows (C1).

**Half-done.** Nothing run on an Apple TV. The crowded bench is the worst case measured: a lineup
of 142 channels on a library that small is not one anyone has.

## 2026-11-01 (one title on one channel at a time: the lineup's days packed together)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `schedule/cross-channel-dedupe`, off main `9438f2a`, carrying the
harness commit from `harness/cross-channel-duplicates`. Not pushed. Trello: z4K7aJG6.

**Why.** Each channel's day was packed on its own, so a film in several pools aired on two or
more channels at once for almost the whole day. `resolveConflicts` only relabels the info
panel; tuning still plays the doubled title. Measured on a guide and its manifests pulled
read-only from a real Apple TV: a title was on two or more channels at once for 95.3% of the
minutes of one day and 94.2% of the next. One film under two ratingKeys (copies across
libraries or servers) was not part of it there: 0.04% of the doubled minutes, all music videos.

**Changed.** One engine change, in Swift and JS together, with new golden vectors.
- `DailyManifestScheduler.packLineupDay` / `packLineupDay` in `scripts/nostalgex-daily-manifest.js`:
  when a day isn't stored, it is packed for the whole registered lineup at once. Channels go in
  priority order (channels with `timeRestrictions` last, so no other channel's day depends on
  the hour a device first built it; then by id, so the lowest keeps a title, as
  `resolveConflicts` does). Each channel keeps its own running order, except that a programme
  another channel has on in an overlapping slot waits: `pickCandidate` takes the first of the
  next 8 that is free. The primary pass hands over to the filler loop when nothing waiting
  fits (the unplayed films stay unplayed for tomorrow); the filler takes the least overlap
  when nothing fits, never the title that just played, and a later part of a story never jumps
  ahead of an earlier one. Stored days and what runs over from the night before are fixed.
- With no lineup registered, or nothing on elsewhere, the pick is always the first: a channel
  packs exactly as before. The lowest channel never changes.
- The lineup comes from `AppState.channels` (`didSet`, scoped to the sign-in's credential
  fingerprint) and from `guideLineup()` in `plex-tuner.html`. A channel off the guide packs
  after the lineup, against it, and is seen by none of it.
- Schema bumps (Swift manifest 1 to 2, web 2 to 3), so the first launch after the update packs
  today again from yesterday's history: a one-time reshuffle. Channels that had no clash keep
  their day exactly; the others change from their first clash on.
- `scripts/schedule-parity-golden.json`: a fourth case (a crowded lineup: three channels
  sharing two films, a three-part story, a premiere channel, a time-gated one, one off the
  guide); the other three cases now pack across their lineups. Four new negative controls in
  the parity smoke. New `scripts/nostalgex-schedule-lineup-smoke.mjs` (in `npm test`),
  `NostalgexTests/ScheduleLineupTests.swift`, `scripts/qa/cross-channel-repack.mjs` and
  `CrossChannelDuplicateHarness.testRepackOnDeviceData`.

**Measured.** On the pulled data, the device's next day packed again from its own history.
The old engine reproduces the device's manifests exactly (every channel, every block), in JS
and in Swift. Then:
- doubled minutes 94.2% before, 0.2% after; on a day with no history, 95.3% before, 0% after.
  What is left is 3 minutes on a three-film franchise channel with no free alternative.
- The Swift and JS engines pack the same day on that data, channel for channel.
- Lookahead 4, 8, 16 and 1000 all give 0.2%; 2 gives 7.6%.
- A rescan that changed nothing packs the days ahead the same (Swift test and JS smoke).
- Pack time for the whole lineup's day, before (each channel alone) and after (the lineup):
  JS (Node, Mac) 21 ms before, 33 ms after. Swift (tvOS simulator, debug build) 346 ms before,
  305 ms after; it is faster because it now reads each yesterday file once, not twice. With
  half the lineup off the guide the web page also builds those channels: 22 ms before, 45 ms
  after with a memo of the lineup's day, 222 ms without it.

**Review fixes (same branch).**
- A caller that found its day unstored and then waited on the pack lock while another
  thread packed the day could get an empty schedule back, if the memo was dropped in between
  (`purgeDays`, or the 256-entry memo full with today and tomorrow of a large lineup). It now
  reads the store again inside the lock, and `packLineupDay` returns the stored days as well
  as the packed ones. `ScheduleLineupTests.testAWaiterGetsTheDayAnotherThreadPacked`
  reproduces the empty return without the fix.
- Web: the off-guide memo is keyed on which channels the guide holds, so a channel switched on
  or off (any path that flips `enabled`) can't leave it stale. A smoke control keyed on the day
  alone clashes; the fix doesn't.
- Apple TV: the lineup is registered again whenever anything the credential fingerprint is
  made of changes (backend, servers, server URL, Jellyfin/Emby user), not only the channels.
- Two time-gated channels: a time-gated channel gives way to the ungated lineup only, never to
  another time-gated one, so its day can't depend on the hour the other was first built. Two
  of them can air the same title at once; channels.json has one (VHS VAULT). A second gated
  channel in the golden case and a negative control cover it.
- `ScheduleTiming` (trigger `sched-timing` in `soak.trigger`) and
  `scripts/qa/appletv-schedule-timing.sh` time, on a real Apple TV's main thread, what a tune
  waits for when the day isn't packed, before and after, in a scratch manifest folder. Not run
  yet: it needs the owner's OK to install on the low-end bench TV.

**Half-done.** Roku: `roku/tests` goes red on `ScheduleParityGoldenTests` until the
BrightScript port of `packLineupDay` lands in the same merge. Not measured on an Apple
TV or a Roku stick; the Roku build time on a large library is the open number. Same show on two
channels at once (different episodes) is unchanged and out of scope.

**Next.** Roku port, then a device check on the living room Apple TV and the stick. Web and
Docker need a tuner version bump when this ships.

own accordion under MY COLLECTIONS. Trello bJu4Q3Ap, ours, not tydude001's.

**Verified.** 50 cases in `tests/SettingsChannelsTests.brs`. `tests/run.sh` (`NX_TEST_JOBS=2`)
ends in ALL TESTS PASSED, and `deploy.sh --test` on the Streaming Stick Plus (OS 15.3.4) does too,
the 50 cases among them (on a Mac, `deploy.sh --test` needs a fix that is not on main yet).
Static analysis shows one warning, `SubtitleSettings.brs` line 181 at 1,434 characters, which is

On the stick, with the settings tour (made-up data, no video), each seen in a screenshot and the
console clean:

- the merged A to Z list, with a dimmed duplicate collection among the franchises;

On the real app, over a real library, through the real guide to Settings, also in screenshots:

**Not matched.** The A to Z list compares lowercased text character by character. The Apple TV's
`localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` is locale-aware, so a title starting with an accented letter
sorts after Z here and with its base letter there. BrightScript has no collation, and a table
for it would be a guess at ICU's order. Collection titles that start with an accent are rare.

**Open.** On the Apple TV the page lists franchise collections while the switch is off and lets

## 2026-11-01 (Roku: a Jellyfin or Emby scan does less per item, #155)

**Why.** #155: every cold boot rescans the whole library, and Chad asked where a cold scan's
time goes before picking a change. On a 55R617 (Roku OS 15.3.4) signed in to a test Emby with
5,551 titles (763 films, 4,773 episodes in 148 shows), a cold scan on 1.0.8 with timing prints
took 17.5 s: about 3.3 s downloading (36 MB in 160 answers), 3.5 s in `ParseJson` and about
10.7 s building items. Building channels took 10.9 s more. In a 200-episode sample, 90% of the
bytes are `MediaSources`, most of them subtitle stream descriptions (937 titles carry 10 or
more subtitle tracks). Dropping the show-level `Fields` from the episode request saves about 2%
of the bytes.

**Changed.** Branch `roku-mb-scan-speed` (tydude001), off main at 0795e19.
`MediaBrowserLibrary.brs`: `NxMbIsTextSub` compares the codec in place instead of building
an 11-item list per call; `NxMbUnixSeconds` makes its regex once per thread; `NxMbDoviProfile`
tests the prefix before making a regex (Emby sends "None" for 5,530 of 5,559 files); the
first video and audio stream come from one walk. The saved library is unchanged: on the 55",
an MD5 over every scanned item's `FormatJson` matched main's across 8 scans. Scan time, 4
scans each, behind a saved guide: main 18.7 to 19.3 s (mean 19.0), branch 16.7 to 19.3 s
(mean 17.8). About 6%.

**Next.** What's left is downloading and parsing the subtitle descriptions, and building
items and channels. A guide seed in the registry (#155's second option) would let a cold boot
show a guide while the scan runs, as a warm launch does. Leaving the subtitle detail out of the
scan would need another way to get what the scan reads from `MediaSources` (the Dolby Vision
profile, container, codecs, bitrate). Both are Chad's call.

## 2026-11-01 (Roku: Back puts the TV's caption setting back, #117 option C)

**Why.** The Roku draws subtitles only while the TV's own caption mode is on, so the app
turns it on while its subtitles show. On 2026-10-30 a 43" TCL (Roku OS 16.0.4) kept the
TV's captions on after leaving with Back as well as Home, until the next launch. Back left
without a `subtitles false`, so `restoreCaptionMode` never ran. Chad picked option C on
#117: put it back on Back too; Home stays as it is, since the app gets no event before Home
closes it.

**Changed.** Branch `roku-caption-back` (tydude001), off main at 9438f2a.
`GuideView.brs`: the Back handler runs `restoreCaptionMode()` before every exit (stop the
server's stream first, report the stop first, let Roku close the app, and Back on an empty
guide), and `setCaptions` keeps captions off once `m.leaving` is set, so a track list
arriving while the app waits to close can't turn the mode on again. Checked on the 43"
with the lab Emby's forced-subtitle film: the TV read Off 5 s and 20 s after Back closed
the app (On after both on 2026-10-30).

**Next.** Option A (draw forced text subtitles in the app, so the setting is never
touched for them) is on Chad's roadmap for after the Roku settles.

## 2026-11-01 (Web tuner and Docker: franchise channels and the FRANCHISES / OTHER COLLECTIONS split, #122)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `web/franchise-parity`, cut from `origin/main` at `9438f2a`, not
merged, not pushed. A push to `main` deploys the hosted tuner; the Docker image needs its own
`tuner-v` tag and a `tunerVersion` bump in the tagged commit.

**Why.** The web tuner and Docker showed the seven classics (CH 100-106 by channel rules) and
nothing else: no found franchises, no switches, and every server collection in one list from
CH 400. The Apple TV (1.0.29) and the Roku (1.0.8) build a franchise channel for each series in
the library and split collections into FRANCHISES and OTHER COLLECTIONS. The franchise builder
(`scripts/nostalgex-franchise-builder.js`) already existed and was checked against its own golden
file, but the page never loaded it, and `nostalgex-collections.js` said outright that the classifier
and found franchises were not ported.

**Changed.**
- The classics are CH 300-306. Found franchises and the server's franchise collections share
  CH 310-399 (90 places) as one pool, numbered A to Z by name then stable id; when more are on than
  fit, the ones with the most films stay. Other collections take CH 400-499 (100 places, the first
  100 switched on). Ids stay per kind (1,000,000, 1,010,000 and 1,020,000). HIGH ROTATION is 500 up.
- `nostalgex-collections.js` gained `classify` (CollectionClassifier.swift, rule for rule, with
  Swift's Character handling for lengths and prefixes), `keptInDisplayOrder` and a `materialize`
  that numbers both blocks. It is opt-in (`ctx.classify`, `opts.found`): without them the module
  answers exactly as before, which the Roku collection vectors rely on (they came out
  byte-identical before and after).
- New `scripts/nostalgex-franchise-lineup.js` puts the pieces in the Apple TV's order: the builder
  groups the library; while the FRANCHISES package is on, what a classic covers joins that classic's
  pool unless another channel owns the item (manifest lock or exclusive rule); each collection is
  classified and folded into a classic or a found franchise (FranchiseCollectionFold.swift, with the
  guard that a collection holding shows folds only into a franchise that airs them); then the
  blocks are numbered. `plex-tuner.html` calls it as `refreshDynamicChannels()` after the library
  loads, after enrichment (which is what carries a film's TMDB collection), after a collection scan
  and after every switch.
- Settings, Bundles: a FRANCHISES section under the packages. The package switch heads it, then
  ADD ALL and REMOVE ALL (buttons, for TV browsers) and one alphabetical list of the classics, the
  found franchises and the franchise collections, each with its own switch. MY COLLECTIONS lists
  only the other collections. The FRANCHISES switch is every franchise channel's: off, none airs
  (found franchises, franchise collections, classics). Choices are saved by stable id in
  `nostalgex_enabled_franchises` and `nostalgex_disabled_franchises`, the Apple TV's key names.
- The franchise builder had a 7.6 s hot spot that the page would have hit on its first call: it
  re-derived every explicit title list for every episode, 180 microseconds each. A library of
  42,000 episodes and 2,000 films took 7,586 ms; it takes 17 ms now (an episode takes the answer
  its show's first episode got, and the lists are keyed once). Same answers: all 48 existing
  franchise golden checks pass.

**How it is held to the Apple TV.** `scripts/franchise-lineup-golden.json` (65 classifier cases, 10
block cases, 9 lineups) is read by three tests. The expected answers were not written by any engine
under test: `Nostalgex/NostalgexTests/FranchiseLineupGoldenTests.swift` builds every case with the
app's own `CollectionClassifier`, `AppState.rebuildFoundFranchises` and `materializeDynamicChannels`
and, with `TEST_RUNNER_NOSTALGEX_GOLDEN_DUMP` set, writes what it got; `scripts/merge-franchise-lineup-golden.mjs`
puts that in the file. Then:
- Swift: `FranchiseLineupGoldenTests` passes against the file (tvOS simulator, 0.19 s).
- Web: `npm run test:franchise-lineup`, 97 checks, in `npm test`. Four deliberate breaks (the franchise
  block starts at CH 300, the repeated-word threshold, the order that decides who stays, the lock on a
  classic's pool) each fail it.
- Roku: `roku/tests/FranchiseLineupTests.brs` reads a byte copy (`gen-vectors.mjs` vendors it), 134
  checks, run in the brs interpreter on its own (not on a TV). Two cases are listed as known
  differences in the test and not counted as failures, each with its reason: the classifier compares
  code points where Swift compares Characters (a combining accent in a shared title prefix), and with
  the FRANCHISES package off the Roku folds nothing where the Apple TV still folds against the
  classics it built. The test fails if a listed case starts to agree.
- The page: `npm run test:franchise-channels:browser` (headless, not in `npm test`) loads
  `plex-tuner.html` against a Jellyfin-shaped test server holding the first lineup of the golden file,
  with its TMDB collections served as the enrichment rows the page reads, and compares the classics'
  pools, the Settings rows, each collection's category and fold, every runtime channel and the
  guide with the Apple TV's answers: 51 checks, identical on the repo's page, `dist` (hosted) and
  `dist-selfhost` (Docker). Against `origin/main`'s page the same script fails all 9 sections.
  It also clicks and keys through the switches, REMOVE ALL, ADD ALL, the package switch and a reload,
  and checks the section at 390x844, 820x1180, 1440x900 and 960x540 (clicks only, nothing in
  browser full screen). A rebuild on a synthetic 11,539-item library (10,000 episodes) took 8 to 10 ms.

**Also fixed.** Eight browser smokes read their root from `new URL("../", import.meta.url).pathname`,
which keeps a space as `%20`, so none of them could start from a checkout whose path has a space
in it. They use `fileURLToPath` now.

**Why.** Since `e66be04` (#125) the web tuner's Plex loader reads every server answer

## 2026-10-31 (Roku: tests/run.sh runs as many interpreters as memory allows)

**Why.** `tests/run.sh` ran one brs interpreter per CPU thread. Each takes 0.5-1.7 GB, so
on a 20-thread, 31 GB Linux desktop the 20 of them filled about 25 GB, and the kernel's
out-of-memory killer took the desktop (kwin, plasmashell) instead of them (2026-10-25).

**Changed.** On `roku-test-memcap` (off main), not pushed. Both pools (the component parse
and the suites) run at most one interpreter per 2 GB free (MemAvailable on Linux, the whole
RAM on macOS), and never more than the CPU threads; `NX_TEST_JOBS` still overrides. On
Linux the run marks itself the kernel's first pick (`oom_score_adj` 1000), and with a
systemd user session each pool runs in a scope held to the memory free at the start, with
no swap, so an overrun kills a test part, which then fails, and not the desktop.

before writing to it. It is git-ignored, so in a fresh clone or worktree both died

## 2026-10-31 (Roku: Norwegian, Bokmal and Nynorsk are one language)

**Why.** Norwegian has three ISO 639-1 codes ("no", "nb", "nn") and three ISO 639-2 ones
("nor", "nob", "nno"). Servers tag the same track with any of them and a TV set to
Norwegian reports nb_NO, so the exact compare from issue #119 never matched across them.

**Changed.** On `roku/norwegian-one-language` (off main), not pushed. `NxLanguageKey`
folds the six to "no" where codes are compared: the setting (`NxPreferredLanguageFrom`),
a track (`NxSubComparableTag`) and the prefix compare (`NxSubMatches`). `NxIso639Table` is
unchanged. Every other language keeps the exact compare. The Apple TV and web tuner do the
same on `fix/norwegian-one-language`. Cases in `tests/SubtitleTests.brs`.

`0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed. A Docker release needs its own `tuner-v` tag and a
`tunerVersion` bump in the tagged commit.

**Why the first fix was not enough.** `363a888` wrapped the one write the report named
(`saveChannelConfig()`), and that is on `main`. Measured against a fake 6,738-item Plex
library (519 movies, 6,219 episodes) padded so the old trimmed cache lands at 5,236,139 of
Chrome's 5,242,880-character localStorage quota, the way the report describes it:

- 1.0.9: `QuotaExceededError` at `saveChannelConfig`, error screen "COULD NOT LOAD LIBRARY.
  YOUR SERVER MAY BE UNREACHABLE", channel config not saved.
- `main` with the try/catch: the library loads, but the channel config is still not saved
  (the cache leaves 6 KB and the config needs 7.5 KB). With 6.5 KB of other settings saved
  in that browser the error screen is back: the next write after the cache,
  `markInitialLibraryLoadComplete()` in `nostalgex-library-load.js`, was unguarded and threw
  the same error. A try/catch on one write only moves the throw to the next one.

So the cause in the report is right, and the cure is not guarding one write. The cache has
no business taking the whole quota.

**Changed.**

- The library cache moved from localStorage to IndexedDB (`scripts/nostalgex-storage.js`,
  web only, new file). IndexedDB has no 5 MB ceiling and the enrichment cache already uses
  it. The cache is now stored whole, summaries included; localStorage used to drop them
  to fit. The page deletes the old localStorage copy at start-up, so a browser a 1.0.9
  tuner left full is freed on its first visit. It is not migrated: that costs one rescan.
- Sign-out still has to forget the library at once (the items carry the Plex token). The
  record in IndexedDB only counts while a short id in localStorage matches it, so
  `clearLibraryCache()` is one synchronous `removeItem` and a page that navigates away
  before IndexedDB finishes deleting cannot leave a cache that loads.
- Every `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` write in `plex-tuner.html` goes through
  `lsSet`/`ssSet`, which never throw. On a full quota a small setting gives up rebuildable
  data and retries: the old library cache, then the collection scan, the MusicBrainz cache
  and the daily manifests, stopping as soon as it fits. A cache write never evicts
  another cache. If nothing can be freed the setting stays in memory and the console says so.
- `markInitialLibraryLoadComplete()` goes through the same path. The Plex client id is held in
  memory too, so a failed save does not mean a new device id on every request. In
  `web-tuner.html`, `getClientId()` was the one unguarded localStorage write (its sign-in
  saves already had a try).
- The error screen says what failed. A storage error now reads "THIS BROWSER RAN OUT OF
  STORAGE. YOUR SERVER IS FINE...", and a failure while building the guide (including the
  cache-restore path, where no server was asked) reads "THE LIBRARY LOADED, BUT THE GUIDE
  COULD NOT BE BUILT...". A scan that got no answer still says the server may be unreachable.
  Both backends use it. Checked at 390x844, 820x1180, 1440x900 and 960x540: no overflow.

**Measured, same library, fixed code.** Guide up in 3.3 s, 66.6 KB of localStorage (1.3% of
the quota), 7.0 MB cached in IndexedDB, channel config and first-load flag saved. A reload
restores the guide in 0.7 s with zero requests to the server. With the padded library and
6.5 KB of extra settings: same result. The built Docker output (`dist-selfhost`) passes the
same checks.

**Tests.** New `scripts/nostalgex-storage-smoke.mjs` (33 checks, in `npm test`): quota error
shapes, eviction order, a cache write not evicting a cache, the cache id, a failed write, a
stuck database, and that the evictable key names still match what the tuner writes. New
`scripts/storage-quota-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:storage-quota`, Playwright, not in
`npm test`): 55 checks over the 6,738-item library at the real quota, the full-browser
state, a quota full of rebuildable data, one full of data the page cannot rebuild, the error
messages, sign-out, and no or stuck IndexedDB. `TUNER_ROOT=<checkout>` runs it against any
other build: against 1.0.9 it fails 23 of its first-load checks. Taking eviction out of
the module makes the rebuildable-data case fail. `nostalgex-season-smoke.mjs` got an `lsSet`
stand-in; `cache-restore-crash`, `channel-config-quota` and `stream-quality` browser smokes
now read the cache from IndexedDB. All of those, plus `empty-guide`, `empty-lineup`,
`start-over:browser` and `plex-bad-byte`, pass.

**Half-done.** Not verified on a real Docker host, a TV browser, Safari or Firefox: the
checks ran in headless Chromium 156. A browser with no IndexedDB keeps working and rescans
every visit (tested by removing it). If IndexedDB hangs, a visit waits 5 s for the cache
before scanning (tested with a stub). `repopulateChannelsFromLibrary` rewrites the cache on
every load, restored or not, so the 24 hour TTL counts from the last visit; unchanged,
and not looked at further.

**Next.** Needs review and a push decision from Chad. Cross-product: localStorage and IndexedDB
are browser-only, so nothing to port to Apple TV or Roku; the Roku CI job watches
`plex-tuner.html` and the engine files, and none of the shared engine files changed.

## 2026-10-31 (Apple TV and web tuner: Norwegian, Bokmal and Nynorsk are one language)

**Why.** Norwegian has three ISO 639-1 codes, "no" (Norwegian), "nb" (Bokmal) and "nn"
(Nynorsk), and three ISO 639-2 ones, "nor", "nob" and "nno". Servers tag the same track
with any of them, and a TV set to Norwegian reports "nb-NO". Since N-014 compared codes
exactly, a Bokmal viewer never got a track tagged "nor", and the other way round.

**Changed.** On `fix/norwegian-one-language` (off `release/1.0.29-rc`), not pushed.
The ISO 639 table is unchanged (still identical to the Roku app's); the six codes are
folded to "no" when two codes are compared. Every other language keeps the exact compare.
- Apple TV: `SubtitleSelectionLogic.norwegianCodes` and `languageKey` (table reduction,
  then the fold), used by `sameLanguage` and the Jellyfin and Emby audio pick;
  `tagMatchesPreferred` adds the same rule to the prefix compare the player's own tracks
  use (Plex audio and subtitles, foreign-audio subtitles, forced tracks).
- Web tuner: `scripts/nostalgex-language.js` gains `NORWEGIAN` and `languageKey`, and
  `sameLanguage` compares keys, so the page's `langMatches` follows with no change there.
- Tests: `LanguageCodeMatchingTests` covers all 36 Norwegian pairs, regions, the TV locale
  nb_NO, the audio and forced-subtitle picks and the player-track compare, and Danish,
  Swedish, Dutch, Nepali and Icelandic staying apart. The look-alike test skips "nob" for
  "no" (now deliberate). The web smoke has the same cases; run against the old module it
  fails six of them.
- The Roku side is on `roku/norwegian-one-language` (NxLanguageKey), from main.
- NostalgexTests: 1,037 run, 1,022 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped. npm test green
  (language-match 33 passed). Not tried against a real Norwegian-tagged library.

## 2026-10-31 (Apple TV: a package switch flips at once and builds in the background)

**Why.** On a real Apple TV, switching a package on stalled before the switch flipped
and BUILDING showed. Measured on a tvOS 26.1 simulator with the franchise fixture padded
to an 11,863-item library and every package offered: the press itself took 0 ms, but the
build that followed filtered each channel on the main actor, yielding only every third
channel, so the main actor was held 350 to 580 ms at a time for about 3 s (NOSTALGEX:
seven blocks). The switch drew 1.2 to 2.1 s after the press. Three packages switched on
in a row were three builds, one after another (3.0 s, 2.7 s, 0.7 s), each holding the
main actor the same way.

**Changed.** On `settings/bundle-toggle-instant` (off `release/1.0.29-rc`), not pushed.
Same shape as the Roku app's package switch: the switch flips and saves on the press,
BUILDING shows at once, the build runs behind it, and switches made while one waits or
builds become one build.
- `scheduleBundleBuild` waits 0.5 s after the last switch, then builds every package
  waiting. A new switch restarts the wait and drops a build already running, so a run of
  quick switches reaches the guide once: one filter pass, one guide swap, one snapshot.
- `buildPendingBundles` filters off the main actor (as the launch build already did)
  and merges into the lineup as it stands when the build ends, so a collection scan or
  franchise change made meanwhile is kept. A package switched off before its build starts
  is left out of it. Signing out drops a waiting build.
- The guide takes the new lineup when the build lands; nothing changes what is playing.
- After, same library: the switch draws in about 270 ms (the UI test's polling floor),
  the main actor was never held over 65 ms while builds ran, and three quick switches
  were one build (NOSTALGEX, KIDZ ZONE and CASE FILES together, 6.0 s off the main
  actor). Switching off is unchanged (about 270 ms, no build).
- Tests in `BundleBuildTests`: three quick switches commit one build; a package switched
  off while waiting is left out; the press filters nothing and the main actor's longest
  gap during a 30-channel build over 60,000 items is under 150 ms (9 ms measured); four
  real packages from channels.json built together give the same channels and pools as
  the launch's full build. NostalgexTests: 1,028 run, 1,013 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped.

**Half-done.** Not tried on a real Apple TV. The filter cache (one pass over the
library) is still built on the main actor when a build starts: 22 ms for 11,863 items on
the simulator, more on an Apple TV.

Rebased again onto `c4d936f`, which changed the shared channel filter: 16 of the Apple TV's filter cases then failed on Android (STAND-UP, ANIME, CERTIFIED GOLD, THE 60S). `ChannelFilter.kt` now has `manifestOnlyGenreFallback` and the OMDb fallback for `ratingMin`, and `FilterGoldenTest` now reads a case's OMDb values, which it had been dropping, so the OMDb gates are tested for the first time. All 24 engine tests pass.

**Watershed on Android.** Ported from `fb260ec`: Settings has the SCHEDULE section with WATERSHED (off by default, the Apple TV's `nostalgex_watershed` key). While on, every channel without its own `blockRatings` drops R, NC-17 and TV-MA titles (GB-15 and GB-18 through the US mapping) before 9 PM, in `ChannelConfig.timeFilteredPool`, which every schedule, tune and next programme reads. A channel left empty only by that shows the cyan BROADCASTS WILL RESUME AT 9 PM card in the tuner and full screen, and BROADCASTS RESUME AT 9 PM across its guide row. `WatershedGoldenTest` checks `scripts/watershed-golden.json`: 13 of 13 match the Apple TV. On the emulator against Jellyfin, with every test title set to R: the channel held at 08:30 and at 20:59; switching Watershed off put it back on the air at once (0.8 s); with the emulator clock started at 20:59, the 21:00 minute tick brought it on by itself (a transcode, 0.75 s).
