Fixed on the way: the tuner's info panel stayed blank when a channel gained a schedule with nothing else changing, as at 9 PM; it now redraws on the schedule tick. Not run on the SHIELD.

**Library selection on Android.** Ported from `521157b` (I-054). After sign-in, when the servers in use have more than one library, CHOOSE YOUR LIBRARIES lists them all on, with focus on CONTINUE; a library left off is never scanned. Settings has a LIBRARIES list under SERVERS, where the last library on has no switch and changing one reads the library again. The choice is stored under the Apple TV's `nostalgex_deselected_library_sections` key, as `serverId::key`, and resets to every library on at each sign-in, as `presentLibrarySelectionOrScan` does. Both scanners drop excluded libraries from the list before any item request: `MediaBrowserScanTest.anExcludedLibraryIsNeverFetched` checks that no request names the excluded view over the Roku fixture server. On the emulator against Jellyfin (Movies and Shows): the picker showed both; with Shows off the read gave 19 items (the films) in 99 ms; switching Shows back on in Settings gave 25 in 279 ms and an empty stored list. Not tried: Plex (the SHIELD is signed in, and the picker only appears at sign-in, though Settings' LIBRARIES list will show there), Emby, and a single-library server, which should skip the picker.

**Loading screen, START OVER and unfinished loads on Android.** Ported from `LoadingView`, `LibraryLoadPhase`, `LaunchGuard` and `UnfinishedLoadsView` (`b24c570`, `e7f2424`). A full library read now shows the step rail (LINEUP, LIBRARY, CHANNELS, READY: the Apple TV's COLLECTIONS, METADATA and MUSIC have no work behind them here), the first-setup warning on the first full load, the headline with what is being read ("TV SHOWS 3/10", "MOVIES"), the section line, a progress bar for sections and then channels, and START OVER behind the Apple TV's question. A short wait with nothing to report is the logo and a heartbeat. Both scanners report `ScanProgress` (library of how many, items, shows done). `LaunchGuard` uses the Apple TV's keys: a marker set as a foreground load starts and cleared as it ends (reading the saved library clears it without resetting the count; a background refresh is not tracked), and two loads in a row that never finished make the next launch ask LOADING DIDN'T FINISH, TRY AGAIN or START OVER. The reinstall half is not needed on Android (app data goes with the app; backup is off). The Apple TV's STOP WAITING for a scan that goes quiet is not ported: there is no stall watch here yet. Measured on the emulator through a proxy holding each Jellyfin library request for 1.5 s and then 8 s: the rail moved LINEUP to LIBRARY to CHANNELS and read 25 items in 6.7 s; two launches stopped mid-load gave counts 1 and 2 and the third opened on LOADING DIDN'T FINISH; START OVER asked first, KEEP LOADING went back to the load, and confirming signed out with nothing from the cancelled load landing in the 20 s after.

Found and fixed on the way: after typing in a text field (an address, a username, a password), the next screen's first OK press did nothing. Logging the keys showed OK arriving as key code 45, the letter q: Android TV's keyboard stayed attached but unseen after its field went away, and turned OK into the key it had focused; arrows got through, so any arrow press "fixed" it. This was also the SETTINGS press ignored once on 2026-10-29. Fields now close the keyboard whenever they stop editing; the same sequence then delivered key code 23 and CONTINUE took the first press. Also: on Emby, `Lineup` passed "plex" to the channel filter, so Dolby Vision profile 5 titles stayed on channels; it now passes the real backend, with a test.

**On the SHIELD (Plex), `022f073`.** Installed over the earlier build: the sign-in and settings were kept. Launch from the saved library: 11,436 items read in 1,425 ms, 28 channels built in 1,385 ms, first picture (direct play) 1.6 s after that; the load marker was set and cleared. Settings listed the server's five libraries under LIBRARIES, all included. A forced full read (the saved copy removed, nothing else changed) showed the new loading screen against a real server: CONNECTING TO PLEX, then per-library progress up to TV SHOWS 245/291 in section 3 of 5, then BUILDING CHANNELS; 20.4 s to read, 1.5 s to build, then the guide as before. The channel-count progress bar under BUILDING CHANNELS was not caught on screen (the build took 1.5 s between screenshots 3 s apart), so it is unverified on a device. Watershed was left off and no library was switched off on this device. Not tried on the SHIELD: Jellyfin or Emby, START OVER, LOADING DIDN'T FINISH (all tested on the emulator). Library selection was then used on the SHIELD from Settings, three changes in a row, each re-reading the library (19 to 20 s) and keeping 28 channels: a Plex music library is read but adds nothing, on Android or the Apple TV (Plex lists artists, with no running time, and the scan drops entries without one), so switching one off only saves its requests; a small Other Videos library held 39 items and a Sports library 5 episodes with no genres.


## 2026-10-30 (Roku: port the two filter engine changes of 2026-10-29, so the `roku` job goes green)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `roku/filter-port-manifest-fallback-ratingmin`, cut from
`origin/main` at `0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed. Found by the 80s +3 renumber card
(numJBa3V), which guessed the red `filter` tests came from the renumbering; they do not.

**Why.** Two engine commits of 2026-10-29 reached `scripts/nostalgex-channel-filter.cjs`, the
shared filter golden file and the Swift app, and not `roku/source/filter/ChannelFilter.brs`.
`roku/` says an engine change lands with its Roku port; this is the port, late. Until it
lands, `filter` shards 0 to 6 and `filter-golden` fail on main and so does the `roku` CI job.
On the Roku the effect is real: STAND-UP and ANIME miss titles the Apple TV and web tuner
put on them, and a library whose server sends no star rating (Emby's `CommunityRating`) can
leave the 13 channels on a plain `ratingMin` empty when OMDb enrichment is on.

**Changed.**

- `4fa4cb5`, `manifestOnlyGenreFallback`: a `manifestOnly` channel that sets the flag now also
  runs the normal genre and keyword matching, so a title the manifest never claimed can still
  reach it (STAND-UP and, since `6dc02db`, ANIME opt in). The flag is read once per channel in
  `NxFilterChannel`.
- `d56729f`, `ratingMin`: when neither the Plex rating nor the user rating clears the bar, the
  OMDb rating from enrichment (the value `imdbRatingMin` reads) at the same threshold does. With
  no enrichment there is none and the item is rejected as before.
- `tests/FilterGoldenTests.brs` passes `enrichment.imdbRating` through, as upstream's
  `nostalgex-filter-golden-smoke.mjs` did in `d56729f`: the two Emby zero-rating cases need it.

**Measured.** Before, on `0fe27e9`: `filter` 9 channels (58, 60, 90 to 96) failing under both
clocks, `filter-golden` 276 passed, 16 failed. After: every `filter` shard passes and
`filter-golden` is 292 passed, 0 failed. The rest of the run is unchanged. The two renumber
fixes in `roku/renumber-80s-fixtures` clear the other three failures: with both branches
together the whole `tests/run.sh` ends in ALL TESTS PASSED.

**Half-done.** Not run on the stick: the filter vectors take about 55 s a shard off-device and
longer on a Streaming Stick, so `scripts/deploy.sh --test` was left to the next session.
Enrichment is off in the test stick's build, so the `ratingMin` fallback is proved by the
golden cases only.

## 2026-10-30 (Roku: the 80s-channels +3 shift, tests that read live numbers and one real number bug)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `roku/renumber-80s-fixtures`, cut from `origin/main` at
`0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed. Trello numJBa3V.

by 3 (only `number` changed, every `id` stayed). Swift's `SeasonalBundleTests` were fixed in

A full `tests/run.sh` on `0fe27e9` (`NX_TEST_JOBS=2`) says it is only part of it.

**Measured on `0fe27e9`.**

- Caused by the shift: `collections` 2669 passed, 2 failed (`CH 100 STAR WARS` is `CH 103`),
  `franchise-guide` 58 passed, 1 failed (`list: star wars number`, 100 is 103).
- Not the shift: `filter` shards 0 to 6 (18 FAIL lines, channels 58, 60 and 90 to 96, each
  under two clocks) and `filter-golden` (276 passed, 16 failed: stand-up, anime, the 7
  Carl Barron and Arj Barker titles, and the two Emby zero-rating cases). Those are the
  engine commits `4fa4cb5` (`manifestOnlyGenreFallback`) and `d56729f` (`ratingMin` falls
  back to the OMDb rating) that never got their Roku port. `ChannelFilter.brs` has neither.
  The filter vectors and golden cases key on channel id, so no number is involved. Left for
  its own change.

**Changed.**

- `tests/CollectionTests.brs` and `tests/FranchiseGuideTests.brs`: the three stale
  expectations now read the channel's number from the live `channels.json`. The Swift cases
  they transcribe make their own `Channel(id: 100, number: 100)`; here the stock channels are
  built from the real file, so a hard-coded 103 would break at the next renumber too.
- A real on-device bug, `NxFranchiseListRows` in `source/guide/Franchises.brs`. It took a
  stock classic's number from the kept channels and fell back to the channel's id when the
  classic was cut for too few films. Before the shift id and number matched, so nobody saw
  it. Now Settings shows `CH 102` for HARRY POTTER where the channel is CH 105. It reads the
  number from every channel in the lineup, as the Apple TV's `allChannels` does. A new check
  makes every stock row's number its channel's: on the old code 5 of the 7 failed (102 for
  105, 106 for 109, 103 for 106, 104 for 107, 105 for 108).
- Production code has no other channel-number literal. Every `CH n` on screen, the deep-link
  number fallback and the guide read `ch.number` from `channels.json`; the 300, 450 and 500
  blocks for found franchises and collections sit clear of the stock numbers (top one 216).

**Verified.** Off-device, same suites after the change: `collections` 2671 passed, 0 failed;
`franchise-guide` 66 passed, 0 failed; `franchise` unchanged. On the Streaming Stick Plus
(`deploy.sh --test`, one suite per build): `franchise-guide` 66 passed, 0 failed;
`collections` 2671 passed, 0 failed. The stick's own Plex library has all seven classics
in it, so Settings already showed CH 103 to 109 correctly before the fix and still does;
the bug needs a library short of a classic, which is what the new test builds.

**Next.** Port `manifestOnlyGenreFallback` and the `ratingMin` OMDb fallback to
`ChannelFilter.brs`: until then `filter` and `filter-golden` stay red and the `roku` CI job
with them. `scripts/deploy.sh --test` needs GNU `stat -c` and `timeout`, which macOS lacks.

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/livingroom-test-findings`, local, on top of the early-exit
fix below. Not yet confirmed on a real Apple TV.

**Why.** After the early-exit fix, a live retest still took about 48 seconds. Timing logs
from a real device trace showed the second cause: a shared server whose only working path
was relay had its relay candidate succeed in about 0.5s, but relay is the lowest priority,
so the early exit correctly waited for the remote-HTTPS candidate ranked above it. That
candidate never succeeds for this server, yet takes its full patient budget (25s, one
retry, up to 50s) to fail. `discoverServers` waits for every server before deciding whether
to show a picker, so one slow server set the pace for the whole sign-in.

**Changed.** Once any candidate succeeds, whatever still outranks it gets one grace window
instead of its full budget, scheduled as a timer task in the same task group (a time check
inside the loop alone would never fire, since the loop only wakes when a task reports).
The window is sized by what is pending, because lost and no-connection rates are tracked
and this must not trade a slow but real connection for a faster, worse one:

- Anything patient still outranks the hit (remote or relay, which can take 10 to 20s to
  cold-establish and still succeed): 15s.
- Only local candidates outrank the hit (local answers fast or not at all): 3s.

A flat 4s window measured 5 seconds on the same multi-server account; this version trades
some of that back for safety, so the relay-only case should now settle at about 15s.

**Verified.** `ConnectionDiscoveryEarlyExitTests`: 7 tests reproducing the task-group shape
with timed synthetic candidates (fast local hit, second candidate winning, nothing
reachable, earlier-ranked hit inside the grace window, patient vs local-only grace, a
higher-priority hit inside the window still winning), all passing; full `NostalgexTests`
green.

**Half-done.** Temporary `DISCOVERY TIMING` prints are still in `bestReachableURI` for the
one on-device confirmation run. Remove them after that run.

**Next.** One sign-in on a real Apple TV with a multi-server Plex account, console
captured, to confirm which tier wins and the total time. Then drop the prints and merge.

## 2026-10-30 (Apple TV: Plex sign-in waited on a slow relay probe even after a fast local hit)

**Shipped.** Nothing until this lands on main.

**Why.** Chad measured 45 seconds from QR scan to found-the-server over Plex, timed
with a stopwatch. Plex is the primary backend, so this mattered more than the same
delay would on Jellyfin or Emby.

**Found, not guessed.** `PlexAPIService.bestReachableURI` races every connection
candidate for a server (local, remote HTTPS, remote plain, relay, in that priority
order) with `withTaskGroup`, but drained every task before returning, even once the
winner was already decided. Relay candidates get a 25s timeout with one retry (up to
50s), and Plex's `/api/v2/resources` always offers a relay candidate when
`includeRelay=1` is requested, whether or not the account actually needs it. So a
local connection that answered in a second or two still sat blocked behind a relay
probe that was always going to fail or time out, on nearly every sign-in, not only
ones that genuinely needed relay. 45 seconds lines up closely with one relay probe
attempt timing out, plus overhead.

**Changed.** `bestReachableURI` now tracks which candidates have reported (success or
failure) as results stream in, and stops once every candidate ranked ahead of the
current best hit has reported, cancelling whatever is still in flight. A fast local
success now returns immediately instead of waiting on remote and relay. `testReachable`
also bails out on `Task.isCancelled` between its retry attempts rather than retrying a
probe whose result is already moot.

**Verified.** Swift's async `URLSession.data(for:)` already respects structured-concurrency
cancellation, so `group.cancelAll()` genuinely aborts in-flight probes rather than
leaving them to idle out their timeout in the background. `bestReachableURI` itself is
private and does real networking, so it isn't directly unit-testable; added
`ConnectionDiscoveryEarlyExitTests.swift`, which reproduces the exact same TaskGroup
shape with synthetic timed outcomes instead of HTTP calls. The key case (a 50ms local
hit racing a 2000ms doomed relay candidate) completed in 54ms, not ~2000ms, proving the
early exit actually returns fast rather than trusting the logic by reading it. Full
`NostalgexTests` suite green.

**Half-done.** Not independently re-verified against a real Plex account's relay path
(no relay-only test account set up); the timed synthetic test is the closest proof
available without one. Needs Chad's live re-measurement of the QR sign-in time.

## 2026-10-30 (Apple TV: STOP WAITING belongs to the server it was pressed on, #146)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/146-stop-waiting-crash`, local only, not pushed.

**The report.** #146: on Plex with several large libraries, a few stop answering
during the first scan, and pressing STOP WAITING either moves on or crashes the app,
about half the time each. The reporter has to press it once per stuck library, which on
a single server is impossible (one press ends that server's whole scan), so the setup is
most likely several servers.

**No crash log.** App Store Connect had 0 TestFlight crash submissions for the app, and
its diagnostics API holds no crash data (it covers hangs, disk writes and launches only,
and returned nothing for builds 45 to 52). The issue asks the reporter for the build
number, library sizes and a crash log.

**Harness.** New `StopWaitingHarnessTests`: a loopback fake Plex where chosen sections
never answer (connection held open, nothing sent), driven through the real first load
(`AppState.loadLibrary`, the real `PlexAPIService`, the real stall watch and partial-guide
path), pressing STOP WAITING the way the button does at varied moments, then building the
guide the way TunerView does and waiting for the snapshot write. The soak is off by
default (`TEST_RUNNER_NOSTALGEX_STOPWAIT_N`, `_SERVERS`, `_MODE`, `_SEED`, `_OUT`; each
iteration is written to the host file before it runs, so a crash names its iteration).

**Measured.**

- Crash: not reproduced. Before the fix, 50 first loads (20 on one server, 30 on one to
  four servers pressing on every stall), 100 presses acted on: 0 crashes, 0 hangs, every
  load ended in a guide. After the fix, 30 first loads on one to four servers across all
  five press patterns, 81 presses acted on: 0 crashes, 0 hangs, 0 error screens.
- Found instead: a press that lands as one server's scan finishes is never read (the
  stall watch polls every 2s and that server is already done), so it stays set and the
  next server's watch abandons that server, a healthy scan, at its first poll. Measured
  with a deterministic test (server A finishes as the press lands, server B takes 4.4s
  and reports progress throughout): before, B kept 0 of 40 items and the library was
  marked partial; after, 40 of 40, not partial. The soak shows it from the other side:
  in the first after-fix run, a double press on server 1 of 2 no longer reached server
  2, which then sat on its own stuck section waiting for a press of its own, as it
  should. The harness's scripted modes now press again on every later stall.

**Changed.** `AppState.loadLibrary` clears the pending press and the "still waiting" flag
at the start of each server's scan. A press now only stops the server it was made on, and
the STOP WAITING block leaves the screen once the server it was about has answered. START
OVER is unaffected: it also ends the sign-in, which the stall watch checks on its own. Also (review follow-up): signing out between
servers now stops the scan before the next server, which before the fix still received 18
requests with the old token in the 2s until the stall watch noticed; now 0.

**Verified.** NostalgexTests on the tvOS simulator: 984 tests, 969 passed, 0 failed, 15
skipped (the soak among them).

**Not verified.** The crash itself. Things the harness cannot see: memory on a real Apple
TV (a partial guide from several large libraries is still large, and the earlier 400k-item
work showed tvOS ending the app on memory right as the guide appeared; that leaves a
JetsamEvent report, not a crash log), and the real STOP WAITING button and the RootView
switch to the guide.
The fix has not been on a physical Apple TV.

**Next.** The reporter's build number, library sizes and a crash log decide where to look.
With a log: name the frame. Without one: reproduce on the living room Apple TV with
several stuck sections across two servers and watch for a jetsam event.

## 2026-10-30 (Apple TV: a rescan keeps episodes in show order, N-011)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/n011-episode-batch-order`, cut from `origin/main` at
`0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** Jellyfin and Emby fetch a TV section's episodes ten shows at a time and appended
each show's episodes in the order the requests finished. The schedule reads the library
in order (`interleaveByShow` groups shows by first appearance before its seeded shuffle),
so two scans of an unchanged library could build two different guides. Today's guide
survives a rescan (the day's manifest is keyed by the sorted pool), but every later day
was built from whichever order the last scan happened to get.

**Measured.** New `EpisodeBatchOrderHarnessTests` serves one fixed library (40 shows, 3 to
11 episodes each) from a local HTTP server inside the test, holds each show's episode
request back by a delay, and loads it through each backend's real `loadLibrary` twice:
delays in show order, then shuffled. It builds three days of four channels from each load
with the real `DailyManifestScheduler` and counts the minutes that differ. Before the fix:
Jellyfin 16,434 of 17,280 channel-minutes differed (95.1%), Emby 16,458 (95.2%), Plex's
per-show fallback 15,780 (91.3%). Plex's normal path, one paged `type=4` sweep, was already
stable: 0. These are worst-case numbers (every batch fully reordered, episode-only
channels); the field figure on card N-011 was 7 to 9% of channel-minutes. After: 0 on all
four.

**Changed.** Jellyfin, Emby and the Plex per-show fallback keep each batch's results by
the show's place in the list, not by arrival. Requests still run in parallel. The web
tuner already did this (`Promise.all` keeps input order).

**Verified.** NostalgexTests on the tvOS simulator: 982 tests, 968 passed, 0 failed, 14
skipped. Not checked against a real Jellyfin or Emby server.

## 2026-10-30 (Web tuner and Docker: audio and subtitle language codes match exactly, N-014)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/web-n014-iso639-language-match`, cut from `origin/main`
at `0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** `langMatches` in `plex-tuner.html` decided two language tags were the same when one
started with the other, and kept a 50-entry map from a two-letter code to one three-letter
code. Measured with the new smoke against the page from main: all 67 codes whose first two
letters spell another language's code matched that language ("est" as Spanish, "arm" as
Arabic, "jav" as Japanese, "slo" as Slovenian, "rum" as Russian, "swe" as Swahili), and 81 of
the 203 codes in the ISO 639-2 table missed their own viewer ("ces" for Czech, "slk" for
Slovak, "jav" for Javanese, "ben" for Bengali, "baq" for Basque, and more). The effects were
on Jellyfin and Emby only: a Spanish viewer got the Estonian audio track listed first, a
Czech viewer's "ces" track was passed over for the file's default, and an Estonian-only file
did not turn subtitles on. The same compare picks the subtitle track and decides which forced
subtitle is burned in. Plex has no language pick in the web tuner. Same bug, and same fix, as
the Apple TV's `preferredAudioIndex` (branch `fix/n014-iso639-language-match`).

**Changed.** New `scripts/nostalgex-language.js` (`NostalgexLanguage`): one ISO 639-2 to
ISO 639-1 table, both the terminology and bibliographic forms, and `sameLanguage`, which
reduces both tags through it and compares them exactly. The table string is the Roku app's
`NxIso639Table` (issue #119), character for character, the same string the Apple TV carries.
`langMatches` now calls it; the old map and the first-letters compare are gone. Behaviour
matches `SubtitleSelectionLogic.primaryLanguage` on Apple TV: a code the table lacks ("yue")
stays itself and still matches itself, and "und", "mul", "zxx" and "mis" match nothing.
`scripts/nostalgex-jellyfin-subtitles-smoke.mjs` now hands its test pages the module, as the
page's script tag does.

**Verified.** New `npm run test:language-match` (26 checks, in `npm test`). It reads the Roku
`.brs` and fails if the module's table is not that string character for character, if any pair
reduces differently, or if the page grows its own table or a first-letters compare again. It
runs the page's own `langMatches`, `pickAudioStream`, `pickSubtitle` and
`shouldAutoEnableSubs`. Against the tree from main plus the new smoke: 20 failed, 6 passed.
Against main's `plex-tuner.html` with the new module present (so only behaviour can fail):
17 failed, 9 passed. After the fix: 26 passed. Across every table code against every
two-letter language, the only pairs the old compare matched and the new one does not are the
67 look-alikes. `npm test` passes. `build:tuner` and `build:selfhost` both ship the new script
and its tag, and the self-host copy is byte for byte the source. Not checked in a browser
against a real multi-language Jellyfin or Emby file.

**Half-done.** One of the 67 look-alikes is a true match: "nob" (Norwegian Bokmål) starts
with "no", and a viewer who picks Norwegian ("no" in Settings) got it by accident. Exact
compare reads "nob" as "nb", so it no longer matches a "no" setting ("nor" does, and a
browser set to "nb-NO" matches "nob"). The Apple TV and Roku compare the same way, so whether
"no", "nb" and "nn" should count as one language is a decision for all three apps, not the
web tuner alone.

**Next.** Nothing needed on Roku: it already has the table and the exact compare.

## 2026-10-30 (Apple TV: Jellyfin/Emby audio language codes match exactly, N-014)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/n014-iso639-language-match`, cut from `origin/main`
at `0fe27e9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** `JellyfinPlaybackResolver.preferredAudioIndex` compared the first two letters of
a track's three-letter code with the viewer's two-letter language. Measured with the new
tests against the old code: "est" (Estonian) passed as Spanish, "arm" (Armenian) as

**Changed.** `SubtitleSelectionLogic.primaryLanguage` now reduces a tag through one ISO
639-2 to 639-1 table, both the terminology and bibliographic forms, and the audio pick

table on "tgl" (Tagalog). The forced-subtitle burn-in check already went through

track whose language is a full name ("English") no longer matches by its first letters;

## 2026-10-30 (Roku: fix an on-device kbps rounding bug found by tydude001, PR #130)

**Shipped.** `NxMbBitrateKbps` in `roku/source/mediabrowser/MediaBrowserLibrary.brs` now
rounds in LongInteger instead of plain Integer.

**Why.** tydude001 measured on a real TV (43" TCL, Roku OS 16.0.4) that
`(Int(bps) + 500) \ 1000` silently goes through a Float on device: 19269499 rounds to
19270 instead of 19269. The off-device `brs` interpreter (`tests/run.sh`) does not
reproduce this at all, so CI never saw it and the existing test (`MediaBrowserTests.brs`,
"kbps: 19269499 rounds down") already asserted the right answer and already passed
there, both before and after this fix. He measured two candidate fixes on the same TV:
LongInteger math gave the right answer; a Float-based rewrite also looked right at that
one value but gave the wrong answer once the input came through a `for each` over an
array literal, so only the LongInteger form is used here.

**Changed.** `NxMbBitrateKbps`'s rounding line assigns `Int(bps)` into a LongInteger
(`whole&`) before the `+ 500& \ 1000&`, so the whole sum stays in LongInteger. The
`>= 2000000000` overflow guard above it is untouched (different magnitude, not the
reported bug).

**Verified.** `tests/run.sh` (`NX_TEST_JOBS=1`, one process at a time): mediabrowser
cases 5653 passed, 0 failed. Every other failure in the full run is byte-for-byte
identical to the known pre-existing baseline (stale decade/anime channel numbers from
the 80s-channels shift, and Roku parity gaps already tracked separately), confirmed by
diffing this run's FAIL lines against a clean baseline run of the same unmodified main.
Not independently re-verified on a real Roku TV; the fix follows tydude001's own
on-device measurement for the LongInteger approach, not a fresh one.

**Next.** None. Worth a reply on PR #130 pointing at this commit so tydude001 knows it
landed, since his own comment there was never answered.

## 2026-10-30 (Web tuner: a storage-quota exception no longer looks like an unreachable server)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `fix/web-tuner-quota-crash`, cut from `origin/main` at
`c4d936f`, not merged, not pushed.

**Changed.** Fixed issue #152 (reported by tyleerb, web tuner/Docker 1.0.9, a Plex
library of about 6,220 episodes and 519 movies): a large library could show "COULD NOT
LOAD LIBRARY. YOUR SERVER MAY BE UNREACHABLE" even though the server answered fine.
`saveChannelConfig()` ran right after `saveLibraryCache()`, which can land `localStorage`
right at its quota on a library that size. `saveLibraryCache()` already falls back
gracefully on `QuotaExceededError` (strip summaries, then give up quietly); the smaller
`saveChannelConfig()` write next to it had no try/catch of its own, so the exception was
uncaught, propagated out of `fetchPlexLibrary()`, and landed in its generic catch block,
which blames the server for a Plex backend. Wrapped the write in the same try/catch
shape as `saveLibraryCache()`: on failure it logs to the console and moves on, so losing
the channel-config save (toggles don't persist that run) never blocks the rest of the
library load. Left `fetchPlexLibrary()`'s catch block itself alone, since the actual fix
is making sure a storage exception can't escape the save functions in the first place.

New `scripts/channel-config-quota-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:channel-config-quota`,
not wired into `npm test`, same as the other Playwright browser-smoke scripts): loads the
real `plex-tuner.html` headless against a Plex-shaped server, overrides
`localStorage.setItem` to throw `QuotaExceededError` only for the `plex90_channel_config`
key, and checks the library still loads and tunes. A negative control reverts
`saveChannelConfig()` to its pre-fix shape and confirms the same thrown exception then
does reproduce the original symptom: the generic "server unreachable" message, and the
connect screen instead of the guide. 10/10 checks passed, including the negative
control; `npm test` is green.

**Half-done.** Not yet reviewed or pushed; Chad has not seen a go for this branch.
Several other `localStorage.setItem` calls elsewhere in `plex-tuner.html` have no
try/catch of their own either (bundle preferences, collection switches, and a few
smaller settings keys). None of them are the one this report named, and none sit right
after the big library-cache write the way `saveChannelConfig()` does, so they were left
alone rather than widening this fix past what was asked for. Worth a pass later if
another quota-shaped report comes in naming a different save.

**Next.** Needs review and a push decision from Chad. If pushed to `main`, the hosted
tuner picks it up on deploy; a Docker release still needs its own `tuner-v` tag and a
`tunerVersion` bump in that commit.

## 2026-10-30 (Roku: channel pools filtered one server at a time, I-065)

**Shipped.** Nothing yet. Branch `roku/i065-multi-server-oom`, cut from `main` at
`c4d936f`, not merged, not pushed.

**Changed.** `roku/components/LibraryTask.brs`'s `loadLibrary()` combines every
enabled server's items into one array before `buildGuide()` runs one filter pass
over all of it, per channel. With several large servers on at once that scales
peak memory with the sum of every server's library, not the largest one: reported
on a Roku Streaming Stick 4K (Trello I-065), a crash about 30 minutes into channel
generation with several large servers selected, where one server of about 1,000
files worked.

New `NxFilterPoolsByServer` (`roku/source/filter/ChannelFilter.brs`) filters one
server's items against every pool channel, folds the matches into a running
per-channel pool, then deletes that server's items' `nxFilter` (the per-item
filter cache `NxFilterItem` memoizes) before moving to the next server, instead of
leaving every server's cache resident for the rest of the build. `NxFilterPool`
has no state carried between items, so this gives the exact same pools, in the
exact same order, as one pass over everything; `tests/MultiServerFilterTests.brs`
proves it across every real channel in `data/channels.json` against a synthetic
4-server, 100-item fixture (144 checks, 0 failed, off-device).
`buildGuide()`'s own per-channel loop now calls it instead of its old inline
`NxFilterPool(items, ...)` call; `rebuildForBundles` (a package switched on or off
in Settings) goes through `buildGuide()` too, so a package switch over a large
multi-server library gets the same fix with no separate change.

Franchise and collection classification, enrichment and the saved-library write
still read the full combined item list once `loadLibrary()` has built it (they
need every server's items together: a franchise can span servers, and a server's
collections are matched against the whole library by ratingKey). That part is
unchanged; only the channel-pool filter pass, which was the one place doing
`O(channels) * O(every server's items)` work over the combined array, is now
server-incremental. One known, minor trade: when remote enrichment adds new
records mid-build, the second filter pass used to reuse `nxFilter` for items that
didn't change; it now recomputes it for every item (recomputing that per-item
cache is cheap; the actual channel-matching cost was already paid twice either
way, since that second pass always re-filters with no reuse).

Also chunked `NxSavePools`' channel summaries and filtered map into one
`FormatJson` per channel instead of one call over the whole array each time,
matching how the per-item write path was already chunked after the Discussion #8
Streaming Stick Plus OOM crash; triage flagged it as a plausible secondary
contributor on top of the main cause above.

**Half-done.** Not yet run on a real multi-server stick (needs the tester; the
off-device suite and a synthetic fixture are as far as this went). Not yet
reviewed.

**Next.** Reviewer pass, then the tester with two or more real servers enabled on
the stick, watching the `library: ... memory N%` lines through a full build. Then
Chad's go to merge.

## 2026-10-29 (Android TV: a native spike)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `android/spike`, off main `46abf29`, not pushed.

**Why.** To watch on an NVIDIA SHIELD. The web tuner in a TV browser gets no D-pad or Back (2026-10-16 entry), and a browser direct plays only MP4, WebM and MOV, so everything else is transcoded. A native app on Media3 ExoPlayer can direct play MKV and HEVC and pass surround through. The question for this spike is how much more that is on a SHIELD, measured before porting the rest.

**Changed.**
- `android/engine`: the schedule (`DailyManifest.kt`, from `scripts/nostalgex-daily-manifest.js`) and the channel filter (`ChannelFilter.kt`, from `scripts/nostalgex-channel-filter.cjs`) in plain Kotlin with no Android in it, so the tests run on the JVM. Where the JS reads the browser's time zone the port takes a `ZoneId`, and the JS text rules that differ from Kotlin's (`\s`, `.`, `trim`, the ASCII `\b`) are spelled out in `JsText.kt`.
- `ScheduleParityGoldenTest` runs the walk of `scripts/schedule-parity-dump.mjs` field for field against `scripts/schedule-parity-golden.json`: all 3 cases (Plex in New York, Jellyfin in Santiago, Emby in London, with 23 and 25 hour days) match the Apple TV. `FilterGoldenTest` runs all 102 cases of `scripts/filter-golden.json` against the shipped `channels.json` (v43), its exclusive rules and `channels-memberships.json`.
- `Lineup.kt`: library to guide, as `repopulateChannelsFromLibrary`, `applyBundleFilter`, `autoEnableBundlesWithContent`, `rebuildAllSchedules` and `nextAfterEnd` in `plex-tuner.html`. `minItems || 50`, NOSTALGEX on by default, guide ordered by number.
- `android/app`: Plex PIN sign-in with the Apple TV's QR (`plex.tv/link/?pin=`), owned servers first, each on the first address that answers `/identity`; the library scan of `scanOnePlexServer` in library order; a full-screen player with the channel banner, Up and Down for channel, OK for the guide over the picture. Each programme tries direct play for any container Media3 reads and falls back to a Plex HLS transcode (its own session id, stopped on change) on a player error, or when a video or audio track has no decoder, since ExoPlayer otherwise plays a DTS film silent with no error. `adb logcat -s Nostalgex` logs each choice, why a direct play fell back, and time to first frame.
- Channel data comes in through symlinks in `android/app/src/main/assets/`, as `roku/data/`. The fonts are VT323 and DM Mono, as on the Apple TV and Roku (`THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`).
- `ci.yml`: an `android` job runs `:engine:test` and `:app:assembleDebug` when `android/`, the shared data or the two golden files change. `scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh` skips the site deploy for a push that touches only `roku/` or `android/`, checked in a scratch repo (android only: skip; with `index.html`: build).

**Measured.** Planted bugs fail the tests: two in a row becoming three, a changed xorshift constant, and the higher channel keeping a shared title each fail the schedule golden file; ignoring exclusive locks and dropping the kids adult-rating gate each fail the filter golden file. Filtering every channel over a made-up library of 4,200 items took 5,274 ms on the JVM at first, because each of the 139 channels re-read its rules from JSON and re-lowercased every item's title. With channel and item facts worked out once it takes 640 ms, all golden cases unchanged. That is a MacBook, not a TV. On an Android TV emulator (API 31, the SHIELD runs Android 11) the APK installs, launches and gets a real code from plex.tv.

**Found.** `scripts/filter-golden.json` has no case that tells a whole word from a substring: the JS filter with `titleContainsWord` replaced by `includes` still passes all 102 cases. The Android tests pin it directly (`titleRulesMatchWholeWordsOnly`); a golden case would cover the Apple TV and Roku too.

**On a SHIELD (Android 11), against a Plex library of 11,435 items.** Every programme flipped to direct played, none transcoded: MP4 with H.264 and AAC, MKV with H.264 or HEVC, MKV with HEVC and AC3, AVI with MPEG-4 and MP3. First frame 0.6 to 2.2 s after the tune (3.1 s for the first stream after a launch), each at the clock's offset into the programme. The browser would have transcoded all but the MP4.

**Then, on the SHIELD's numbers.**
- Reading the library took 46 to 53 s on every launch, and filtering all 139 channels 10.9 to 11.2 s. The guide only shows the packages that are on, so `Lineup.build` now filters those packages' channels first, on every core (`parallelStream`), and every channel only when they fill nothing, as the web tuner builds every channel only on a first load (`staticChannelIDsForPoolBuild`). 3.2 s for the 19 channels shown, from 10.9 s. On the JVM at 11,400 items: 178 ms against 1,265 ms for all of them. On the JVM the 19-channel build is about 100 ms warm, so most of the SHIELD's 2.5 s is the debug build on a cold runtime. The app now parses `channels.json` and the 1.3 MB `channels-memberships.json` once per launch, alongside the saved-library read rather than after it (390 ms on the API 31 emulator), and logs the split of config, item facts and filtering. A release build type, signed with the local debug key so it sideloads over the debug one, is not debuggable. On the SHIELD it read the saved library in 860 ms (from 2.0 s), parsed the config in 297 ms alongside it, built the 19 channels in 1,836 ms (per-item facts 1,390, filtering 446) and read Plex again behind the picture in 18.3 s (from 49 s). Per-item facts then went onto every core, each distinct content rating is mapped once, and the exclusive locks reuse the item's lowercased title; all golden cases unchanged. Measured over two relaunches after the first (which runs before Android has compiled the app): saved library 0.60 to 0.62 s, 19 channels in 0.96 to 1.03 s (facts 353 to 371 ms, filtering 604 to 660 ms), first frame about 3 s after launch, from about 67 s this morning.
- The first build of that crashed on the SHIELD: `Stream.toList()` is Java 16, Android 11 lacks it, and `engine` compiled against JDK 21 never said so. Lint's API check skips a plain Kotlin module (it has no minSdk), so `engine` now compiles against the JDK 8 API (`-Xjdk-release=1.8`): the same call planted again fails to compile. The app's lint makes NewApi fatal, and the CI job runs `:app:lintRelease`. Lint, while it briefly covered `engine`, also found literal byte-order mark and line separator characters in `JsText.kt` where `\u` escapes were meant; they are escapes now. R8 shrinking stays off until its kotlinx.serialization rules are checked on a device.
- `LibraryStore`: the library as last read, one file in the app's storage, written to a temporary file and renamed, used only for the same servers and format. A launch builds the guide from it and reads the servers again behind the picture (the guide header says UPDATING LIBRARY), swapping the lineup in only if the library changed, which is the Roku port's start-up. Measured: saved library read in 2.0 s, guide built in 2.5 s, picture 5.7 s after launch, against about 67 s before; the refresh read 11,435 items in 49 s and found them unchanged. `LineupTest.aSavedLibraryBuildsTheSameGuide` holds the round trip to the same pools and schedules.
- The remote follows the Apple TV's full screen (`PlayerView.swift`): Left and Right change channel, wrapping; Up opens the guide; Down shows the banner, where the Apple TV opens Now Playing. The first build had Up and Down changing channel, wrongly described as the Apple TV's. The guide opens on the key's release: opened on the press, the release reached the focused row as a click and closed it again at once.

The app opens on TunerView as the Apple TV does, built from `TunerView.swift`, `InfoPanelView.swift` and `ChannelGuideView.swift` at their 1920 x 1080 measurements (one Apple TV point scaled to the screen): the info panel for the focused channel, the picture in a 4:3 box at 51.43% of the height, and the timeline grid with `ProgramRowLayout`'s segments, the two-hour window, Left and Right by the half hour up to 44 slots, the cyan now line, the bolt and the channel-coloured focus. **Then, full screen's overlays** (`PlayerView.swift`, `NowPlayingPanel.swift`). Up opens the mini channel strip: a card per channel along the bottom with what is on, focus on the channel playing, OK tunes it and flashes the OSD. Down opens Now Playing: the poster (Plex's `/photo/:/transcode` at 300 wide, so items now carry `thumb` and the saved library's format went to 3), channel, title and year, rating and UP NEXT, then CAPTIONS (CC, subtitles in full screen only, off by default, as `subtitlesInFullscreenEnabled`), AUDIO (the file's tracks, a choice for that programme only), PICTURE (RETRO MODE, which for now switches the 4:3 crop to the whole picture; the CRT overlay is not ported) and SLEEP TIMER (OFF, 15 MIN, 30 MIN, 1 HR with a countdown, then STILL WATCHING? for 20 s, then playback stops and the tuner returns). **Then, the rest of Now Playing, and RETRO MODE's look.**
- `engine/StreamQuality.kt`: the five levels, held to `scripts/stream-quality-golden.json` by `StreamQualityGoldenTest`, with `isLikelyLocalServer` (private, loopback and link-local addresses, plain or as a plex.direct name). The transcode request carries `location`, `maxVideoBitrate`, `videoQuality`, `videoResolution` and `autoAdjustQuality=0`; away from home a file over the level's direct-play ceiling (20 Mbps on Auto, none on Maximum) is transcoded, so items carry `bitrate` and the saved library's format went to 4. The app side follows the Apple TV's `SettingsView` and `SignInFlow`: a picker (CONNECT TO PLEX, then JELLYFIN), LAN discovery on UDP 7359, a typed address that tries `:8096` first, Quick Connect first when the server has it on, otherwise user tiles or a name and password, with the Apple TV's wording for each failure. The password sign-in was rerun afterwards and passed: the full username went in, Next moved to the password, a wrong one showed "Incorrect username or password." with focus back on the password, and the right one signed in and played. That run read the library in 6,125 ms against a freshly restarted container, not the 676 ms measured warm. Emby followed: the picker offers EMBY, and stopping an encode on Emby also posts `/Sessions/Playing/Stopped`, as `EmbyAPIService.stopTranscode` does; everything else is the shared path. Measured on the emulator against Emby Server 4.10.2.0 in Docker with the same 25 files: discovery answered to "who is EmbyServer?"; the check read Emby (no ProductName, no Quick Connect) and its two public users, shown as WHO'S WATCHING? tiles; the user with a password moved focus to PASSWORD FOR NOSTALGEX and signed in, the one without signed in on the press; library read in 59 to 114 ms; direct play in 1.3 to 1.4 s. The app's hand-built HLS request, sent by curl, answered 200 for master, variant and segments, with `PlaySessionId` on every segment URL and H.264 and AAC in TS; segment 30 came back in 0.42 s; the stop and the stopped report both answered 204. Fixed: a label too long for its button (SOMEONE ELSE in a tile) was cut off, and now shrinks to as little as 60%, as the Apple TV's `minimumScaleFactor(0.6)`. Unverified: an Emby transcode inside the app (none came up in the schedule during the run; the request itself is checked above), the encode stop as seen by the Jellyfin server, and anything on the SHIELD, which stays signed in to Plex. ## 2026-10-29 (ratingMin falls back to OMDb when Emby's CommunityRating is null)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/emby-rating-fallback`, cut from `main` at
`56ee192`, not merged, not pushed.

**Changed.** A real check against Chad's own Emby server (500 real movies
sampled) found `CommunityRating` null or zero for 100% of titles. Thirteen
channels gate purely on a plain `ratingMin` rule that reads that field
(via `item.rating`, `EmbyAPIService.swift` and `JellyfinAPIService.swift`
both map `CommunityRating ?? 0`): LOL, BLOCKBUSTER, ALL TIME GREATS,
CERTIFIED GOLD, RUSH, HOLIDAZE, and all seven decade channels (THE 60S
through THE 20S). On Emby every one of those channels was quietly empty,
not because of a code bug, but because the server genuinely has nothing in
that field.

The fix reuses the existing OMDb enrichment path rather than inventing a
second one: when neither `item.rating` nor `item.userRating` clears
`ratingMin`, the gate now falls back to the same OMDb-enriched rating the
`imdbRatingMin` gate already reads, at the same numeric threshold, before
rejecting. Chose this shape (fallback behaviour on `ratingMin` itself) over
giving all 13 channels a second `imdbRatingMin` field, because the
`ratingMin` values already sit on IMDb's 0-10 scale and the enrichment data
was already flowing through the exact same cache `imdbRatingMin` reads; a
second field per channel would have duplicated the threshold for no
behavioural difference. `scripts/nostalgex-channel-filter.cjs` and
`AppState+Channels.swift` both changed, in the same spot the OMDb gates
already live.

OMDb enrichment is tvOS-only (written to the shared cache the web reads,
per the file's own comment). On web, Docker and Roku, with no enrichment
record, the fallback has nothing to read and falls straight through to the
native-only check: unchanged from before the fix. A content rating of
exactly 0.0 is still indistinguishable from a missing one on any backend;
that ambiguity predates this change and is not solved by it.

Verified with golden cases (`scripts/filter-golden.json`, read by both
`FilterGoldenTests.swift` and `nostalgex-filter-golden-smoke.mjs`, which
needed `enrichment.imdbRating` added to both harnesses since neither
previously passed OMDb fields through the golden fixture at all): one
decade channel (THE 60S, id 90) and one non-decade channel (CERTIFIED
GOLD, id 68), each checked for (1) a real native rating above the bar
still passing with no enrichment at all, no regression; (2) a real native
rating below the bar with no enrichment still rejected, no regression; (3)
a missing native rating (0, as on Emby) with a qualifying OMDb rating now
reaching the channel, which is the fix; (4) a missing native rating with a
non-qualifying OMDb rating still rejected; (5) a missing native rating with
no enrichment at all (web/Docker/Roku today) still rejected, unchanged.
`npm test`: 139 filter-golden cases passed (up from 131). Xcode build and
build-for-testing both green on the tvOS simulator destination; the actual
`NostalgexTests` run was not done (needs the orchestrator's go to use the
simulator).

**Next.** Needs Chad's go to merge. Once merged, the 13 channels should
stop coming back empty on Chad's and other Emby libraries without anyone
touching channels.json. Roku is untouched (out of scope this pass; the
official Roku app does not yet carry OMDb-based gates at all).

## 2026-10-29 (SLIME TV: matching who made a show let two adult NBC shows through)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/slime-tv-adult-leak`, cut from `main` at
`ee2f5d9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Changed.** SLIME TV (channel 26) matched on a broad `studios` rule: a
plain substring test checked against Plex's studio field, TMDB production
companies and TMDB networks all at once. Its list carried the Nickelodeon
names plus bare "Paramount", "Paramount+" and "Paramount Television", meant
to catch Paramount+-era Nickelodeon credits. Those same strings match any
show Paramount's TV arm ever made. Measured on live TMDB: Frasier's
production company is literally "Paramount Television" (Comedy, Family,
TV-PG, inside the channel's own rating list), and Dark Skies carries the
same "Paramount Television" production credit, which is how both NBC shows
reached the channel.

A first pass at a fix added a genre gate requiring Animation or Kids
alongside the studio list. That would have correctly kept Frasier and Dark
Skies out, but it would also have kept out live-action Nickelodeon shows
with no cartoon tag, like iCarly and Drake & Josh, which is the actual
point of a Nickelodeon-themed channel, not just its cartoons. Replaced
rather than kept: switched SLIME TV from `studios` to the engine's existing
`networks` rule, which matches only against TMDB's networks field, where a
show actually aired, not who made it. Dropped the Paramount studio variants
entirely: once the rule keys on where a show aired, Nickelodeon itself is
the network, and the Paramount corporate-parent names are not needed.
Dropped "Nickelodeon Animation Studio" and "Nickelodeon Productions" too,
since those are production-company names, not TMDB network names. No engine
change in any of the three ports: `networks` is already a rule type the
filter understands and uses elsewhere (9 other rule blocks in
`channels.json`).

Checked on live TMDB:

- Frasier: production company "Paramount Television" (the old leak),
  network NBC only. Excluded.
- Dark Skies: production company "Paramount Television" (the same leak),
  network NBC only. Excluded.
- Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012): networks Nickelodeon, Nicktoons.
  Still included.
- Rugrats (1991): network Nickelodeon. Still included.
- iCarly: network Nickelodeon, live-action, no Animation or Kids genre tag.
  Included, where the genre-gated version would have wrongly excluded it.
- Drake & Josh: network Nickelodeon, live-action, same shape as iCarly.
  Included.

`channels.json` stays at v44 (this replaces the earlier commit on this
branch that also moved it from v43 to v44, rather than stacking another
bump on top). `CHANNELS.md`, `public/sitemap.xml` and
`scripts/bundle-lastmod.json` regenerated. `scripts/filter-golden.json`: the
4 genre-era cases are replaced with 6 cases built from the TMDB lookups
above (Frasier and Dark Skies excluded, TMNT 2012 and Rugrats 1991 still
included, iCarly and Drake & Josh newly included), each carrying the real
`enrichment.networks` TMDB returned.

`npm test`: all green (filter golden 108 cases, full suite clean). Also ran
the Roku off-device `brs` interpreter directly against the filter golden
suite (`roku/tests/run.sh`, not part of `npm test`): all passed, confirming
the Roku port's existing network-matching code needs no change for this
data-only fix.

**Next.** Needs Chad's go to push the branch and open a PR. Open product

## 2026-10-29 (ANIME: the same second claim path, with its own guard, branch only)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/standup-missing-specials`, on top of the
STAND-UP commits (not a new branch; a direct follow-up Chad asked for in the
same session), not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** ANIME (channel id 60, CH 59) was `manifestOnly: true`, same shape as
STAND-UP before its fix: a title reached it only if its TMDB ID was already
in `channels-memberships.json`. The STAND-UP commit flagged ANIME as a real
candidate for `manifestOnlyGenreFallback`, but said flipping it on as-is
would let every TMDB "Animation" title through (Disney, Pixar, kids
cartoons), since ANIME had `genres.include: ["Animation"]` and a keyword
list but no `keywordGatedGenres`.

**Adding `keywordGatedGenres: ["Animation"]` alone was not enough.** Checked
against live TMDB data (API key already in `.env`), not guessed:
`keywordGatedGenres` only applies when nothing else matched first. A keyword
hit (`matchesKeyword` in the content-matching block) bypasses it entirely,
and two of ANIME's own keywords were too generic to be a safe keyword
signal once this fallback could actually run:

- **"dark fantasy" and "supernatural"** are TMDB keywords on real anime
  (Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer, Attack on Titan all carry them), but also
  on Western, non-anime content that already carries the "Animation" genre
  tag `keywordGatedGenres` was meant to gate. Coraline (TMDB id 14836) is
  tagged Animation/Family/Fantasy/Horror with the "dark fantasy" keyword and
  would have reached ANIME regardless of the new gate, since the keyword hit
  short-circuits past it. Dropped both from ANIME's keyword list; every real
  anime title checked (Jujutsu Kaisen, Demon Slayer, Attack on Titan, Akira,
  Ghost in the Shell, Paprika, Jin-Roh, Vampire Hunter D, Mob Psycho 100,
  Devilman Crybaby, Rurouni Kenshin) also carries the literal "anime"
  keyword, so nothing real is lost.
- **`keywordsRequireAnyGenre`** was `["Animation", "Action & Adventure",
  "Sci-Fi & Fantasy"]`, broader than `genres.include`. Every real anime
  show checked also carries the "Animation" genre tag on TMDB, so the extra
  two never widened the real catch, but they did open a hole: a live-action
  show tagged Sci-Fi & Fantasy with no Animation genre at all (Supernatural,
  TMDB tv id 1622) or Action & Adventure (Alice in Borderland, TMDB tv id
  110316, carries the real "based on manga" keyword ANIME still uses) would
  have cleared the keyword path on genre alone, Animation tag or not.
  Narrowed to `["Animation", "Anime"]`, matching `genres.include`.

**Changed (channels.json only; the engine already supports both flags from
the STAND-UP commit, no Swift/JS changes needed here).**

- ANIME's `genres.include` gained the narrow server tag "Anime" (the same
  tag the shipped `exclusiveRules` entry already locks to channels 32/60),
  mirroring STAND-UP's narrow-tag pattern: specific enough to reach the

- `keywords`: dropped "dark fantasy" and "supernatural"; kept "anime",

- `keywordsRequireAnyGenre`: narrowed from `["Animation", "Action &
  Adventure", "Sci-Fi & Fantasy"]` to `["Animation", "Anime"]`.
- Added `keywordGatedGenres: ["Animation"]` and `manifestOnlyGenreFallback:
  true`.
- `channels.json` v44 to v45. `CHANNELS.md`, `scripts/bundle-lastmod.json`

## 2026-10-29 (STAND-UP: a second claim path, not just a manifest, branch only)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/standup-missing-specials`, cut from `main`
at `ee2f5d9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** STAND-UP (channel id 58, CH 64) was `manifestOnly: true`: it only
took a title whose TMDB ID was already listed in `channels-memberships.json`,
built once by `scripts/channel-keyword-tuner/discover-standup.mjs` from
TMDB's "stand-up comedy" keyword. A title missing that keyword, or added to
TMDB after that one run, never reached the channel, with no fallback. Seven
specials (Carl Barron and Arj Barker) were reported missing; checked live
against TMDB on 2026-10-29, none of the seven carry the "stand-up comedy"
keyword, and all carry only a bare "Comedy" genre (one also "Documentary").
Rerunning the discovery script (below) does not pick them up, since TMDB's
own signal for them is too coarse, the fix has to accept a narrower signal
than TMDB gives these titles.

**Changed (Swift + JS, channels.json, the shared golden file, not merged).**

- `manifestOnly` channels can now opt in to a second, additive claim path
  with a new flag, `manifestOnlyGenreFallback: true`. When set, the normal
  genre/keyword content-matching block also runs, same as any other channel
  (`AppState+Channels.swift`, `scripts/nostalgex-channel-filter.cjs`). The
  flag is a per-channel opt-in, not an automatic inference from the rules,
  it does not itself guard against a catch-all, the channel's own
  genres/keywords/`keywordGatedGenres` do, so each manifestOnly channel gets
  reviewed before it's set.
- STAND-UP opts in. `genres.include` gained "Stand-Up"; `keywordGatedGenres`
  gates only "Comedy" and "Documentary" (the broad, generic tags also used by
  ordinary comedy films and documentaries), not "Stand-Up". Two mechanisms
  this relies on, already in the engine before this change: `keywordGatedGenres`
  matches a genre EXACTLY, while `genres.include` matches by substring, so a
  compound server tag like "Stand-up Comedy" or "Comedy Special" already
  satisfies the "Comedy" include rule but is a different string from the
  gated "Comedy" itself, and reaches the channel ungated. A narrow genre tag
  (any of "Stand-Up", "Stand-up Comedy" or "Comedy Special", as the server
  itself tags it) or the TMDB "stand-up comedy"/"comedian" keyword now reach
  STAND-UP without a manifest claim; a bare "Comedy" or "Documentary" genre
  alone, with neither signal, still does not, verified with a real comedy
  film (Anchorman, TMDB id 8699, Comedy only, no stand-up keyword) that stays
  off the channel.
- Reran `discover-standup.mjs` against live TMDB: manifest version 1 to 2,
  240 titles added, 5 relocked, 1,468 already locked (1,713 total). This is
  independent of the genre fallback above and keeps working the same way.
- `channels.json` v43 to v44. `CHANNELS.md`, `scripts/bundle-lastmod.json`
  regenerated to match (`npm run channels:doc`, `npm test`'s bundle render).
- `scripts/filter-golden.json`: 14 new cases (102 to 116) covering the three
  narrow genre tags, the keyword-gated bare genre both ways, the Anchorman
  guard, a bare Documentary guard, each of the 7 named titles reaching the
  channel under an assumed "Stand-Up" server tag (their real TMDB ids, with a

**Checked, not changed: the other 4 `manifestOnly` channels.** Per the Trello
card's own ask (F9euJWiF). None get `manifestOnlyGenreFallback` in this
branch.

  rule concept (a collection or distributor check). Separate investigation.

## 2026-10-29 (library selection, Apple TV reference implementation, branch only)

large library saw the Apple TV app crash after about 10 minutes of loading
(a smaller set of libraries was the workaround they found by hand); a Plex
user with several large libraries couldn't get through first setup at all.
Both are cheaper to avoid than to make faster: let the viewer leave a
library out before the first scan ever touches it, instead of scanning
everything and hoping. Spec: `projects/nostalgex-internal/docs/LIBRARY-SELECTION.md`.

**Done, on the branch.**

- `Services/MediaBackend.swift`: `loadLibrary` takes a new
  `excludedSectionKeys: Set<String>` parameter. A key in that set is dropped
  from the section list before a single item request goes out for it, not
  fetched and then discarded. Two convenience overloads (`loadLibrary()` and
  `loadLibrary(progress:)`) keep every existing call site compiling with
  "every section included" as the default.
- `Services/PlexAPIService.swift`, `Services/JellyfinAPIService.swift`,
  `Services/EmbyAPIService.swift`: each `loadLibrary` filters its section
  list against `excludedSectionKeys` right after reading it, before the
  per-section fetch loop starts.
- `Services/LibrarySelectionStore.swift` (new): `LibrarySectionRef` (a
  section's identity, scoped by server id so two Plex servers both numbering
  their first section "1" don't collide) and `LibrarySectionSelectionStore`,
  plain `UserDefaults` persistence for which sections are turned off.
  Default is every section ON (absent = on): this is opting a library OUT,
  not opting one in, so nobody lands on an empty guide by not noticing a
  screen or because a new library showed up later.
- `App/AppState.swift`: new state, `needsLibrarySelection`,
  `pendingLibrarySections` (what the onboarding screen shows),
  `availableLibrarySections` (what Settings shows), and
  `deselectedLibrarySectionKeys`.
- `App/AppState+Auth.swift`: `presentLibrarySelectionOrScan()` is the new
  step between server selection and the first scan, reads every section
  across the chosen servers, shows the picker when there's more than one,
  otherwise scans immediately (existing single-library accounts see no new
  screen). `confirmLibrarySelection(includedIDs:)` commits the onboarding
  choice. All four sign-in completion points (Plex single-server, Plex
  multi-server picker confirm, Jellyfin, Emby) now call this instead of
  jumping straight to `loadLibrary()`. Settings side:
  `refreshAvailableLibrarySections()`, `toggleLibrarySection(_:)` (mirrors
  `toggleServer`: won't turn off the last enabled section, clears the saved
  snapshot synchronously, then reloads), and `excludedSectionKeys(forServerID:)`,
  which turns the persisted choice into the raw keys a backend's

- `App/AppState+Library.swift`: the real scan call site now computes
  `excludedSectionKeys(forServerID:)` per server and passes it into
  `scanAPI.loadLibrary`, before the stall-watch wraps it. Computed outside

  `self` is not).

## 2026-10-29 (Apple TV: channel overlay stuck on after a stall, branch only)

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `fix/channel-overlay-stuck`, cut from `origin/main`
at `ee2f5d9`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** The channel info overlay could reappear during playback after a brief
stall and then stay on screen for good (Trello gENSCnj1). `PlayerView` read
`appState.player?.timeControlStatus == .playing` live inside the view body to
decide whether to show the overlay. `timeControlStatus` lives on the plain
`AVPlayer`, not on an `@Observable` property, so SwiftUI had no reliable
reason to re-render when it changed on its own. A brief stall flips it away
from `.playing`; if any unrelated render happened to land at that moment, the
overlay showed; once the stall cleared, nothing forced another render, so it
sat there until some other interaction (channel change, Play/Pause, Back)
happened to redraw the view. A tester harness reproduced the mechanism with a
real stall and a control case before this fix was written.

**Changed.**

- `Nostalgex/Nostalgex/App/AppState.swift`: new tracked property
  `isVideoPlaying: Bool`, mirroring `player.timeControlStatus == .playing`.
- `Nostalgex/Nostalgex/App/AppState+Playback.swift`: `installFreshPlayer` now
  subscribes to the fresh `AVPlayer`'s `timeControlStatus` via KVO (same
  pattern as the existing Now Playing heartbeat observer in
  `installStarvationMonitor`) and mirrors it into `isVideoPlaying`, guarded on
  `self.player === fresh` so a stale observer from a retired player can never
  win. Every load path (`loadCurrentItem`, `retryLoad`, `fallbackToTranscode`)
  already calls `cancellables.removeAll()` immediately before
  `installFreshPlayer` runs, so the previous player's subscription is gone
  before the new one is added, no leaked observer, and a channel change
  re-attaches fresh rather than relying on a stale subscription from the old
  `AVPlayer` instance. `expireSleepTimer` and `stopChannelAfterRepeatedFailures`
  now also set `isVideoPlaying = false` explicitly, since both pause the
  player without installing a new one (and the latter already cleared
  `cancellables` first, so nothing else would flip it back).
- `Nostalgex/Nostalgex/App/AppState+Auth.swift`: `disconnect()` resets
  `isVideoPlaying = false` alongside `player = nil`.
- `Nostalgex/Nostalgex/Views/PlayerView.swift`: the channel OSD visibility
  check now reads `appState.isVideoPlaying` instead of
  `appState.player?.timeControlStatus`.
- `installFreshPlayer` changed from `private` to internal visibility so tests
  can drive it directly with a real `AVPlayer`.

**Tests.** New `Nostalgex/NostalgexTests/ChannelOverlayPlaybackStateTests.swift`:
drives a real `AVPlayer` through `installFreshPlayer` and confirms (1) a
`timeControlStatus` change (`play()`/`pause()`) actually updates
`isVideoPlaying`, polling rather than asserting immediately since the KVO
sink is routed through `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)`; and (2) across a
simulated channel change (`cancellables.removeAll()` + a second
`installFreshPlayer` call, matching the real load paths), the retired
player's state changes no longer reach `isVideoPlaying` while the new
player's do.

**Update, same day.** The earlier "ready" claim above was wrong: the device
test suite had never actually been run, only `build-for-testing` had, and
when `NostalgexTests` was actually run on the tvOS Simulator both tests in
this file failed, `isVideoPlaying` never observed becoming `true` after
`play()`. Root-caused before touching anything: the fixture in both tests,
`AVPlayerItem(asset: AVMutableComposition())`, builds an item from an empty
composition with zero tracks and zero duration. A standalone macOS probe
(plain Swift + AVFoundation, outside the test target and the simulator,
driving a real `AVPlayer` with the same empty-composition fixture under
direct KVO) showed this is not a reliable "paused player" at all: across
repeated runs the player either flashed to `.playing` for under 50ms before
settling straight back to `.paused` (nothing to decode, nothing to play), or
never left `.waitingToPlayAtSpecifiedRate` /
`AVPlayerWaitingWithNoItemToPlayReason` within several seconds. Neither
outcome gives a polling assertion a stable playing window to observe,
regardless of whether the KVO bridge in `installFreshPlayer` is correct. The
bridge itself was not at fault.

Fix: added `PlayableTestAsset` to the test file, which writes a tiny real
`.mov` (a handful of solid-colour frames via `AVAssetWriter`, ~64x64, a few
seconds, generated once per test run into a temp file, no network access and
no binary asset added to the repo) and both tests now build their
`AVPlayerItem`s from that file instead of the empty composition. A second
standalone probe confirmed a real `AVPlayer` given that generated file
reaches and holds `.playing` reliably across repeated runs. `NostalgexTests`
builds clean again (`build-for-testing`) with the new fixture.

**Half-done.** The actual `xcodebuild test` run against the tvOS Simulator
with the corrected fixture has not been confirmed green yet. That needs a
go-ahead before it runs again, per the standing rule after today's audio
incident.

**Next.** Get the go to run `NostalgexTests` on the tvOS Simulator with the
corrected fixture. If green, this is ready for the normal review/merge path;
no device hardware check is strictly required since the fix itself is pure
state-propagation (no new playback behavior), but one on the Apple TV would
be a reasonable final check given "schedule and playback are the product."

**Shipped.** Nothing. Branch `roku/plex-password-signin`, cut from `main` at
`072b399`, head `0bc748d`, not merged, not pushed.

**Why.** Roku certification rule 2.2 requires on-device authentication and
prohibits an off-device-only sign-in flow. The Roku app only offered
plex.tv/link (entered on a second device), the same flow Plex's own Roku app
had to drop at version 7.6.0/7.6.1 over this same rule. Jellyfin and Emby
already sign in on-device here; only Plex was missing it. Chad's 2026-10-29
decision corrects the 2026-10-28 one (link code only): keep the link code as
the easy option, add an on-device email and password option alongside it.

**Changed.** Nothing on `main`.

**Done, on the branch.**

- `roku/source/plex/PlexApi.brs`: `NxHttp` takes an optional POST body (the
  two existing POST callers, the pin create and check, keep sending none).
  New `NxPlexSignInWithPassword(login, password)` posts to
  `https://plex.tv/users/sign_in.json` with the same X-Plex-* headers the
  link flow already sends, form-encoded `user[login]` / `user[password]`.
  `NxPlexPasswordAuthResult(code, json)` is the pure parser: "ok" with a
  token and name (read from whichever field the legacy JSON endpoint used,
  nested under `user` or flat, `authToken` or the older `authenticationToken`),
  "invalid" on 401 (a wrong password, or an account that signs in through
  Google or Apple and has no Plex password at all; the Roku can't tell
  those apart), "error" otherwise. A two-factor code goes on the end of the
  password with no separator, Plex's own documented workaround for an app
  with no separate code field; nothing in the code needs to know that.
- `roku/components/PlexSignInTask.{brs,xml}`: a `mode` field, `""` (the link
  code, unchanged) or `"password"` (new, with `email`/`password` fields).
  The tail both modes share (save the token, learn the account, clear
  another account's caches, list or confirm the servers) is now one shared
  sub, `finishSignIn`, extracted from the existing flow rather than
  duplicated. `password` is cleared on the task the instant the request is
  sent; only the token reaches `NxPlexSaveToken`.
- `roku/components/ConnectView.brs`: a USE EMAIL AND PASSWORD button next to
  CONNECT TO PLEX on the picker, leading to a new `plexCreds` screen built
  on the same field/keyboard pattern as the Jellyfin/Emby password screen
  (`addField`, `openKeyboard`, `keyboardDone`). It runs its own
  `PlexSignInTask` (mode "password") rather than going through MainScene's
  plexState/plexCode bridge, since there is no second device and no code to
  show. A standing line on the screen says a Google or Apple sign-in has no
  Plex password and to use CONNECT TO PLEX instead (it has to be standing,
  not triggered only on failure, since a 401 can't tell that case apart
  from a wrong password); the 401 error itself reads "Incorrect email or
  password."
- `roku/components/MainScene.brs`: `onConnectDone` gets a `"plexSignedIn"`
  branch (ConnectView's own task already saved the token and the servers)
  that picks up exactly where the link code's "ready" status does: the
  server picker if the account has more than one, else straight to the
  library.
- `roku/source/mediabrowser/SignInFlow.brs`: five new lines in `NxSignInCopy`
  (swept automatically by the existing em-dash/emoji/"tap" copy test) and a
  default-focus case for the new screen.
- Tests: `roku/tests/SignInFlowTests.brs` adds cases for
  `NxPlexPasswordAuthResult` (success nested under `user`, a flat response,
  the older field name, 401, a network error, a 2xx with no token, and that

## 2026-10-28 (web tuner: a crash on a returning visit no longer freezes the loading screen)

**Shipped.** Nothing until this lands on main. Branch `web/cache-restore-catch`, off main `9ea9e15`.

**Why.** A support report (web tuner, Chrome on macOS 26): worked on first connect, then every return visit "finds the server, loads the library, and then build the channels and gets stuck at 139 of 139." Reproduces on reconnect, refresh, reboot. Reading `fetchPlexLibrary()` found the cause of the freeze itself, though not yet what actually throws: the function has two branches, a fresh server fetch wrapped in `try/catch` that shows an error screen, and a cache-restore branch (used on a returning visit, within the 24 hour cache TTL) with no try/catch of its own. An exception anywhere in that branch (filtering, schedule building, autogenerated channels, render) left `LL.hide()` never called, the loading screen frozen forever, and nothing in the console. Because the saved cache persists, the same crash reproduces identically every time. "139 of 139" is the last channel's name written to the step-rail text before the per-channel loop ends; the freeze does not have to come from that channel's own rules, since nothing after the loop (bundle filtering, the schedule-build pass, autogenerated channels, render) updates that text either.

**Not changed.** The actual trigger. A harness (real `plex-tuner.html`, headless, a Jellyfin-shaped library built to populate all 139 channels including the one from the report, every bundle switched on as the reporter described) completed cleanly in both a first-connect and a cache-restore pass, at normal and 8x library size. Whatever throws depends on a shape only the reporter's real server data produces, not reproduced here.

**Changed.**
- `plex-tuner.html` (`fetchPlexLibrary`): the cache-restore branch now runs inside the same `try` as the fresh-fetch branch, so the same `catch` and the same error screen cover both. The wording was written for a fetch failure; it is generic enough to reuse for a build crash too, and a safety net beats a silent freeze while the real cause is unconfirmed.
- The console log now names which branch failed (`Library fetch error (cache-restore): ...` vs `(fetch): ...`), so the next occurrence says more than "it froze."
- `scripts/cache-restore-crash-browser-smoke.mjs` (`npm run test:cache-restore-crash`, needs Playwright, not in `npm test`): the real page against a Jellyfin-shaped server, connects once to save a cache, then reloads with a flag that makes a post-load step throw only on that second load, the one that takes the cache-restore branch. Checks the error screen shows, with text, the connect screen returns, and the loading screen is hidden rather than left up. Negative control: the same crash served against the branch's pre-fix shape (the cache-restore work outside any try/catch) times out with the loading screen still up and no error shown, proving the test exercises the actual fix.

**Measured.** The regression smoke: 11 checks passed, including the negative control against the reverted (pre-fix) code, which times out as expected instead of passing. `npm test`, both builds, tuner isolation and tuner version all pass unchanged.

**Half-done.** The real trigger is still unknown. Trello card (P1, Bug, Ready): https://trello.com/c/nAsb4O8f.

**Next.** Watch for the console line naming the branch and the error the next time this is reported; that is the fastest path to the actual cause.

## 2026-10-27 (Roku: the loading note after the TV clears the saved library no longer gives a time)

**Shipped.** Nothing until this lands on main. Branch `roku/restart-loading-note`, off main `9ea9e15`. Chad's go (option 1 of the power-loss rescan).

**Why.** Two beta users on Discord report a full rescan every time the stick loses power. Cause: the saved library, guide, pools and enrichment cache live in `cachefs:`, which Roku keeps in RAM and empties on a reboot (Roku's file-system docs; no SD card on a Streaming Stick Plus). The registry survives a reboot but holds 32 KB, so a library can't go there. The sign-in, server kind and server list are in the registry, so a Jellyfin or Emby user comes back to the same server, not Plex. The loading screen already says what happened, but ended "This can take a few minutes", which is wrong for most libraries (Chad's 1,545 films read in 6 to 13 s).

**Changed.**
- `source/util/LoadingNote.brs`: `NxLoadingNote(firstRun, savedBefore)` returns the line under the logo. First-ever setup keeps "First setup can take a few minutes to scan and build channels." A library saved before and now gone (`savedBefore`, from the registry's `librarySaved`) says "The TV cleared the saved library, so it's being read again." with no time. A library still saved shows nothing.
- `components/LoadingView.brs` and `.xml`: use it (the headline still names Plex, Jellyfin or Emby, `NxScanHeadline`).
- `tests/MediaBrowserTests.brs`: the four states, no "minute" in the cleared note, a length that fits the line, and that `LoadingView` calls the function and holds no copy of the old text.

**Not changed.** The scan, the schedule and playback. No speed work.

**Half-done.** A cold-boot measurement on the stick (time to guide, the screen shown) waits for a restart of the stick.
